findings.title: STEP 0 — PlayerLoop shape: Mirror is NOT a MonoBehaviour, it is injected into the PlayerLoop, so netcode brackets the whole frame
findings.detail: Il2CppMirror.NetworkLoop.RuntimeInitializeOnLoad() calls AddToPlayerLoop(UpdateFunction, Type ownerType, ref UnityEngine.LowLevel.PlayerLoopSystem, Type playerLoopSystemType, AddMode) to splice NetworkLoop.NetworkEarlyUpdate() and NetworkLoop.NetworkLateUpdate() directly into Unity's PlayerLoop. Those fan out to NetworkServer.NetworkEarlyUpdate/NetworkLateUpdate and NetworkClient.NetworkEarlyUpdate/NetworkLateUpdate. Receive/deserialize/Command+RPC invocation therefore happens in EarlyUpdate BEFORE any FixedUpdate or Update runs; send happens at the end of PreLateUpdate, i.e. AFTER every MonoBehaviour LateUpdate and before rendering. Send is rate-limited, not per-frame: NetworkServer.get_sendRate()/get_sendInterval()/get_tickRate() and NetworkClient.get_sendRate()/get_sendInterval() gate NetworkServer.Broadcast() -> BroadcastToConnection(NetworkConnectionToClient) -> SendToObservers(NetworkIdentity, msg, int channelId).
findings.members: Il2CppMirror.NetworkLoop.AddToPlayerLoop, NetworkLoop.RuntimeInitializeOnLoad, NetworkLoop.NetworkEarlyUpdate, NetworkLoop.NetworkLateUpdate, NetworkServer.Broadcast, NetworkServer.BroadcastToConnection, NetworkServer.SendToObservers, NetworkServer.sendRate, NetworkServer.tickRate, NetworkClient.sendInterval
findings.modding: Because sends fire after LateUpdate, a mod that mutates transforms or SyncVars in LateUpdate still makes that frame's packet — but a mod that mutates them in OnPreRender/custom-pass code does not. Do not try to Harmony-patch a 'NetworkManager.Update' — there is none; patch NetworkServer.Broadcast or NetworkClient.NetworkLateUpdate.

findings.title: STEP 1 — FixedUpdate: MasterController.FixedUpdate drives CMF locomotion; CMF does the ground sensing, not Unity's CharacterController
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.MasterController declares Update(), FixedUpdate() and LateUpdate() (all three). Its FixedUpdate feeds Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController.FixedUpdate() -> ControllerUpdate() -> CalculateMovementDirection()/CalculateMovementVelocity()/DetermineControllerState()/HandleMomentum()/HandleJumping(), which in turn drives Il2CppCMF.Mover.CheckForGround() and Mover.SetVelocity(Vector3). Mover is the physics-cost centre: RecalibrateSensor(), RecalculateSensorLayerMask(), RecalculateColliderDimensions(), GetGroundNormal/GetGroundPoint/GetGroundCollider — a raycast/spherecast sensor per character per fixed step. Mover also has its own LateUpdate(). Note AdvancedWalkerController ALSO has an Update() whose only job is HandleJumpKeyInput() (input latching, so a jump press between fixed steps is not lost).
findings.members: MasterController.FixedUpdate, MasterController.Update, MasterController.LateUpdate, CMF.AdvancedWalkerController.FixedUpdate, ControllerUpdate, HandleJumpKeyInput, CMF.Mover.CheckForGround, CMF.Mover.SetVelocity, CMF.Mover.LateUpdate, CMF.Mover.RecalibrateSensor
findings.modding: Movement mods belong in AdvancedWalkerController.CalculateMovementVelocity or MasterController.FixedUpdate, never in Update — writing velocity in Update is overwritten by the next ControllerUpdate. Widening Mover's sensor layer mask multiplies fixed-step raycasts by the number of characters.

findings.title: STEP 2 — FixedUpdate: GameManager.FixedUpdate -> CallFixedBrainUpdate() runs only a SLICE of the bots' physics, round-robin
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.GameManager declares FixedUpdate(), Update() and LateUpdate() and is the game's master pump — there is no AIManager type. GameManager.CallFixedBrainUpdate() walks get_allAI() (List<BrainAI>) using cursor get_AI_FixedUpdateIndex() and slice size get_AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame(), calling BrainAI.CallPhysicsFixedUpdate() on each. BrainAI itself declares Awake/Start but NO Update, FixedUpdate or LateUpdate — it is 100% externally ticked. GameManager.get_FixedDeltaUpdateFPS() (float) suggests the fixed timestep itself is a settings-driven value.
findings.members: GameManager.FixedUpdate, GameManager.CallFixedBrainUpdate, GameManager.allAI, GameManager.AI_FixedUpdateIndex, GameManager.AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame, BrainAI.CallPhysicsFixedUpdate, GameManager.FixedDeltaUpdateFPS
findings.modding: Adding work to a bot's physics path costs AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame × cost per fixed step, not N_bots × cost. Raising AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame is the direct lever if bots feel physically laggy; it is a plain int property.

findings.title: STEP 3 — FixedUpdate: WeaponsAI.FixedUpdate and WeaponsAI.Update run per bot every frame and are NOT amortised — the one hole in the AI scheduler
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponsAI declares its own Start(), Update() AND FixedUpdate(). Unlike BrainAI/EyesAI (which have no Unity lifecycle methods at all and are ticked by GameManager), every bot's weapon component ticks unconditionally twice per frame path. WeaponsAI is where burst timing (_fireTimer, currentBurst, timeBetweenBursts), reload state and the FinalIK arm solvers live. Its only self-defence is IK_RangeCheck(), which disables ikBehaviours (Behaviour[]) and the RootMotion.FinalIK.ArmIK LeftArmIK/RightArmIK beyond maxIKdistance using _sqrDistanceToCamera. Similarly Il2Cpp.AiAnimationController has BOTH Update() and Tick(float dt), and Il2Cpp.AiRotationController has BOTH LateUpdate() and Tick(float dt) plus ClientSideLogic() — the Tick(dt) is the amortised brain-driven path, the Update/LateUpdate is unconditional per-bot presentation work.
findings.members: WeaponsAI.Update, WeaponsAI.FixedUpdate, WeaponsAI.IK_RangeCheck, WeaponsAI.maxIKdistance, WeaponsAI._sqrDistanceToCamera, AiAnimationController.Update, AiAnimationController.Tick, AiRotationController.LateUpdate, AiRotationController.Tick, AiRotationController.ClientSideLogic, BrainAI.CallUpdate, EyesAI.Awake
findings.modding: This is the highest-value perf target in the AI stack for a mod: with 40 bots you pay 40× WeaponsAI.Update + 40× WeaponsAI.FixedUpdate + 40× AiAnimationController.Update + 40× AiRotationController.LateUpdate per frame regardless of GameManager's slicing. Lowering maxIKdistance is a supported, zero-risk win. Do NOT add work inside these four methods.

findings.title: STEP 4 — FixedUpdate: BulletManager.FixedUpdate is the ballistics solver — one batched RaycastCommand job for every bullet in flight
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletManager declares Awake(), FixedUpdate() and LateUpdate(). FixedUpdate is the integrator: for each BulletInstance in List<BulletInstance> _bullets it calls BeginManagedTick(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, ref RaycastCommand command, ref bool needsRay) -> bool to fill NativeArray<RaycastCommand> _commands, schedules with RaycastMinPerJob, then ResolveManagedTick(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, bool chordHit) against NativeArray<RaycastHit> _results; EnsureScratch(int n) grows the arrays. Travel(float, Vector3, bool skipRaycast) is the per-bullet integration with predictionStepsPerFrame sub-steps. BulletManager.LateUpdate() separately drives tracer visuals. This is real per-fixed-step work proportional to rounds in flight, and shotguns fire N independent full-fidelity projectiles rather than a cone.
findings.members: BulletManager.FixedUpdate, BulletManager.LateUpdate, BulletManager._commands, BulletManager._results, BulletManager.RaycastMinPerJob, BulletManager.EnsureScratch, BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick, BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick, BulletInstance.Travel, BulletInstance.predictionStepsPerFrame
findings.modding: You cannot intercept individual bullet raycasts with Physics.Raycast patches — they go through the Jobs batch API. Patch BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick for every hit. A high-RPM weapon mod scales _bullets linearly and raises predictionStepsPerFrame cost with it; that, not the fire event, is the cost.

findings.title: STEP 5 — FixedUpdate: the remaining fixed-step ticks — PlayerNetworking.FixedUpdate, WeaponV3.FixedUpdate, MilkTransformSync.FixedUpdate, WeaponSFX.CallFixedUpdate
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking declares Awake/Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate; Il2Cpp.WeaponV3 declares Awake/Start/Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate/OnDisable — the weapon is one of the very few types that ticks in all three phases. Il2Cpp.MilkTransformSync declares Awake/Update/FixedUpdate and is where owner-authoritative object motion is sampled before being sent (SendPosition/SendRotation/SendPositionAndRotation, each taking NetworkConnectionToClient LAST = Mirror Command). Il2Cpp.WeaponSFX has Update() plus an externally-driven CallFixedUpdate(), so its fixed-step work is scheduled by GameManager rather than by Unity.
findings.members: PlayerNetworking.FixedUpdate, WeaponV3.FixedUpdate, WeaponV3.Update, WeaponV3.LateUpdate, MilkTransformSync.FixedUpdate, MilkTransformSync.Update, MilkTransformSync.SendPositionAndRotation, WeaponSFX.CallFixedUpdate, WeaponSFX.Update
findings.modding: WeaponV3 ticking in all three phases makes it the most expensive single gameplay component on the local player; a weapon mod that adds per-frame work should pick exactly one phase. MilkTransformSync sampling in FixedUpdate means a modded grabbable moved in Update will be sampled a frame late.

findings.title: STEP 6 — Update: input and camera rotation happen in Update, not LateUpdate — CMF.CameraController.Update is the authority on look direction
findings.detail: Il2CppCMF.CameraController declares Awake/Setup/Update and Update runs HandleCameraRotation() -> RotateCamera(float newHorizontalInput, float newVerticalInput) -> UpdateRotation(), reading Il2CppCMF.CameraMouseInput.GetHorizontalCameraInput()/GetVerticalCameraInput(); movement input comes from Il2CppCMF.CharacterKeyboardInput.GetHorizontalMovementInput()/GetVerticalMovementInput()/IsJumpKeyPressed(). External overrides exist as first-class API: ExternalSetRotation(float X, float Y), ExternalAddRotation(float X, float Y), ExternalSetRotationDelayed(float,float,float) (coroutine), StartFollowRotation(Transform target, float speed, float blendIn)/StopFollowRotation(), RotateTowardPosition/RotateTowardDirection, SetFOV(float), plus readers GetFacingDirection/GetAimingDirection/GetStrafeDirection.

findings.modding: Recoil/aim-assist/cinematic mods should call ExternalAddRotation rather than writing the transform — the transform is recomputed from the controller's internal angles every Update. Because rotation resolves in Update, everything in the LateUpdate follower stack (STEP 15) reads an already-final camera angle.

findings.title: STEP 7 — Update: MasterController.Update and PlayerNetworking.Update — stance, lean, stamina, weight and the interaction raycast
findings.detail: MasterController.Update() covers the physiology layer: CalculateTotalWeight(), GetWeightSpeedMultiplier(), GetWeightFallDamageMultiplier(), UpdateSprintStamina(), UpdateSprintBreathingSFX(), the transitionProne(bool isCrouch) coroutine, and the seat blend (_seatBlendTimer/StartSeatPositionBlend). Stance/lean cross the wire from here via CMD_UpdateValues(float playerStanceOutput, float playerLeanOutput) -> RPC_UpdateValues, and velocity via CMD_UpdateSavedVelocity(Vector3). PlayerNetworking.Update() owns interaction discovery (raycast first, proximity fallback). That raycast is throttled by Il2Cpp.RaycastingOptimisation, which declares only Start() — no Update — and exposes playerNetworking, RaycastPosition (Transform), detectionMask (LayerMask), updateIntervals and updateTimer, i.e. it is a passive config/timer object read by PlayerNetworking's own loop.
findings.members: MasterController.Update, CalculateTotalWeight, UpdateSprintStamina, UpdateSprintBreathingSFX, CMD_UpdateValues, CMD_UpdateSavedVelocity, PlayerNetworking.Update, RaycastingOptimisation.Start, RaycastingOptimisation.updateIntervals, RaycastingOptimisation.detectionMask
findings.modding: RaycastingOptimisation.updateIntervals is the single float that trades interaction-prompt responsiveness for raycast cost. It has no Update of its own, so patching it does nothing — patch PlayerNetworking.Update or just write the field.

findings.title: STEP 8 — Update: GameManager.Update is a mega-pump running at least NINE independent round-robin schedulers over global registries
findings.detail: GameManager holds a global registry plus a cursor/slice pair for nearly every expensive subsystem, and amortises each across frames. Confirmed cursor/budget pairs: AI logic — AI_UpdateIndex / AI_MinPerFrame / AI_MaxPerFrame / AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks over allAI (List<BrainAI>); AI physics — AI_FixedUpdateIndex / AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame; bot health — Health_BotLastUpdateIndex / Health_BotNumPerFrame over allBotHealth (List<Health>), with allHealth separate; weapon collision — WC_LastUpdateIndex / WC_NumPerFrame and WC_AnimLastUpdateIndex / WC_AnimNumPerFrame over allWeaponCollisions/allOwnedWeaponCollisions; bot aim correction — AIweaponCollisionUpdatePerFrame / _lastAIweaponCollisionUpdated over allAIAimCorrection (List<BotAimCorrection>); V1 audio occlusion — NumOccludersUpdatePerFrame / _lastUpdatedOccluder over audioOccluders (List<AudioOcclusion>); weapon-SFX occlusion — weapSFX_numOccluders / _lastUpdatedWeapSfxOccluder over weaponSFX (List<WeaponSFX>); weapon mods/flashlights — NumModsToUpdatePerFrame / _lastModUpdated over activeWeaponMods (List<WeaponMod>); dynamic lights — NumDynamicLightToUpdatePerFrame / _lastDynamicLightUpdated over DynamicLights (List<DynamicLight>) plus onDemandShadowMapUpdaters (List<OnDemandShadowMapUpdate>). Plus ring buffers bulletShells/shellWriteIndex and bulletHoleDecals, and per-frame housekeeping ManageAtakMarkers(), ManageDOFS(), SetFPSCounter(), updateRadioIcon().
findings.members: GameManager.Update, GameManager.LateUpdate, AI_UpdateIndex, AI_MinPerFrame, AI_MaxPerFrame, AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks, Health_BotNumPerFrame, WC_NumPerFrame, WC_AnimNumPerFrame, AIweaponCollisionUpdatePerFrame, NumOccludersUpdatePerFrame, weapSFX_numOccluders, NumModsToUpdatePerFrame, NumDynamicLightToUpdatePerFrame, shellWriteIndex, ManageDOFS, ManageAtakMarkers
findings.modding: Every one of these NumXPerFrame ints is a plain settable property and together they are the game's real quality/perf dial — far more impactful than any graphics setting. Conversely: a mod that registers many objects into any of these lists does not increase per-frame cost, it increases LATENCY (each object is visited less often). That is the failure mode to expect, not stutter.

findings.title: STEP 9 — Update: the 'CallX' convention — a dozen components have had their Unity lifecycle methods deliberately removed
findings.detail: The externally-ticked set, all confirmed by signature: Health.CallUpdate() (Health declares Awake/Start/OnEnable/OnDisable but NO Update/FixedUpdate; it also carries CullDistance, beingForceCulled and cullBehaviour (Behaviour[]) so it is distance-culled as well as sliced); WeaponCollision.CallUpdate() and CallUpdateAnimation() (two separate cursors, hence the split); WeaponMod.CallLateUpdate(); DynamicLight.CallUpdate(); OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.CallUpdate() and UpdateShadowMap(); BotAimCorrection.CallLateUpdate(); WeaponSFX.CallFixedUpdate(); FootstepAudioController.CallUpdate(); BrainAI.CallUpdate(float minSqrDistToPlayer)/CallBrainUpdate()/CallPhysicsFixedUpdate(); LightOptimize.UpdateLight(). Naming maps the phase: CallUpdate -> GameManager.Update, CallLateUpdate -> GameManager.LateUpdate, CallFixedUpdate -> GameManager.FixedUpdate.

findings.modding: Patching Health.Update, DynamicLight.Update or WeaponMod.LateUpdate without warning does nothing — those methods do not exist. Always hook the CallX form. The phase mapping is an inference from naming; confirm with a runtime probe that logs the Time.frameCount and Time.inFixedTimeStep inside each CallX.

findings.title: STEP 10 — Update: BrainAI.RunBrainTick(float dt) is the one call per bot per logical tick, and it computes its own delta because ticks are irregular
findings.detail: GameManager.CallBrainUpdate() selects the slice and calls BrainAI.CallUpdate(float minSqrDistToPlayer) -> CallBrainUpdate() -> RunBrainTick(float dt). BrainAI keeps _lastCallUpdateTime/_callUpdateDt precisely because the scheduler skips frames. A priority lane bypasses the round-robin: GameManager.RequestPriorityBrainUpdate(BrainAI ai) adds to _priorityBrainUpdates (HashSet<BrainAI>) drained up to AI_MaxPriorityPerFrame. Two console-exposed knobs exist: GameManager.SetAI_UpdateFreqency(float time) and SetAI_UpdateIntervals(int frameCount), plus get_aiUpdateFrequency()/get_aiUpdateInterval(). Inside the tick: EyesAI.Vision()/DoorVision()/Hearing(), CalculateDynamicSpeed(float baseSpeed) with GetSlopeSpeedMultiplier() (itself throttled by _slopeCheckTimer/SlopeCheckInterval and cached in _cachedSlopeMultiplier), then AiAnimationController.Tick(float dt) and AiRotationController.Tick(float dt).

findings.modding: RunBrainTick(float) is THE hook for one call per bot per logical tick — use the dt argument, never Time.deltaTime, or your logic runs at the wrong rate. To make a bot react immediately, RequestPriorityBrainUpdate instead of shrinking the interval globally.

findings.title: STEP 11 — Update: the two remaining per-frame raycast budgets — EyesAI LOS and DynamicCoverFinder — both job-batched, only one with a hard cap
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.DynamicCoverFinder (singleton) enforces an explicit frame budget: TryAcquireQuerySlot() -> bool against maxQueriesPerFrame with _queriesThisFrame/_lastBudgetFrame, plus maxCandidatesPerQuery, over its own NativeArray<RaycastCommand> _cmds / NativeArray<RaycastHit> _results with RaycastMinPerJob and EnsureScratch(int n). Il2Cpp.EyesAI declares NO Update at all (only Awake) and is called from the brain tick; it has RaycastMinPerJob, _candidateIndices (List<int>) and cacheHit (RaycastHit) — the RaycastMinPerJob name is the RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch parameter — but it declares NO NativeArray fields, so it either allocates scratch per Vision() call or borrows a buffer. That difference is the open question for per-frame GC pressure at high bot counts.

findings.modding: maxQueriesPerFrame is a direct latency/CPU trade for how fast bots take cover. For EyesAI, the runtime probe is a GC.GetTotalMemory delta around Vision() with 30+ bots — if allocations scale with bot count, per-call NativeArray allocation is confirmed and is the single best AI optimisation available to a mod.

findings.title: STEP 12 — Update: A* Pathfinding runs as ECS, outside every MonoBehaviour — Il2CppPathfinding.FollowerEntity has no Update
findings.detail: Il2CppPathfinding.FollowerEntity declares only OnEnable(), Start() and OnDisable() — no Update, FixedUpdate or LateUpdate. Movement integration therefore happens inside Unity.Entities systems in the ECS SimulationSystemGroup, which Unity injects into the PlayerLoop independently of script order. This is the navigation half of bot movement; the other half (BrainAI.CalculateDynamicSpeed, SyncAgentAndAnimator, UpdateMovementRotation) runs in the amortised brain tick and writes into the agent. MasterController's UnityEngine.AI.NavMeshAgent field is vestigial — there is no baked NavMesh.
findings.members: Il2CppPathfinding.FollowerEntity.OnEnable, FollowerEntity.Start, FollowerEntity.OnDisable, BrainAI.SyncAgentAndAnimator, BrainAI.UpdateMovementRotation, MasterController.agent
findings.modding: There is no script-order lever over pathfinding and no MonoBehaviour to patch — bot movement cost is ECS job cost and scales with agent count independently of AI_MaxPerFrame. Writing agent maxSpeed directly is overwritten every brain tick by CalculateDynamicSpeed; patch that method instead.

findings.title: STEP 13 — Update: audio occlusion schedules its job here — AudioOcclusionJobManager.Update schedules, LateUpdate completes
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusionJobManager declares Awake(), Update() and LateUpdate(). Update schedules one RaycastCommand per registered OccludeSource into NativeArray<RaycastCommand> commands / NativeArray<RaycastHit> results with a JobHandle; LateUpdate calls CompleteJob() -> ApplyResults() -> SmoothSources(). It is additionally time-sliced by framesToSpread / currentSlice / sliceStart / sliceCount and updateInterval, so not every source is tested every frame. One ray per source means occlusion is binary — smoothing (lowPassSmoothingSpeed/volumeSmoothingSpeed, CutoffSnapEpsilon/VolumeSnapEpsilon) is what hides the pop. Two OTHER occlusion systems also run: the legacy Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion (a data blob with only Start(), mutated round-robin by GameManager) and Il2CppAxelF.Occlusion (its own LateUpdate, high+low pass, speedOfSound).

findings.modding: The schedule-in-Update / complete-in-LateUpdate split means a mod that stalls in LateUpdate before AudioOcclusionJobManager runs will serialise the job. Retuning AudioOcclusionJobManager touches only V2 sources — AxelF emitters and anything still on V1 are unaffected.

findings.title: STEP 14 — Update: the un-amortised strays — GroupDistanceCuller, GameobjectOptimize, LightFPS, ScopeInputSetter, NonDualRender, PoolTimerManager
findings.detail: Not everything got a manager. Il2Cpp.GroupDistanceCuller declares Update() on every instance (ParentObjectToDisable, DistanceToCull, culled) and Il2Cpp.GameobjectOptimize likewise declares Start()+Update() per instance (GameobjectToDisable, DistanceFromObject, VisibilityDistance, Distance, MainCamera) — naive per-object distance checks with no round-robin, in direct contrast to LightOptimizeManager. Il2Cpp.LightFPS declares Start()+Update() per light and throttles HDAdditionalLightData by fPSLimitType (FPSLimitType enum), fixedFps, fpsTimer, fpsTime. Il2Cpp.ScopeInputSetter.Update() and Il2Cpp.NonDualRender.Update() run per equipped optic. Il2Cpp.PoolTimerManager.Update() is the one that IS centralised: it walks three flat lists (delayedList, vfxList, bloodList) with SwapRemove<T>(List<T>, int) instead of an Update per pooled effect.

findings.modding: GroupDistanceCuller and GameobjectOptimize are the cheapest wins in a map-heavy scene if instance counts are high — count them at runtime before deciding. PoolTimerManager is the pattern to copy: register into a manager list, do not give your pooled object an Update.

findings.title: STEP 15 — LateUpdate: FinalIK and the animator-dependent body work, per player AND per bot
findings.detail: After Unity's Animator writes poses, the IK stack corrects them in LateUpdate. On the player, PlayerNetworking holds aimIK (RootMotion.FinalIK.AimIK), lookatIK (LookAtIK), grounderIK (GrounderFBBIK), interactionSystem (InteractionSystem), TP_LArm/TP_RArm (ArmIK) and kickBipedIK (FullBodyBipedIK); alongside them Il2Cpp.FeetIK (updateLegs, updateLegsProne, LoseBalanceDistance, MaxBendWeight) and Il2Cpp.CharAnimationHelper (blendshape blink, UpdateIK_L/UpdateIK_R coroutines). On bots, Il2Cpp.AiRotationController.LateUpdate() runs per bot with the spine/leg decoupling (_spineTransform, MaxSpineAngle, _legAngleCorrectionAmount) and Il2Cpp.BotAimCorrection has BOTH LateUpdate() and CallLateUpdate() — the latter is the GameManager-sliced path over allAIAimCorrection. WeaponsAI.IK_RangeCheck() is the only thing that switches bot arm IK off at distance.

findings.modding: FinalIK solving is the classic Unity LateUpdate hotspot and here it runs per character with only distance culling on the bot arms. GameManager ships Debug_DisableAllPlayerIK()/Debug_EnableAllPlayerIK() and DebugSetAIcullMode(AnimatorCullingMode) — use those to A/B the cost before optimising anything else.

findings.title: STEP 16 — LateUpdate: the camera/viewmodel follower stack, then four KINEMATION recoil rigs
findings.detail: Order within LateUpdate matters here and is script-execution-order dependent. Il2Cpp.FPS_Holder.LateUpdate() follows Head/RotationTrackerObject/Camera against CMF.CameraController (TrackRotation) and owns StartPositionBlend(float duration) mirroring MasterController.StartSeatPositionBlend(float)/_seatBlendTimer. Il2Cpp.Camera_Rotation_Tracker copies selected axes (CopyX/CopyY/CopyZ). Il2Cpp.Character_FollowCamera resolves the third-person body (isTracker/isTrackerPosition/isTrackerPositionAndRotation, Target/TargetNoAuth, InVehicle, Resolve()/SnapToTarget()). Il2Cpp.BetterFuckingSmoother interpolates the tracked Rigidbody for a list of Followers (YDamping/SnapYHeight/SnapRotation). Then MasterController applies four Il2CppKinemation.FPSFramework.Runtime.Recoil.RecoilAnimation instances — CameraRecoil, CameraHitShake, CameraShake, CameraSuppressionFlinch — plus two Il2CppWeaponBobbingV2.BobStyle2 (weaponBob, cameraBob). WeaponV3.LateUpdate() and BulletManager.LateUpdate() (tracers) also land here.

findings.modding: This is a chain of small followers, so a mod that inserts itself must respect script execution order or it will be overwritten by the next link. Recoil/flinch feel is retunable without code: HitShake and SuppressionFlinch are RecoilAnimData ScriptableObjects. For a spectator/free camera drive the shipped TpToggle and PlayerNetworking.freeCamera (ScreenshotFreeCamera) rather than fighting this stack.

findings.title: STEP 17 — LateUpdate: render-feeding followers that must run before culling — NvgLensFollower, FoliageBendFollow, SpeedTreeProxyManager
findings.detail: Three LateUpdate components exist purely to have data ready for the render phase. Il2Cpp.NvgLensFollower.LateUpdate()/OnEnable/OnDisable -> NotifyPassState() maintains the static lens registry (s_driver, s_activeCount, AnyActive, HasActiveLenses, LensCount, LensWorldCenters, ActiveLensRenderers) that NVGAutogateCustomPass.FillMeterCircles(Camera) projects; NvgScopeFollower subclasses it with its own s_scopeCount. Il2Cpp.FoliageBendFollow.LateUpdate() (setCenter, radius, stampWhenIdle, idleStampLength, lastPos, lastDirXZ) queues the swept-quad grass stamp consumed by FoliageBendPass. Il2Cpp.SpeedTreeProxyManager.LateUpdate() moves one camera-following proxy per tree prefab (TreeProxyInstances, TreeInstanceCounts, _cam) so BRG-instanced tree draws are not culled; InstancedTreeProxyManager is the non-SpeedTree twin.

findings.title: STEP 18 — End of PreLateUpdate: Mirror sends — Smooth Sync relays player transforms, MilkTransformSync target-rpcs objects per client through NetworkLOD
findings.detail: Player transforms are owner-authoritative and relayed, not validated: Smooth.SmoothSyncMirror with SmoothSyncFromOwnerToServer and SmoothSyncFromServerToNonOwners, plus SmoothSyncUpdate, InitialSmoothSync, SmoothSyncForcedUpdateTimer, childObjectSmoothSyncs, mainSmoothSync. Networked objects use Il2Cpp.MilkTransformSync, which has NO ClientRpc — the server loops connections and emits ReceivePosition(NetworkConnectionToClient, Vector3) / ReceiveRotation / ReceivePositionAndRotation as TargetRpcs. That hand-rolled interest management is gated by the static Il2Cpp.NetworkLOD.ShouldUpdate(Vector3 objectPosition, int stableId) -> bool against SQR_CLOSE / SQR_MID / SQR_FAR — per-recipient distance culling with stableId used to phase-offset which frame each object sends on. Bot replication has its own throttles: GameManager.SetBotSendThreshold(float) and ToggleFixedBotSendRate().

findings.modding: Send cost on the host is O(objects × connections) because of the TargetRpc design — a mod spawning many synced objects is a host-side CPU and bandwidth problem, not a client one. Pass distinct stableIds or every modded object phases onto the same frame and spikes. There is no server-side movement validation anywhere, so speed/teleport mods replicate as-is.

findings.title: STEP 19 — Render, before culling: BRGRenderer rebuilds batches and does its own GPU HZB occlusion culling — these objects are invisible to every Unity API
findings.detail: Il2CppBRGInstancedRenderer.BRGRenderer (singleton) draws vegetation and props through Unity's BatchRendererGroup: GetBatchID(int protoIndex) -> BatchID, BuildBatchMetadata(int protoIndex) -> NativeArray<MetadataValue>, NativeArray<BatchDrawCommandIndirect> stores, with dirty-state batching (RequestBatchRebuild(BatchRebuildScope), IncAddPrototype/IncRemovePrototype, IncAddPrototypeCommands/IncRemovePrototypeCommands, IncFlush(), IncFullRebuild(), MarkBatchesDirtyForFullRebuild(), FlushDirtyState()). Camera and shadow draw ranges are tracked separately — EmitCameraCommands/EmitShadowCommands(int protoIndex,...), AllocCameraCommand/AllocShadowCommand(ulong rangeKey,...), FindOrCreateCameraRange/FindOrCreateShadowRange(ulong key,...), ActiveCameraCommandCount/ActiveShadowCommandCount. Culling is its own GPU pipeline: cullingShader, uploadShader, OcclusionShader/_occlusionShader, CameraHZBState, CameraCullingContext, useHZB, ChunkVisibilitySlot, ViewFadeState; SpeedTree gets IsSpeedTreeProto(int)/EnsureSpeedTreeBatchIDs()/UpdateSpeedTree(). Il2Cpp.NakedTerrainRenderer sets Terrain.drawTreesAndFoliage=false to hand rendering over. GameManager exposes ToggleHZBOcclusionCulling(bool), SetCameraOcclusionCulling(bool), Quality_SetToGPUResidentDrawer(), SetMeshDetailDistance(int), SetFoliageQuality(int), SetMaximumLOD(int).

Add content via RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab + AddInstance and force a redraw with RequestBatchRebuild/IncFullRebuild. Calling IncFullRebuild per frame from a mod would be catastrophic; use the Inc* incremental API.

findings.title: STEP 20 — Render, culling stage: ScopeDOF.AggregateCullingParameters widens the culling set every frame even when the effect is off
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ScopeDOF : CustomPass overrides AggregateCullingParameters(ref ScriptableCullingParameters cullingParameters, HDCamera hdCamera) — it forces extra objects into the camera's culling results so its mask pass has something to draw. Alongside it, Il2Cpp.DisableCamCull subscribes RenderPipelineManager_beginCameraRendering(ScriptableRenderContext, Camera) and holds fields literally named number1..number6 (float) plus _cam — placeholder naming that shipped, most likely a manual bounds/culling override applied at camera-render time.

findings.modding: Setting ScopeDOF.EffectStrength to 0 does NOT recover the cost — AggregateCullingParameters still runs. Disabling the CustomPassVolume is the real perf win. Anything hooking beginCameraRendering runs once per camera per frame, which in this game means the main camera plus every active scope and laptop camera.

findings.title: STEP 21 — Render: the custom-pass chain — at least eleven CustomPass subclasses, two of them compute-driven and one using live C# reflection into HDRP internals
findings.detail: Confirmed CustomPass subclasses in Assembly-CSharp: NVGAutogateCustomPass (Execute -> ExecuteSceneAverage + ExecuteBurnIn, ComputeShader sceneAverageCompute with kernels kReduceTiles/kReduceFinal, ComputeBuffer zoneAvgBuffer, persistent BurnInTexture history RT, FillMeterCircles(Camera)/ProjectCircle(...)), NVGGrainCustomPass (RenderLensMask writes lensMaskBuffer by drawing lens Renderers submesh-by-submesh via GetSubMeshCount(Renderer)), NVGIRBeamsCustomPass, CapsuleShadows (ComputeShader compute with kernel/lightKernel, SetComputeParams, DispatchCharacterLight(ctx,int charactersCount), CreateExclusionsBuffer), ScopeDOF (seven RTHandles, GetGaussianWeights(int) cached in Dictionary<int,ComputeBuffer>, WeightedGaussianBlur/WeightedRadialBlur/RadialBlur), FoliageBendPass (ping-pong rtA/rtB, ID_DecayFactor, ID_GlobalRT), CameraDepthBake (offline depth/normal/tangent bake with a render latch), and three gbuffer/color/normal modifiers — AlbedoModifyPass, ColorModifyPass, NormalModifyPass. AlbedoModifyPass is the notable one: it holds Il2CppSystem.Reflection.FieldInfo s_GBufferOutputField and s_MrtField with TryResolveReflection(HDRenderPipeline pipeline) -> bool and cached s_ReflectionResolved/s_ReflectionAvailable — it reaches into HDRP's private gbuffer MRT bindings by reflection. HTraceAO adds six more pass objects (_prePassObject, _mvPassObject, _gBufferPassObject, _ssaoPassObject, _gtaoPassObject, _rtaoPassObject, _finalPassObject).

The NVG stack costs a compute reduction plus a persistent history RT every frame the tubes are down; NVGAutogateCustomPass.debugDisableMask and ManualGainLevel are plain setters, but the per-zone auto-gate will fight a mod that only pins ManualGainLevel unless the AutoGate*Speed values are pinned too.

findings.title: STEP 22 — Render: HTraceAO owns ambient occlusion and overwrites HDRP's own SSAO override every update
findings.detail: Il2CppHTraceAO.Rendering.HTraceAO selects among GTAO, SSAO and hardware RTAO via get_Profile() -> HTraceAOProfile + CheckProfile(), pinging pass objects with Ping(CustomPassObject) -> bool. Critically it creates and owns HDRP's own AO override: _ssaoOverrideComponent (UnityEngine.Rendering.HighDefinition.ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion), _volumeComponent (Volume), CreateSSAOOverrideComponent(), SetSSAOOverrideComponentSettings(), SetupVolumeHDRP(), UpdateSSAO(), InitComponentsHdrp(). RTAO is real ray tracing — Unity.UnifiedRayTracing.Runtime.dll ships. Debug pass names appear as literals: 'Thread Compaction', 'Occlusion Tracing', 'Temporal Filtering', 'Spatial Filtering', 'Contact Occlusion Rendering'.

findings.modding: A mod that sets HDRP's built-in ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion through the Volume stack is without warning reverted by the next SetSSAOOverrideComponentSettings — change the HTraceAOProfile instead. Whether RTAO is actually reachable on a given machine needs a runtime probe: read HTraceAO.Profile and log which pass objects Ping() true.

findings.title: STEP 23 — Render: custom post-processing is exactly two VolumeComponents, and registering a third at runtime probably will not take
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.MilkPostSettings and Il2Cpp.SuppressionPostFX both implement the HDRP contract get_injectionPoint() -> CustomPostProcessInjectionPoint, IsActive() -> bool, Setup(), Render(CommandBuffer cmd, HDCamera camera, RTHandle source, RTHandle destination), Cleanup(). MilkPostSettings is the global grade (intensity/Brightness/Gamma/Hue/Contrast/Saturation ClampedFloatParameters, shader Hidden/Shader/MilkPost). SuppressionPostFX is the being-shot-at blur/vignette/chroma effect with AddSuppression(float amount, float multiplier), ProccessSuppressionFrame(), ClampIntensityMultiplier(), a PreviousFrame shader id (temporal), and MakeFullySuppressed. Registration is gated by HDRenderPipelineGlobalSettings.beforeTransparentCustomPostProcesses / beforePostProcessCustomPostProcesses / beforeTAACustomPostProcesses / afterPostProcessBlursCustomPostProcesses / afterPostProcessCustomPostProcesses — all List<string> backed by m_CustomPostProcessOrdersSettings.
findings.members: MilkPostSettings.Render, MilkPostSettings.injectionPoint, SuppressionPostFX.AddSuppression, SuppressionPostFX.PreviousFrame, SuppressionPostFX.MakeFullySuppressed, HDRenderPipelineGlobalSettings.beforePostProcessCustomPostProcesses
findings.modding: A reshade-style mod needs no shader at all — drive MilkPostSettings through the Volume stack. SuppressionPostFX.AddSuppression(float,float) is a directly callable screen-effect trigger. But a NEW custom post-process type must have its name appended to one of those List<string> AND HDRP builds the ordered pass list when the pipeline is constructed, so appending after boot likely requires a pipeline rebuild.

findings.title: STEP 24 — Render: scope cameras are additional full HDRP camera renders, throttled by resolution, enable-state and frame interleaving
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ScopeInputSetter.Update() decides per frame what the optic costs: SetLowRes()/SetHighRes(), SetCamsDisabled()/SetCamsEnabled(), with state RenderLowResWhenUnADS (bool), UsingLowRes (bool), camEnabled (bool) and LastScopeFrame (int) — a frame index, i.e. the scope render is interleaved, not every frame. It owns ScopeCamera (Il2CppUltimateScopes.ScopeController), a cameraFPS (Il2Cpp.CameraFPS) budget object and a cameraDisable (Il2Cpp.CameraDisable) distance gate, plus two layer masks RegularScopeLayerMask / NVGScopeLayerMask. Il2Cpp.CameraFPS is data-only (fPSLimitType (FPSLimitType), fixedFps, maxFps) — no Update, it is read by ScopeInputSetter. Il2Cpp.CameraDisable carries distance and canZoomCamera. Il2Cpp.NonDualRender.Update() fades the non-dominant-eye render (renderers, localADS, targetAlpha/alpha/targetSpeed). Every camera also carries its own Il2Cpp.CameraSettings, and the static registry CameraSettings.AllCameraSettings (HashSet<CameraSettings>) includes scope cameras — flagged by isScopeCamera.

findings.modding: A magnified optic is a second scene render — the single most expensive thing a loadout can add. When forcing graphics quality, iterate CameraSettings.AllCameraSettings and SKIP isScopeCamera or you will break optics. SetCamSettings/SetBloom/UpdateShadowsQuality/SetMaxLod/SetVegetationLodBias/ToggleDynamicResolution are plain instance methods and are Harmony-patchable, unlike the il2cpp field accessors.

findings.title: STEP 25 — Render: upscaling is the last stage and hides fifteen backends behind one static facade
findings.detail: Il2CppTND.Upscaling.Framework.UpscalerName enumerates None, FSR1, FSR2, FSR3, FSR4, ASR, DLSS3, DLSS4, XeSS1, XeSS2, SGSR1, SGSR2, Reserved1..3, PSSR; UpscalerQuality is Off, Custom, NativeAA, UltraQuality, Quality, Balanced, Performance, UltraPerformance. The facade TNDUpscaler is fully static: SetUpscaler(UpscalerName) -> bool, GetSelectedUpscaler(), GetActiveUpscaler(), SetQuality(UpscalerQuality), GetScaling() -> float, SetSharpening(bool)/SetSharpness(float), SetAutoReactive(bool), GetUpscalerSettings(UpscalerName) -> UpscalerSettingsBase, ResetCamera(), GetSupported() -> List<UpscalerName>, IsSupported(UpscalerName). Shipped plugin assemblies: TND.Upscaling.FSR3, TND.Upscaling.DLSS4, TND.Upscaling.HDRP.DLSS, TND.Upscaling.XeSS2. Per-camera glue is CameraSettings.SetUpscalerSettings()/SetDLSSUpscalerSettings()/TND_upscaler and GameManager.ApplyUpscalerSettings()/DisableUpscalers().

Always verify with GetActiveUpscaler(), which is deliberately distinct from GetSelectedUpscaler() because a selection can without warning fail to activate. Upscaling interacts with the scope cameras (STEP 24) — TND_upscaler is per-CameraSettings.

findings.title: STEP 26 — Deferred across frames: lighting and shadows are amortised twice over, so light changes are visibly stale by design
findings.detail: Two independent amortisers. Il2Cpp.LightOptimizeManager (singleton) declares Awake()+Update() and walks get_AllLightOptimizers() (List<LightOptimize>) a slice at a time using NumToUpdatePerFrame / LastUpdatedIndex / NumLights, calling LightOptimize.UpdateLight() (which has no Update of its own) against LOD0_Distance..LOD3_Distance, disableLight, LightShadowLevel, updateInterval/_Timer. Separately GameManager round-robins DynamicLights (List<DynamicLight>) via DynamicLight.CallUpdate() with NumDynamicLightToUpdatePerFrame / _lastDynamicLightUpdated, and onDemandShadowMapUpdaters (List<OnDemandShadowMapUpdate>) via OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.CallUpdate(). That shadow updater is substantial: UpdateShadowMap(), UpdateCascades(), UpdateSubshadows(), UpdateOnCameraMove(), ResetCounters(), with per-distance-band wait tables fullShadowMapDistanceRefreshWaitFrames (Vector2[]) / ...WaitSeconds, per-cascade cascadesRefreshWaitFrames (int[]) / cascadesRefreshWaitSeconds (float[]), updateOnPlayerMove and playerToTrack. Il2Cpp.DirectionalLightResolution.SetShadowResolution() and Il2Cpp.LightFPS handle the sun and per-light refresh rate. Il2Cpp.RenderShadowAtStart declares NO Unity lifecycle method at all despite holding a static List<RenderShadowAtStart> ShadowsToRender — it can never run its own logic.

LightOptimizeManager.NumToUpdatePerFrame is one int trading CPU for light-LOD responsiveness. RenderShadowAtStart is dead or externally driven — worth a runtime instance count before relying on it.

findings.title: STEP 27 — Hard per-frame caps that without warning drop work: impact VFX, ricochet audio, decals and per-bullet impacts
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletEffectManager enforces MaxImpactVFXPerFrame with _impactVFXThisFrame/_lastResetFrame behind CanSpawnImpactVFX() -> bool, and three runtime kill switches ImpactVFXEnabled/ImpactDecalsEnabled/ImpactSFXEnabled with ToggleImpactVFX()/ToggleImpactDecals()/ToggleImpactSFX(). Il2Cpp.BulletCrack independently caps ricochet audio with MaxRicochetSoundsPerFrame/_ricochetSoundsThisFrame/_lastRicochetResetFrame. Per bullet: maxImpactPenetration, maxImpactNonPenetration, currentImpactSFXCount, and BulletInstance.IsPointInFrustum(Vector3 worldPoint) culls offscreen effects entirely. Pool sizes are themselves divided from a global budget by Il2Cpp.PoolInitializer — CountDecalPrefabs()/CountImpactVFXPrefabs() then InitSurfacePools(SurfaceInformation, int perDecal, int perVFX) against TotalDecalBudget/MinDecalsPerPrefab/MaxDecalsPerPrefab/TotalVFXBudget. Il2Cpp.ObjectPooler adds LRU theft for bounded pools (BoundedPrefabs, ActiveByPrefab (Dictionary<GameObject,LinkedList<PooledObject>>), ReclaimOldestIfBounded(GameObject)) and 'parking' (teleport away instead of SetActive(false)) to avoid OnEnable/OnDisable churn.

Registering a new SurfaceInformation divides the same global budget more ways and shrinks every existing pool toward MinDecalsPerPrefab, so raise TotalDecalBudget/TotalVFXBudget in step. findings.title: STEP 28 — Boot-time prerequisite: ShaderWarmup holds the splash screen and gates when a mod may safely touch shaders
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ShaderWarmup runs WarmupRoutine() -> WarmDecalsAndImpacts() / WarmBulletTracer() / WarmSurface(SurfaceInformation info, Vector3 warmPos, List<PooledObject> spawnedPooled) -> int, over shaderVariantCollection (ShaderVariantCollection), prefabsToWarm (GameObject[]) and bulletPrefab, holding applicationSplashScreen (Il2Cpp.ApplicationSplashScreen) until done. It publishes a public static get_IsComplete() -> bool. Companions: Il2Cpp.DecalWarmup (WarmupDecals(), WarmupSurface(SurfaceInformation), DecalsWarmedup, CubeDisableTimer) and Il2Cpp.KillPooledDecals (Start() only — one-shot cleanup of the warmup litter). GameManager mirrors this with WarmDecalPools() and WarmSurfaceDecals(SurfaceInformation).

This matters directly for the established AssetBundle trap (bundles load but lose materials, and you rebind with Shader.Find).

findings.title: SUMMARY — the ranked list of what actually costs, and the six knobs worth turning first
findings.detail: Ranked by evidence that the developers themselves fought it (a budget, cap or round-robin exists only where something was expensive): (1) AI logic and physics — nine GameManager round-robins; (2) per-bot un-amortised WeaponsAI.Update/FixedUpdate + AiAnimationController.Update + AiRotationController.LateUpdate, the only AI work NOT sliced; (3) FinalIK per character in LateUpdate, culled only by WeaponsAI.maxIKdistance; (4) BulletManager.FixedUpdate job raycasts, scaling with rounds in flight and predictionStepsPerFrame; (5) DynamicCoverFinder.maxQueriesPerFrame raycast budget; (6) impact VFX/decal/ricochet caps (BulletEffectManager.MaxImpactVFXPerFrame, BulletCrack.MaxRicochetSoundsPerFrame, PoolInitializer budgets); (7) scope cameras as extra full HDRP renders, mitigated by ScopeInputSetter low-res/disable/frame-interleave; (8) the custom-pass chain, with ScopeDOF's AggregateCullingParameters costing even at zero strength and NVGAutogateCustomPass running a compute reduction plus a history RT; (9) HTraceAO with up to hardware RTAO; (10) shadow refresh, deliberately stale via OnDemandShadowMapUpdate; (11) audio occlusion, one batched ray per source spread over framesToSpread; (12) host-side Mirror send, O(objects x connections) because MilkTransformSync uses TargetRpc + NetworkLOD instead of ClientRpc. The six first knobs: GameManager.AI_MaxPerFrame / AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks, WeaponsAI.maxIKdistance, DynamicCoverFinder.maxQueriesPerFrame, LightOptimizeManager.NumToUpdatePerFrame, ScopeDOF's CustomPassVolume enabled-state (not EffectStrength), and TNDUpscaler.SetUpscaler/SetQuality.

findings.modding: Two rules for a mod author. First, never add per-frame work to anything with a CallX method — you are inside someone else's budget and you will consume another object's slot. Second, before optimising, use the shipped instrumentation: GameManager.SetFPSCounter(), DEBUG_GetGraphicsInformation(), Debug_DisableAllPlayerIK(), DebugSetAIcullMode(AnimatorCullingMode), SetCameraOcclusionCulling(bool), ToggleHZBOcclusionCulling(bool), Quality_SetToMain/Quality_SetToGPUResidentDrawer/Quality_SetToLowQualityColour — most are gated by DevConsole.HasDevAccess(ulong)/RequireDevAccess(), which are ordinary methods and therefore Harmony-patchable to return true locally.

findings.detail: Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard holds MinAI (int), MaxAI (int), Difficulty (GameManager/AIDifficulty), achievement_min_ai_amount, HVTSpawnIsRandom. The player moves sliders through Il2Cpp.OperationBoardUI.SetAI_COUNT(float) / SetAI_HVT_COUNT(float) / SetOpforDifficulty(int) / SetHVTSpawnPoint(int), which forward to CerebusOpboard.SetAI_COUNT(float) and CerebusOpboard.SetAI_HVT_COUNT(float). Neither OperationBoardUI nor CerebusOpboard is a NetworkBehaviour (no UserCode_*/SerializeSyncVars members on either), so this is purely local state on each machine.

findings.title: STEP 1 — CerebusOpboard.Start_Operation() → OperationsManager.StartOperation → CMD_StartOperation → RPC_StartOperation → SERVER_LoadOperation, carrying NO AI data
findings.detail: OperationsManager.StartOperation(string sceneName, int prepTime, string displayName, string infilTime, string _activeAchievement, float targetTime) is mirrored exactly by CMD_StartOperation(same 6 args) -> RPC_StartOperation(int defaultInfil) -> SERVER_LoadOperation(). There is no bot count, no HVT count and no AIDifficulty anywhere in that payload. The numbers therefore never cross the wire — every client computes them from its own identical copy of the opboard prefab, and only the host's copy is ever consumed by the spawner.

findings.title: STEP 2 — The numbers land on GameManager as botAmount / botHVTAmount / AI_Difficulty

RaidManager itself has NO count field of any kind — its entire member list is prefab pools, spawn-point lists and timers. So the loop bound for spawning must come from GameManager.botAmount.

findings.title: STEP 3 — Scene loads; RaidManager.Awake() claims the singleton, RaidManager.OnStartServer() is the spawn kickoff
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.RaidManager.Awake() sets the static singleton; OnStartServer() is the server-only entry. OnStartServer compiles to SIX deferred closures (_OnStartServer_b__43_0 through _OnStartServer_b__43_5), all void() — the shape of a batch of Invoke/coroutine-scheduled setup steps, matching the botSpawnDelay (float) field. RaidManager.OnStartClient() exists separately and does the client-visible half.

findings.detail: Il2Cpp.RaidManager.ServerSpawnAI(bool _custom) selects from standardAI (GameObject[]) when false and customAI (List<GameObject>) when true. Il2Cpp.BotSpawner — despite the name — is a legacy dev tool: it has spawnCode (UnityEngine.KeyCode), SpawnTargets() (IEnumerator), MaxLocalBotAmount/LocalBotAmount, and its CMDSpawnTargets() has NO corresponding UserCode_ method, so it is not a Mirror Command and never crosses the wire. Il2Cpp.AiTeam likewise has zero methods.

The candidate pool is RaidManager.botSpawnPoints (List<GameObject>); each such GameObject carries an Il2Cpp.BotSpawnDetails component that is the authored config for whatever spawns there.
