findings.modding: Placement for a custom map is just a list of GameObjects with BotSpawnDetails on them — no baked data, no navmesh authoring. BotSpawnDetails.isSpawnGroup + GroupSpawnPoints is how squads are placed together.

findings.title: STEP 6 — RaidManager.CanSpawn(Vector3 pos, float radius) is the placement veto
findings.detail: CanSpawn(UnityEngine.Vector3 pos, float radius) -> bool is a proximity gate applied before instantiation — the guard that stops a bot materialising on top of a player or inside another spawn. It is private and takes only a position and radius, so it is a pure spatial test with no knowledge of the prefab.
findings.members: RaidManager.CanSpawn(Vector3,float), RaidManager.GetValidSpawnPoint
findings.modding: Prefix CanSpawn returning true to force spawns anywhere (useful for debugging placement), or tighten it to keep bots out of a custom safe zone.

findings.title: STEP 7 — RaidManager.InstantiateBot(...) creates the GameObject and hands it to Mirror
findings.detail: InstantiateBot(UnityEngine.GameObject pfab, UnityEngine.Vector3 position, UnityEngine.Quaternion rotation, UnityEngine.Transform parent) -> UnityEngine.GameObject is the single instantiation point for standard AI, HVTs and (via VehicleAI.InstantiateBot, a separate copy) turret gunners. Because bots are NetworkBehaviours (BrainAI, WeaponsAI, Health, TeamIdentifier, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC are all weaved), this must be followed by Mirror NetworkServer.Spawn — not visible in signatures.
findings.members: RaidManager.InstantiateBot(GameObject,Vector3,Quaternion,Transform), VehicleAI.InstantiateBot
findings.modding: InstantiateBot is the one hook that sees every bot GameObject the instant it exists, before any component initialises. Best place to attach custom components.

findings.title: STEP 8 — RaidManager.ApplyBotSpawnSettings(GameObject bot, BotSpawnDetails details) is the single config funnel
findings.detail: This is the only place authored spawn config lands on a brain. BotSpawnDetails supplies idleState (BrainAI/IdleStates), reactType (BrainAI/ReactType), doorInteractionType (BrainAI/DoorInteractionMode), DetectionTimeMultiplier, DetectionRange, HearingRange, FOV, maxEffectiveRange, useComms, DoesCounterSuppression, WanderDistance, modifyStance/doesCrouch/doesProne, disableNavmesh, isProne, and the patrol route (patrolPoints List<Transform>, PatrolSpeed, PatrolLooping, patrolWaitTime). Critically crouchDistance and proneDistance are UnityEngine.Vector2 on BotSpawnDetails but plain float on BrainAI — a min/max range is authored and a scalar is ROLLED per bot here, which is where squad variety comes from.
findings.members: RaidManager.ApplyBotSpawnSettings(GameObject,BotSpawnDetails), BotSpawnDetails.crouchDistance (Vector2), BrainAI.crouchDistance (float), BotSpawnDetails.patrolPoints, BotSpawnDetails.reactType, BotSpawnDetails.hvtLinkedSpawnGroup
findings.modding: Postfix ApplyBotSpawnSettings to override any authored bot config globally in one hook. Overwriting BrainAI's scalars afterwards makes a squad uniform — the Vector2 ranges are the intended variety source.

findings.title: STEP 9 — HVTs spawn through a parallel path and register with OperationsManager
findings.detail: RaidManager.ServerSpawnHVTs() draws from hvtAI (GameObject[]) over hvtSpawnPoints (GameObject[]), count from GameManager.botHVTAmount, randomised by CerebusOpboard.HVTSpawnIsRandom. The bot is registered as an objective via OperationsManager.AddHVTBot(Il2Cpp.BrainAI hvtBrain) into OperationsManager.AI_HVTs (List<BrainAI>), and the brain carries BrainAI.isHVT (bool) and BrainAI.myName (string). BotSpawnDetails.hvtLinkedSpawnGroup (BotSpawnDetails) ties a bodyguard group to an HVT.
findings.members: RaidManager.ServerSpawnHVTs, RaidManager.hvtAI, RaidManager.hvtSpawnPoints, OperationsManager.AddHVTBot(BrainAI), OperationsManager.AI_HVTs, BrainAI.isHVT, BrainAI.myName, BotSpawnDetails.hvtLinkedSpawnGroup
findings.modding: BrainAI.myName is the string later matched by RaidManager.CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, uint hvtID) — set it consistently or body-confirm objectives break.

findings.title: STEP 10 — Stat registration: OperationsManager.AddBot() bumps the replicated TotalBots
findings.detail: OperationsManager exposes ResetStats(), AddBot(), AddHVTBot(BrainAI), AddOperator(), AddKill(), AddIntelSpawned(), AddIntelCollected() over SyncVars TotalBots, TotalKills, TotalOperatorsInRaid, IntelSpawned, IntelCollected, HVTdead, WasNight. AddBot is the spawn-side counterpart to AddKill at the death end, and TotalBots is what the mission-complete screen and achievement checks read.
findings.members: OperationsManager.AddBot, OperationsManager.TotalBots (SyncVar), OperationsManager.ResetStats, GameManagerNetwork.CheckAchievements, CerebusOpboard.achievement_min_ai_amount
findings.modding: achievement_min_ai_amount is compared against this population — spawning fewer bots than the board demands is why low-AI runs without warning fail to unlock.

findings.title: STEP 11 — Turret gunners are a second, independent spawn path
findings.detail: RaidManager.SpawnStaticVehicleAI() (gated by spawnVehicleAI, spawnChancePerPoint, maxStaticVehicles, staticVehicleSpawnPoints[], staticVehicleAI[]) creates Il2Cpp.VehicleAI, which then runs its OWN ServerSpawnTurrentAI() -> its own InstantiateBot(...) -> turrentBot (BrainAI) at TurrentSpawn, wired to clients by Cmd_SetBrain(Mirror.NetworkIdentity target) and RPC_SetTurrentAITypeShit(NetworkConnectionToClient target, BrainAI brain). VehicleAI reimplements Vision/FindTarget/GenerateNearMissOffset/FireCannon entirely — it shares no code with BrainAI/EyesAI.
findings.members: RaidManager.SpawnStaticVehicleAI, RaidManager.maxStaticVehicles, VehicleAI.ServerSpawnTurrentAI, VehicleAI.turrentBot, VehicleAI.RPC_SetTurrentAITypeShit, VehicleAI.Vision, VehicleAI.FireCannon
findings.modding: Any perception or accuracy change must be applied twice — once to BrainAI/EyesAI and once to VehicleAI — or manned turrets behave inconsistently with infantry.

findings.title: STEP 12 — BrainAI.Awake() caches the component graph and joins the scheduler roster
findings.detail: BrainAI resolves its siblings as fields readable via properties: eyesAI (Il2Cpp.EyesAI), health (Il2Cpp.Health), agent (Il2Cpp.AgentController), weapons (Il2Cpp.WeaponsAI), networkAnimatorSyncNPC (Il2Cpp.NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC), dynamicCoverFinder (Il2Cpp.DynamicCoverFinder), aiPatrol (Il2Cpp.AIPatrol), anim (UnityEngine.Animator), MyTeamIdentifierReference (Il2Cpp.TeamIdentifierReference). It also joins the static HashSet BrainAI.AllBrainAI and the scheduler list GameManager.allAI (List<BrainAI>).
findings.members: BrainAI.Awake, BrainAI.eyesAI, BrainAI.health, BrainAI.agent, BrainAI.weapons, BrainAI.networkAnimatorSyncNPC, BrainAI.dynamicCoverFinder, BrainAI.aiPatrol, BrainAI.AllBrainAI, GameManager.allAI
findings.modding: BrainAI.AllBrainAI (static) is the cheapest enumeration of every live bot for a debug overlay; GameManager.allAI is the list the scheduler actually walks.

findings.title: STEP 13 — TeamIdentifier.Awake/OnStartServer/Start registers the bot with TeamManager
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.TeamIdentifier has Awake(), OnStartServer(), Start(), OnDestroy() and OnTeamChanged(int previous, int current) over the SyncVar TeamID. Registration goes through TeamManager.EnsureTeam(int id) then TeamManager.AddOperatorToTeam(int teamID, TeamIdentifier). Il2Cpp.TeamIdentifierReference.SetTeamIdentifier(TeamIdentifier) is the lightweight back-pointer BrainAI reads through (BrainAI.TeamId, BrainAI.TeamName, BrainAI.MyTeamStats, BrainAI.FriendlyTeamNames, BrainAI.CommsRange are all read-only getters).
findings.members: TeamIdentifier.OnStartServer, TeamIdentifier.OnTeamChanged(int,int), TeamManager.EnsureTeam(int), TeamManager.AddOperatorToTeam(int,TeamIdentifier), TeamIdentifierReference.SetTeamIdentifier, BrainAI.TeamId, TeamStats
findings.modding: Flipping a bot to the player team is one SyncVar write (TeamIdentifier.TeamID) on the server; the OnTeamChanged hook re-registers it. AI and players share the same int-keyed model.

findings.title: STEP 14 — BrainAI.Start() → SetDifficultyAndStats() applies the global difficulty tier
findings.detail: BrainAI.SetDifficultyAndStats() is a no-arg method, so it must read the global GameManager.AI_Difficulty rather than receive it. What it writes: difficultyAccuracy (tooltip literal '0 = stormtrooper, 1 = aimbot'), baseHitChance, maxEffectiveRangeFalloff, ReactionTime/_baseReactionTime, TimeToContact/TimeToContactMultiplier, AimSnap/MinAimSnap/BaseAimSnap, SkillRandomness, TurnSpeed/turnSpeedMultiplier, Patience, ForgetTime. Because it runs at Start and reads a global, difficulty changed mid-raid does not retroactively apply to already-spawned bots unless it is called again.
findings.members: BrainAI.Start, BrainAI.SetDifficultyAndStats, BrainAI.difficultyAccuracy, BrainAI.baseHitChance, BrainAI._baseReactionTime, BrainAI.SkillRandomness, GameManager.AI_Difficulty
findings.modding: Calling SetDifficultyAndStats() again across GameManager.allAI is how you retune a live squad after GameManager.SetAIDifficulty. Patching it is the clean per-archetype difficulty override.

findings.title: STEP 15 — AgentController.Awake() is the ONLY place Assembly-CSharp touches A*
findings.detail: A signature sweep of all 206 assemblies for AstarPath/FollowerEntity/NavGraph/GraphNode/GraphUpdate types found exactly one Assembly-CSharp hit: Il2Cpp.AgentController.Agent -> Il2CppPathfinding.FollowerEntity. AgentController's only Unity lifecycle method is Awake() (plus CallUpdate()); it also holds OffMeshHandler (Il2Cpp.BotOffmeshLinkHandler), doorWalkLayer/doorOpenLayer/doorBreachLayer (int) and currentDoorInteractionMode. BrainAI never references an A* type directly — everything routes through this facade (position, velocity, destination, pathPending, remainingDistance, hasPath, stopDistance, maxSpeed, rotationSpeed, maxRotationSpeed, updatePosition, updateRotation).
findings.members: AgentController.Awake, AgentController.Agent (Pathfinding.FollowerEntity), AgentController.OffMeshHandler, AgentController.entityExists, AgentController.CallUpdate, BrainAI.agent
findings.modding: Seeker/RichAI/AIPath tutorials do not apply and Unity NavMesh calls are inert. Custom AI movement must go through FollowerEntity's ECS API — or, better, through AgentController's facade.

findings.title: STEP 16 — Graph attachment is passive: FollowerEntity's own OnEnable creates the ECS entity, no game code scans
findings.detail: No Assembly-CSharp type calls AstarPath.Scan / ScanAsync / UpdateGraphs / AddWorkItem — those exist only inside Il2CppAstarPathfindingProject. Therefore a spawned bot 'attaches to the graph' purely by having its FollowerEntity component enabled against whatever AstarPath instance the map scene ships; AgentController.entityExists (bool) is the readback that the ECS entity was created. BotSpawnDetails.disableNavmesh (bool) is how an authored spawn point opts a bot out of navigation entirely.
findings.members: AgentController.entityExists, Pathfinding.FollowerEntity, AstarPath.Scan, AstarPath.UpdateGraphs, BotSpawnDetails.disableNavmesh
findings.modding: A custom map must ship its own AstarPath with a scanned (or runtime-scanned) graph — nothing in the game code will scan one for you. Bots spawned onto an unscanned graph will have entityExists true but never path.

findings.title: STEP 17 — Door capability is applied as an A* traversal tag mask, not as behaviour
findings.detail: AgentController.SetDoorMode(BrainAI/DoorInteractionMode mode) toggles AgentController.EnableNavigationTag(int layer) / DisableNavigationTag(int layer) over the three authored tag indices doorWalkLayer, doorOpenLayer, doorBreachLayer. DoorInteractionMode = {CantGoThrough, CanGoThroughButNotOpen, CanOpenAndGoThrough}. A bot that cannot open doors simply cannot traverse the doorOpenLayer tag — the pathfinder routes around it.
findings.members: AgentController.SetDoorMode(DoorInteractionMode), AgentController.EnableNavigationTag(int), AgentController.DisableNavigationTag(int), AgentController.doorWalkLayer, AgentController.doorOpenLayer, AgentController.doorBreachLayer, BotSpawnDetails.doorInteractionType
findings.modding: Change door behaviour by flipping the mode, never by editing pathfinding. Custom maps must tag door links with the same three layer indices or bots will never use doors.

findings.title: STEP 18 — BotOffmeshLinkHandler.OnEnable() installs the off-mesh link state machine
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BotOffmeshLinkHandler implements both Pathfinding.IOffMeshLinkHandler and Pathfinding.IOffMeshLinkStateMachine, exposed as explicit interface implementations: Pathfinding_IOffMeshLinkHandler_GetOffMeshLinkStateMachine(Pathfinding.ECS.AgentOffMeshLinkTraversalContext) -> IOffMeshLinkStateMachine, Pathfinding_IOffMeshLinkStateMachine_OnTraverseOffMeshLink(ctx) -> Il2CppSystem.Collections.IEnumerable (coroutine-style traversal), OnFinishTraversingOffMeshLink(ctx), OnAbortTraversingOffMeshLink(). It registers/unregisters in OnEnable()/OnDisable(). Traversal flags: OnOffLink, ReachedLink, OpeningDoor, TravelingLink, Finished, KickRequested, WaitingForKick, KickHappened.
findings.members: BotOffmeshLinkHandler.OnEnable, BotOffmeshLinkHandler.Pathfinding_IOffMeshLinkStateMachine_OnTraverseOffMeshLink, BotOffmeshLinkHandler.IsBreacher, BotOffmeshLinkHandler.DoorKickForce, BotOffmeshLinkHandler._doorCooldowns (Dictionary<DoorV2,float>)
findings.modding: The IEnumerable traversal is the clean insertion point for custom door animations. _doorCooldowns is a per-door dictionary so bots cannot spam-kick the same door.

findings.title: STEP 19 — EyesAI.Awake() resolves the stance-aware eye rig
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.EyesAI.Awake() is its only Unity lifecycle method — there is NO Update() on EyesAI. It resolves EyesTransform, EyesTransformPivotPoint, Head, _animTransform, _eyesTransform, initEulurRotation, offset, and the three stance heights StandingEyesOffset / CrouchEyesOffset / ProneEyesOffset, plus DetectionLayerMask and the back-pointer brain.
findings.members: EyesAI.Awake, EyesAI.EyesTransform, EyesAI.StandingEyesOffset, EyesAI.CrouchEyesOffset, EyesAI.ProneEyesOffset, EyesAI.DetectionLayerMask, EyesAI.brain
findings.modding: Custom bot rigs need an eye transform and a head transform assigned or perception without warning fails — Awake resolves them once and never retries.

findings.title: STEP 20 — WeaponsAI.Start() → SERVER_SpawnFirearm() → PuppetWeapon.AI_Equip(WeaponsAI) assigns the loadout
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponsAI.Start() runs SERVER_SpawnFirearm() (gated by the SpawnWeapon bool), which selects from weaponList (List<Il2Cpp.PuppetWeapon>) BY INDEX and publishes that index as the SyncVar puppetWeaponIndex (hook OnPuppetWeaponIndexUpdate(int previous, int current)), with puppetWeaponID alongside. The chosen weapon is bound by Il2Cpp.PuppetWeapon.AI_Equip(Il2Cpp.WeaponsAI _weaponsAI) — the AI counterpart to PuppetWeapon.Player_Equip(PlayerNetworking). RaidManager.prohibitedWeapons (PuppetWeapon[]) and mapSpecificWeapons (PuppetWeapon[]) gate what bots may carry per map.
findings.members: WeaponsAI.Start, WeaponsAI.SERVER_SpawnFirearm, WeaponsAI.SpawnWeapon, WeaponsAI.weaponList, WeaponsAI.puppetWeaponIndex (SyncVar), PuppetWeapon.AI_Equip(WeaponsAI), RaidManager.prohibitedWeapons, RaidManager.mapSpecificWeapons
findings.modding: puppetWeaponIndex syncs as a LIST INDEX, so weaponList must be append-only and identical across host and clients — same constraint as LoadoutManager.Game_Weapons. Insert in the middle and every client equips the wrong gun.

findings.title: STEP 21 — Health.Awake/Start + GetHitBoxes() coroutine builds the AI hitbox index map
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Health.GetHitBoxes() is an IEnumerator run at init that populates the lookup behind Health.GetHitboxIndex(string name) -> int. Health.isBot (bool) distinguishes the AI path, Health.brainAI (BrainAI) is the back-pointer, and Health.MyTeamIdentifierReference ties it to the team model. Health has Awake(), Start(), OnStartClient(), OnEnable(), OnDisable(), OnDestroy() and — notably — CallUpdate() but NO Update(): it is ticked by GameManager's allBotHealth round-robin (Health_BotLastUpdateIndex / Health_BotNumPerFrame).
findings.members: Health.GetHitBoxes, Health.GetHitboxIndex(string), Health.isBot, Health.brainAI, Health.CallUpdate, GameManager.allBotHealth, GameManager.Health_BotNumPerFrame
findings.modding: Hitbox indices are resolved from BONE NAMES at init, so a custom bot rig must keep the shipped bone naming or every AI hit resolves to index -1.

findings.title: STEP 22 — Presentation components register: BotAimCorrection into GameManager.allAIAimCorrection
findings.detail: GameManager owns three independent round-robins over bot components: allAI (List<BrainAI>) for logic, allAIAimCorrection (List<BotAimCorrection>) driven from GameManager.LateUpdate() via BotAimCorrection.CallLateUpdate() with AIweaponCollisionUpdatePerFrame/_lastAIweaponCollisionUpdated, and allBotHealth (List<Health>). Alongside, Il2Cpp.BotNetworking is a data-only manifest (scriptsToDisable: Behaviour[], zero methods) that some other system uses to strip behaviours on non-authoritative instances.
findings.members: GameManager.allAIAimCorrection, GameManager.LateUpdate, BotAimCorrection.CallLateUpdate, GameManager.AIweaponCollisionUpdatePerFrame, BotNetworking.scriptsToDisable
findings.modding: Patching BotNetworking accomplishes nothing — it has no code. Find the reader of scriptsToDisable instead.

findings.title: STEP 23 — The tick: GameManager.Update() → CallBrainUpdate() → BrainAI.CallUpdate(float) → CallBrainUpdate() → RunBrainTick(float dt)
findings.detail: There is no AIManager type. GameManager.Update() fans out via CallBrainUpdate() using index-based round-robin time slicing (AI_UpdateIndex, AI_MinPerFrame, AI_MaxPerFrame, AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks) plus a priority lane (_priorityBrainUpdates HashSet<BrainAI>, RequestPriorityBrainUpdate(BrainAI), AI_MaxPriorityPerFrame). GameManager.FixedUpdate() drives CallFixedBrainUpdate() -> BrainAI.CallPhysicsFixedUpdate() (AI_FixedUpdateIndex, AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame). BrainAI has NO Update() and NO FixedUpdate() of its own — only CallUpdate(float minSqrDistToPlayer), CallBrainUpdate(), CallPhysicsFixedUpdate(), and RunBrainTick(float dt) which is the real body. Because ticks are irregular, the brain computes its own delta from _lastCallUpdateTime into _callUpdateDt.
findings.members: GameManager.Update, GameManager.CallBrainUpdate, GameManager.CallFixedBrainUpdate, GameManager.RequestPriorityBrainUpdate(BrainAI), GameManager.AI_MaxPerFrame, BrainAI.CallUpdate(float), BrainAI.RunBrainTick(float), BrainAI._callUpdateDt
findings.modding: Hook BrainAI.RunBrainTick(float) for exactly one call per bot per logical tick. Never add per-frame work inside BrainAI — it is already amortised. GameManager.SetAI_UpdateIntervals(int) slows the brain enough to watch transitions live.

findings.title: STEP 24 — RunBrainTick's internal sequence, in declaration order
findings.detail: BrainAI's method table lists the per-tick updaters consecutively, which in il2cpp metadata reflects source declaration order: UpdateMovementRotation() → UpdateTimers(float dt) → UpdateLookAtTargets(float dt) → UpdateInteriorCheck(float dt) → UpdateStanceAndCombatState() → UpdateSuppressionAndEvadeLogic() → UpdateStanceBasedOnDistance() → UpdateWeaponAndAnimatorSync() → UpdateStateMachine(float dt) → UpdateAccuracyAndSnap(float dt) → UpdateFlashedAndDetection(float dt) → UpdateRespondingLogic(float dt) → UpdateTeamConfidence(float dt) → UpdateStuckDetection(float dt). SyncAgentAndAnimator() and CalculateDynamicSpeed(float) sit immediately before them in the table, next to CallUpdate.
findings.members: BrainAI.RunBrainTick, BrainAI.UpdateTimers, BrainAI.UpdateStanceAndCombatState, BrainAI.UpdateStateMachine, BrainAI.UpdateAccuracyAndSnap, BrainAI.UpdateTeamConfidence, BrainAI.UpdateStuckDetection, BrainAI.SyncAgentAndAnimator
findings.modding: Declaration order is a strong but not conclusive proxy for call order — settle it by logging entry to each Update* method for one bot over ten ticks with GameManager.SetAI_UpdateIntervals set high.

findings.title: STEP 25 — Perception: EyesAI.UpdateEyes() is pulled by the brain, throttled by _lastEyesUpdateTime
findings.detail: EyesAI has no Unity Update, so EyesAI.UpdateEyes() must be called from the brain tick. It self-throttles on _lastEyesUpdateTime and refreshes its enemy roster on _teamListRefreshTimer. EyesAI.SetEyesForward(Vector3 forward) aims the sensor. The roster itself comes allocation-free from TeamManager.GetPossibleTargets(int myTeam, List<UnityEngine.Transform> results), backed by TeamRuntimeData.AddTarget/RemoveTarget.
findings.members: EyesAI.UpdateEyes, EyesAI._lastEyesUpdateTime, EyesAI._teamListRefreshTimer, EyesAI.SetEyesForward(Vector3), TeamManager.GetPossibleTargets(int,List<Transform>), TeamRuntimeData.GetPossibleTargets
findings.modding: UpdateEyes is the one hook that fires once per perception tick per bot — cheaper than patching Vision/Hearing separately.

findings.title: STEP 26 — Three perception passes: EyesAI.Vision(), EyesAI.DoorVision(), EyesAI.Hearing()
findings.detail: Vision() tests LOS via EyesAI.TestIfCanSeeAtHeight(UnityEngine.Vector3 height, UnityEngine.Transform target) -> bool at the stance-appropriate eye offset, and each posture is independently gateable by CanSeeIfStanding / CanSeeIfCrouching / CanSeeIfProne — a bot can be configured unable to see prone targets at all. Acuity is graduated, not a hard cutoff: BrainAI.EyesFOVAngle, EyesFOVDistancePerfect, EyesFOVDistanceDecimateMultiplier, DetectionRange (with originalDetectionRange kept separately so GameManager.SetBotViewDistanceMultiplier(float) can scale it), HasNVG. LOS raycasts appear batched — EyesAI holds _candidateIndices (List<int>), RaycastMinPerJob (int, the RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch parameter name) and cacheHit — but unlike DynamicCoverFinder it declares no NativeArray fields, so buffer ownership is unresolved.
findings.members: EyesAI.Vision, EyesAI.DoorVision, EyesAI.Hearing, EyesAI.TestIfCanSeeAtHeight(Vector3,Transform), EyesAI.CanSeeIfProne, EyesAI.RaycastMinPerJob, BrainAI.EyesFOVDistanceDecimateMultiplier, BrainAI.originalDetectionRange, GameManager.SetBotViewDistanceMultiplier
findings.modding: Runtime probe worth doing: GC delta around Vision() with 30+ bots. If allocations scale with bot count, EyesAI allocates its RaycastCommand arrays per call and that is a real perf-mod target.

findings.title: STEP 27 — Target selection is a SCORE, not nearest-first: EyesAI.ScoreTarget → FindTarget
findings.detail: EyesAI.FindTarget() -> UnityEngine.Transform is driven by EyesAI.ScoreTarget(UnityEngine.Transform candidate, float maxRange) -> float; EyesAI.FindClosestsTarget() -> Transform exists separately as a fallback. The winner lands on BrainAI.CurrentSeenTarget, and the bot's belief state updates: LastKnownTargetPosition + LastTimeTargetPositionChanged. Target identity is deliberately split into CurrentSeenTarget, PreviousTarget, PreviousTargetActual and _hasVisuallySeenPreviousTarget (bool) — the bot distinguishes 'told about' from 'actually saw'.
findings.members: EyesAI.FindTarget, EyesAI.ScoreTarget(Transform,float), EyesAI.FindClosestsTarget, BrainAI.CurrentSeenTarget, BrainAI.PreviousTargetActual, BrainAI._hasVisuallySeenPreviousTarget, BrainAI.LastKnownTargetPosition
findings.modding: ScoreTarget is the single lever for threat prioritisation — e.g. make bots prefer the loudest or nearest-to-objective player.

findings.title: STEP 28 — Hearing is fed by two STATIC hooks plus a global gunshot broadcaster
findings.detail: Any system in the game can feed the AI's ears through two static entry points: EyesAI.FootstepPlayed(UnityEngine.Vector3 footstepPosition, UnityEngine.GameObject shooterRoot, UnityEngine.Transform lookPosition) and EyesAI.DoorSoundPlayed(UnityEngine.Vector3 doorPosition, float hearingRadius). Gunfire goes through GameManager.ShotFired(UnityEngine.Vector3 shotPosition, float hearingRadius, uint shooterID, bool shooterInInterior), which drives the pooled Il2Cpp.Gunshot propagator (static Get(GameObject gunshotPrefab, Vector3, Quaternion) -> Gunshot / Return(Gunshot), Initialize(), FixedUpdate(), carrying Shooter, ShooterBrain, ShooterTeam and FlatDistance/MediumDistance/FarDistance/MaxDistance tiers). Per-bot reaction entry points on the brain: HeardTarget(Vector3 position, float _distance, Transform _target), ReactToGunFire(Vector3 shooterPosition, float _dis, bool shooterInInterior), ReactToBulletCrack(Vector3 shooterPosition, Vector3 bulletPosition, Vector3 bulletDirection), GetFlashed(float timer, Vector3 explosionLocation). Hearing is context-sensitive: HearingRange, IndoorHearingRange, IndoorGunshotHearingRange, CombatHearingMultiplier, YellTargetPositionRange, AI_MinimumCrackDistance.
findings.members: EyesAI.FootstepPlayed, EyesAI.DoorSoundPlayed, GameManager.ShotFired(Vector3,float,uint,bool), Gunshot.Get, Gunshot.ShooterBrain, BrainAI.HeardTarget, BrainAI.ReactToGunFire, BrainAI.ReactToBulletCrack, BrainAI.GetFlashed
findings.modding: A custom noise source only needs to call the two static EyesAI methods to be heard — no per-bot registration. Conversely a weapon that skips GameManager.ShotFired is completely inaudible to AI regardless of its actual audio.

findings.title: STEP 29 — Comms: EyesAI.TryComms → BrainAI.CalledBackup stages a DELAYED response
findings.detail: EyesAI.TryComms(Il2Cpp.BrainAI friendlyBrain), rate-limited by CommsCooldown/_lastCommsTime, calls BrainAI.CalledBackup(Vector3 position, Transform comrade, Transform Target). That does NOT act immediately — it stages _pendingCommsResponse (bool), _pendingCommsPosition, _pendingCommsComrade, _pendingCommsTarget and starts _commsDelayTimer toward _commsDelayTarget rolled between CommsDelayMin and CommsDelayMax. BrainAI.ProcessPendingComms(float dt) later fires BrainAI.ExecuteBackupResponse(Vector3 position, Transform comrade, Transform Target). Gated by useComms and CanCallBackup; the informed position is stored on the separate memory channel LastCommsTargetPosition with LastTimeCommsTargetPositionChanged, and AlertedByCommsTimer/backupCaller track it.
findings.members: EyesAI.TryComms(BrainAI), BrainAI.CalledBackup, BrainAI.ProcessPendingComms(float), BrainAI.ExecuteBackupResponse, BrainAI.CommsDelayMin, BrainAI._pendingCommsResponse, BrainAI.AlertedByCommsTimer, BrainAI.LastCommsTargetPosition
findings.modding: Patch CalledBackup for the callout, ExecuteBackupResponse for the reaction. Zeroing CommsDelayMin/Max makes a squad react as one organism — a cheap difficulty knob.

findings.title: STEP 30 — Bot memory is four independent position channels with independent timestamps
findings.detail: BrainAI keeps LastKnownTargetPosition, LastHeardTargetPosition, LastCommsTargetPosition and LastSuppressTargetPosition as separate properties over separate backing fields (_lastKnownTargetPosition, _lastHeardTargetPosition, _lastCommmsTargetPosition [sic, triple m], _lastSuppressTargetPosition), each paired with LastTimeTargetPositionChanged / LastTimeHeardTargetPositionChanged / LastTimeCommsTargetPositionChanged / LastTimeSuppressTargetChanged. Forgetting is governed by ForgetTime/forgetTimer and Patience.
findings.members: BrainAI.LastKnownTargetPosition, BrainAI.LastHeardTargetPosition, BrainAI.LastCommsTargetPosition, BrainAI.LastSuppressTargetPosition, BrainAI.ForgetTime, BrainAI.forgetTimer, BrainAI.Patience
findings.modding: This is a real sensor-fusion memory model. Reading all four channels plus timestamps gives an accurate picture of what a bot believes and how it learned it — the basis of a good debug overlay.

findings.title: STEP 31 — Alert gating: reactionTimer / TimeToContact / ShouldBeInCombat() before any transition
findings.detail: Between detection and reaction sit BrainAI.reactionTimer (against ReactionTime / _baseReactionTime), TimeToContact and TimeToContactMultiplier, _combatTimer, AlertedByCommsTimer, and BrainAI.UpdateFlashedAndDetection(float dt) with isFlashed/flashedTimer. Entry into combat is gated by two predicates: BrainAI.ShouldBeInCombat() -> bool and BrainAI.ShouldBeInCombatReady() -> bool, evaluated inside UpdateStanceAndCombatState(). BotSpawnDetails.DetectionTimeMultiplier is the per-spawn-point scalar on this ramp.
findings.members: BrainAI.ShouldBeInCombat, BrainAI.ShouldBeInCombatReady, BrainAI.reactionTimer, BrainAI.ReactionTime, BrainAI.TimeToContactMultiplier, BrainAI.UpdateFlashedAndDetection, BotSpawnDetails.DetectionTimeMultiplier
findings.modding: ShouldBeInCombat/ShouldBeInCombatReady are the two clean booleans to patch for 'bots that never engage' or 'bots always alert' without touching perception.

findings.title: STEP 32 — The FSM is only six states, and BrainAI.SetNewAiState(States) is the single funnel
findings.detail: BrainAI/States = {Idle, TargetSighted, WasSighted, FallBack, Suppress, Evade} — that is the whole machine. BrainAI.UpdateStateMachine(float dt) dispatches to Idle(), TargetSighted(float dt), WasSighted(float dt), FallBack(float dt), Suppress(float dt), Evade(). Attack(bool suppressing), Chase(), CautiousAdvance(), Patrol(float dt) and Wander(float dt) are METHODS invoked from inside those states, not states themselves. Sub-modes are orthogonal enums: BrainAI/IdleStates {Idle, Wander, Patrol, Random}, BrainAI/ReactType {Defensive, Offensive, Random}, BrainAI/Stance {Stand, Crouch, Prone}, BrainAI/PeekState {None, InCover, PeekingOut, Returning}. WasSighted is the search-after-losing-contact state, bounded by _searchSweepCount / MAX_SEARCH_SWEEPS. BrainAI.CurrentState is the readable getter.
findings.members: BrainAI/States, BrainAI.SetNewAiState(States), BrainAI.UpdateStateMachine(float), BrainAI.CurrentState, BrainAI.MAX_SEARCH_SWEEPS, BrainAI/IdleStates, BrainAI/ReactType
findings.modding: Harmony-patch SetNewAiState(States) for a complete, low-noise transition log — it is the only funnel. A actually new state means patching UpdateStateMachine's dispatch, since the enum is baked into il2cpp.

findings.title: STEP 33 — Idle sub-behaviour: BrainAI.Patrol(float dt) over AIPatrol, BrainAI.Wander(float dt) over RandomNavSphere
findings.detail: BrainAI.idleStates (IdleStates) selects between Idle(), Wander(float dt) and Patrol(float dt). Patrol reads the data-only Il2Cpp.AIPatrol component (patrolPoints, currentWayPointIndex, Looping, patrolWaitTime, onReachDestination : AIPatrol/OnReachDestination {Wait, MoveImmediately}) — AIPatrol has no methods at all; BrainAI.Patrol drives it, with patrolTimer and PatrolSpeed. Wander uses BrainAI.RandomNavSphere(UnityEngine.Vector3 origin, float minRadius, float maxRadius) -> Vector3 (legacy NavMesh naming, now sampling the A* graph) bounded by WanderDistance/WanderTimer/wanderTime.
findings.members: BrainAI.Patrol(float), BrainAI.Wander(float), BrainAI.RandomNavSphere(Vector3,float,float), BrainAI.aiPatrol, AIPatrol/OnReachDestination, BrainAI.WanderDistance
findings.modding: Patrol routes are plain Transform lists on AIPatrol — trivially generated for a custom map at runtime.

findings.title: STEP 34 — Movement: BrainAI.CalculateDynamicSpeed(float baseSpeed) → AgentController.maxSpeed/destination → AgentController.CallUpdate()
findings.detail: CalculateDynamicSpeed composes base speeds (PatrolSpeed, TacticalCombatSpeed, FastCombatSpeed, ChaseSpeed, EvasionSpeed), multipliers (SpeedApproachMultiplier, SpeedSprintMultiplier), a chase ramp (ChaseAccelerationRate, _chaseSpeedBonus — bots accelerate the longer they pursue), smoothing (SpeedAcceleration, SpeedDeceleration, DirectionChangeRate, _smoothedDirection) and terrain via GetSlopeSpeedMultiplier() (SlopeUpSpeedMultiplier, SlopeDownSpeedMultiplier, MaxSlopeAngle, _cachedSlopeMultiplier gated by _slopeCheckTimer/SlopeCheckInterval so the slope ray is not per-frame). BrainAI.UpdateMovementRotation() and SyncAgentAndAnimator() bridge to the agent and animator; BrainAI.HasReached() -> bool and SetAgentAngularSpeed(float) complete the facade; UpdateStuckDetection(float dt) watches _stuckCheckPos/_stuckTimer against STUCK_CHECK_INTERVAL/STUCK_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD.
findings.members: BrainAI.CalculateDynamicSpeed(float), BrainAI.GetSlopeSpeedMultiplier, BrainAI._chaseSpeedBonus, BrainAI.HasReached, BrainAI.SyncAgentAndAnimator, AgentController.CallUpdate, AgentController.destination, BrainAI.UpdateStuckDetection
findings.modding: Writing AgentController.maxSpeed directly gets overwritten every tick by CalculateDynamicSpeed — patch that method or the base speed fields instead.

findings.title: STEP 35 — Cover is generated on demand: BrainAI.FindNewCover → DynamicCoverFinder, with a frame budget and a reservation system
findings.detail: BrainAI.FindNewCover(UnityEngine.Vector3 targetPosition) calls into the Il2Cpp.DynamicCoverFinder singleton: TryAcquireQuerySlot() -> bool (hard per-frame budget via maxQueriesPerFrame/_queriesThisFrame/_lastBudgetFrame) → GenerateSamplePoints(Vector3 origin, Vector3 threat, float maxDist) -> int (ring sampling with sampleDensity, maxSamplePoints, maxPointsPerRing, minCoverHeight, maxCoverHeight, obstacleMask, groundMask, Burst-batched over _cmds NativeArray<RaycastCommand> / _results NativeArray<RaycastHit> with EnsureScratch(int n)) → DynamicCoverPoint.Score(Vector3 evaluatorPos, Vector3 threatPos, bool losBlocked, float losHitDist) -> float → FindBestDynamicCover(Vector3 searcherPos, Vector3 threatPos, float maxDist) -> DynamicCoverPoint. Anti-clumping: RegisterCoverPosition(Vector3) / UnregisterCoverPosition(Vector3) / IsTooCloseToActiveCover(Vector3) over _activeCoverPositions with MinCoverSeparation. Points are pooled by Rent()/Return(DynamicCoverPoint). There are NO baked cover volumes. (Il2Cpp.CoveringController is an unrelated snow/dust material driver — pure name collision.)
findings.members: BrainAI.FindNewCover(Vector3), BrainAI.ReleaseCover, BrainAI._currentCover, BrainAI.coverQueryCooldown, DynamicCoverFinder.TryAcquireQuerySlot, DynamicCoverFinder.FindBestDynamicCover, DynamicCoverFinder.IsTooCloseToActiveCover, DynamicCoverFinder.MinCoverSeparation, DynamicCoverPoint.Score
findings.modding: Custom maps need no cover authoring — cover emerges from colliders on obstacleMask. Raising maxQueriesPerFrame is the direct fix if bots feel slow to take cover. Forgetting to ReleaseCover leaks a reservation and blocks that spot for everyone permanently.

findings.title: STEP 36 — Peeking is a real four-state sub-machine on top of the cover point
findings.detail: DynamicCoverPoint exposes four derived firing poses — GetStandPosition(), GetCrouchPosition(), GetPeekLeft(), GetPeekRight() — over position, forward, coverNormal, coverHeight, wallHitPoint. BrainAI.UpdateCoverPeek(float dt) -> bool drives _peekState (BrainAI/PeekState {None, InCover, PeekingOut, Returning}) using PeekChance ('Chance to peek from cover instead of leaving it'), PeekExposureTime, PeekCoverTime, PeekBurstsBeforeReposition, _peekTimer, _peekCount, _peekPosition, _coverReturnPosition. Cover is re-evaluated when the threat moves away from _coverThreatPosWhenChosen, throttled by coverQueryCooldown/_lastCoverQueryTime and held for coverTime/coverTimer.
findings.members: BrainAI.UpdateCoverPeek(float), BrainAI._peekState, BrainAI.PeekChance, BrainAI.PeekBurstsBeforeReposition, BrainAI._coverThreatPosWhenChosen, DynamicCoverPoint.GetPeekLeft, DynamicCoverPoint.GetPeekRight
findings.modding: PeekBurstsBeforeReposition and PeekChance are the two fields that most change how 'sticky' bots feel in a firefight.

findings.title: STEP 37 — Manoeuvre: Chase / CautiousAdvance / TryProactiveFlank / FallBack, all behind TacticsChance
findings.detail: BrainAI.Chase() and BrainAI.CautiousAdvance() are the two approach modes. BrainAI.TryProactiveFlank() -> bool is governed by ProactiveFlankChance, FlankOffsetMin/FlankOffsetMax, FlankTriggerDistance, FlankCooldown/_flankCooldownTimer, _isActiveFlanking. Both flanking and grenades sit behind a single gate, BrainAI.TacticsChance ('Percent chance to use advanced tactics (flanking, grenades) per evaluation'). Retreat is a first-class state: FallBack(float dt) with _fallBackTimer, informed by BrainAI.UpdateTeamConfidence(float dt) → teamConfidence over TEAM_AWARENESS_RADIUS, fed by cached rosters allFriendlyBrains / allEnemyBrains / allEnemyPlayers. ReactType.Defensive bots hold a post at DefensiveInitialPosition (Vector3) / DefensiveInitialRotation (Quaternion). Being flanked is detected separately by EyesAI.CheckFlanker(Vector3 flankerPos, float distance, Transform flankerTarget).
findings.members: BrainAI.Chase, BrainAI.CautiousAdvance, BrainAI.TryProactiveFlank, BrainAI.TacticsChance, BrainAI.FallBack(float), BrainAI.UpdateTeamConfidence(float), BrainAI.teamConfidence, BrainAI.DefensiveInitialPosition, EyesAI.CheckFlanker
findings.modding: TacticsChance is a single scalar that turns the AI from static shooters into manoeuvring opponents — but it gates grenades too. teamConfidence is the most promising single value for a morale mod: read it across a squad while killing members and watch for FallBack via SetNewAiState.

findings.title: STEP 38 — Door traversal mid-path: OnTraverseOffMeshLink → kick RPC → ApplyKickForce
findings.detail: When a path crosses a door link, BotOffmeshLinkHandler's traversal coroutine advances OnOffLink → ReachedLink → OpeningDoor → (KickRequested → WaitingForKick → KickHappened) → TravelingLink → Finished. The kick is mirrored across four types: BrainAI.PlayKickAnimation() and NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.SERVER_PlayKickAnimation() -> RPC_PlayKickAnimation() -> ApplyKickForces(), with ApplyKickForce() and KickAnimationFinished() present on BrainAI, AgentController, BotOffmeshLinkHandler and NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC alike. Breach tuning lives on the handler: IsBreacher (bool), DoorKickDamageMin/DoorKickDamageMax/DoorKickForce, DoorCooldown, _doorCooldowns (Dictionary<Il2Cpp.DoorV2,float>).
findings.members: BotOffmeshLinkHandler.Pathfinding_IOffMeshLinkStateMachine_OnTraverseOffMeshLink, BrainAI.PlayKickAnimation, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.SERVER_PlayKickAnimation, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.RPC_PlayKickAnimation, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.ApplyKickForces, BotOffmeshLinkHandler.IsBreacher
findings.modding: Custom maps need DoorV2s wired as A* off-mesh links or bots path around/into them. Set IsBreacher per bot for kick-capable units.

findings.title: STEP 39 — Aiming: BrainAI.UpdateAccuracyAndSnap + a deliberate miss offset (the AI does NOT roll to hit)
findings.detail: BrainAI.UpdateAccuracyAndSnap(float dt) drives BrainAI.GenerateNearMissOffset(float dt) -> UnityEngine.Vector3 and GetDifficultyKillShotOffset() -> UnityEngine.Vector3, whose result becomes an aimOffset applied to IK_AIMING_TARGET / AimingTargetTransform, refreshed on nearMissUpdateTime/nearMissUpdateTimer. There is no hit roll anywhere — the bot fires real projectiles at a deliberately displaced aimpoint. Tunables: baseHitChance, difficultyAccuracy, maxEffectiveRangeFalloff, WeaponInaccuracy, WeaponInaccuracyDistance, AimSnap/MinAimSnap/BaseAimSnap, AimCentreMass (bool), SkillRandomness, TurnSpeed/turnSpeedMultiplier. BrainAI.LookAtTarget(Vector3 position, bool requireTarget, bool flatY, bool speed0) is the look primitive, feeding AiRotationController.SetAiLookAtTarget(Vector3)/SetBotRotationTarget(Quaternion)/Tick(float dt) and finally BotAimCorrection.RotateParentToMakeChildLookAt(Transform parent, Transform child, Vector3 targetPosition) in LateUpdate — animation drives the pose, then the arm parent is rotated so the real muzzle transform lands on target.
findings.members: BrainAI.UpdateAccuracyAndSnap(float), BrainAI.GenerateNearMissOffset(float), BrainAI.GetDifficultyKillShotOffset, BrainAI.difficultyAccuracy, BrainAI.LookAtTarget, AiRotationController.SetAiLookAtTarget, BotAimCorrection.RotateParentToMakeChildLookAt, BotAimCorrection.CheckWeaponCollision
findings.modding: Two functions control ALL AI lethality — patch GenerateNearMissOffset and GetDifficultyKillShotOffset to retune difficulty without touching damage, health or the FSM. Custom bot weapons need a correctly oriented muzzle child transform and a SimpleWeaponCollision or bots visibly aim off-target and clip guns through walls.

findings.title: STEP 40 — Firing: BrainAI.Attack(bool suppressing) → WeaponsAI.SERVER_SetFireBool → RPC_SetFireBool → SERVER_SendBullet → RPC_SendBullet → PuppetWeapon.SpawnBullet
findings.detail: BrainAI.Attack(bool suppressing) pulls the trigger through WeaponsAI.SERVER_SetFireBool(bool state) -> RPC_SetFireBool(bool state, int _currentBurst). WeaponsAI (which DOES have its own Update() and FixedUpdate()) then runs the burst clock — fireWeapon, currentBurst, fired_Burst, timeBetweenBursts/init_timeBetweenBursts, _fireTimer — and emits rounds via SERVER_SendBullet(Vector3 _muzzlePos, Quaternion _muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread) -> RPC_SendBullet(same three args), landing on PuppetWeapon.Fire() / PuppetWeapon.SpawnBullet(Vector3 _muzzlePosition, Quaternion _muzzleRotation, Vector3 _moaSpread, bool _isOwned) and thence Bullet.SpawnBullet -> BulletInstance in the BulletManager pool. Reload: SERVER_Reload() -> RPC_Reload() -> ReloadWeapon() on reloadTime/isReloading. Note the asymmetry: AI firing is SERVER-authoritative (only UserCode_RPC_SendBullet exists, no UserCode_CMD_) whereas player firing is client-authoritative through WeaponV3's CMD_->RPC_. Perf: WeaponsAI.IK_RangeCheck() disables ikBehaviours and the FinalIK LeftArmIK/RightArmIK beyond maxIKdistance using _sqrDistanceToCamera.
findings.members: BrainAI.Attack(bool), WeaponsAI.SERVER_SetFireBool(bool), WeaponsAI.RPC_SetFireBool(bool,int), WeaponsAI.SERVER_SendBullet, WeaponsAI.RPC_SendBullet, PuppetWeapon.SpawnBullet, WeaponsAI.SERVER_Reload, WeaponsAI.IK_RangeCheck
findings.modding: Bots fire real simulated projectiles through the same ballistics pipeline as players — armour, penetration and drag all apply. A damage mod aimed at players will affect bots identically at the bullet layer.

findings.title: STEP 41 — Suppression is bidirectional, squad-coordinated and GLOBALLY CAPPED
findings.detail: Outgoing: BrainAI.Suppress(float dt), UpdateSuppressionTarget(float dt), AssignSuppressionSector() (squad members divide a sector), SuppressLOSBlocked(Vector3 suppressPoint) -> bool, with SuppressionLeadFactor, SuppressionIntelInterval/_suppressionIntelTimer, _targetVelocityEstimate, _prevSuppressionTargetPos, _baseSuppressPosition, SuppressRange, SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters, _suppressDuration. Throttled globally by GameManager.allAIActiveSuppressing (List<BrainAI>) capped at GameManager.MaxActiveSuppressionAI. Counter-fire is a separate sub-system: doesCounterFire, counterFireChance, coverInsteadOfCounterFireChance, counterFireShotsMin/Max, _counterFireThreshold, _counterFireShotCount, counterFireDuration, counterFireSpread, _isCounterFiring, _counterFireTimer, _counterFireTarget, doesReactionarySuppression. Incoming: underFire, UnderFireTimer/UnderFireTime, suppressionResistance, BrainAI.UpdateSuppressionAndEvadeLogic(), Evade()/evadeTimer/evadeTime/EvasionSpeed.
findings.members: BrainAI.Suppress(float), BrainAI.AssignSuppressionSector, BrainAI.SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters, BrainAI.suppressionResistance, BrainAI.Evade, GameManager.allAIActiveSuppressing, GameManager.MaxActiveSuppressionAI
findings.modding: MaxActiveSuppressionAI is a hard global cap — raising bot counts without raising it means most of the squad never suppresses. SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters is why bots shoot slightly through cover edges.

findings.title: STEP 42 — Grenades: BrainAI.EvaluateGrenadeUse(float dt) → WeaponsAI.CanThrowGrenade → SERVER_ThrowGrenade
findings.detail: BrainAI.EvaluateGrenadeUse(float dt) runs on GrenadeEvaluationInterval/_grenadeEvalTimer behind TacticsChance, and calls WeaponsAI.CanThrowGrenade(UnityEngine.Vector3 targetPos) -> bool then WeaponsAI.SERVER_ThrowGrenade(UnityEngine.Vector3 targetPos, bool useFlashbang). Inventory is replicated: grenadesRemaining and flashbangsRemaining are SyncVars. Ballistics and animation timing are separate concerns: grenadeMinDistance/grenadeMaxDistance/grenadeThrowChance/grenadeCooldown/_grenadeCooldownTimer, grenadeThrowForceMin/Max, grenadeLaunchSpeed, grenadeThrowAnimation (string), grenadeThrowAnimBlend, grenadeWindUpDelay, grenadeReleaseDelay, _isThrowingGrenade.
findings.members: BrainAI.EvaluateGrenadeUse(float), WeaponsAI.CanThrowGrenade(Vector3), WeaponsAI.SERVER_ThrowGrenade(Vector3,bool), WeaponsAI.grenadesRemaining (SyncVar), WeaponsAI.grenadeReleaseDelay, BrainAI.TacticsChance
findings.modding: grenadeReleaseDelay is when the projectile actually leaves the hand relative to the animation — mismatch it and grenades spawn inside the bot.

findings.title: STEP 43 — Suicide bombers: BrainAI's only two weaved RPCs
findings.detail: BrainAI.isSuicideBomber gates a complete pipeline: SERVER_ActivateBomber() -> RPC_BomberActivated() (audible cue via bomberActivationSFX/bomberAudioSource), fuse over bomberFuseTime/_bomberFuseTimer/_bomberFuseStarted, detonation at bomberDetonationRange via SERVER_BomberExplode() -> RPC_BomberExplode(UnityEngine.Vector3 position), damage resolved with _bomberOverlapBuffer (Collider[]) over bomberExplosionRadius/bomberExplosionDamage, and bomberDeathExplodeChance — a probability the vest cooks off when the bot is KILLED rather than reaching its target. These are the ONLY weaved RPCs on BrainAI (UserCode_RPC_BomberActivated, UserCode_RPC_BomberExplode__Vector3): no state, target or cover decision is ever replicated.
findings.members: BrainAI.isSuicideBomber, BrainAI.SERVER_ActivateBomber, BrainAI.RPC_BomberActivated, BrainAI.SERVER_BomberExplode, BrainAI.RPC_BomberExplode(Vector3), BrainAI.bomberDeathExplodeChance, BrainAI._bomberOverlapBuffer
findings.modding: Setting isSuicideBomber on any standard bot prefab should work without a special archetype — all the tuning lives on BrainAI itself.

findings.title: STEP 44 — Only PRESENTATION crosses the wire: NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC SyncVars, clients re-simulate the rest
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC (Start/Update/SyncAnimator/SyncAnimatorBooleans) carries the entire bot presentation state as hooked SyncVars: SpeedXTarget, SpeedYTarget, agentVelocity (Vector3), aimTargetPosition (Vector3), CurrentRotation (OnCurrentRotationChanged), isCrouching (OnCrouchUpdate), isProne (OnProneUpdate), inCombat (OnCombatUpdate), inCombatReady (OnCombatReadyUpdate), isArmed (OnArmedUpdate), InInteriorCollider/InOpenInteriorCollider (OnInInteriorColliderUpdate), plus StartTurnInPlaceAnimation(bool isLeft). Clients then locally re-run AiAnimationController (hash-cached, dirty-gated by SPEED_DIRTY_THRESHOLD), AiRotationController (which has an explicit ClientSideLogic()) and BotAimCorrection. Send rate is tuned globally on GameManager: botTransformSyncRate, botSendThreshold, SetBotSendThreshold(float), disableFixedBotSendRate, ToggleFixedBotSendRate().
findings.members: NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.SyncAnimator, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.aimTargetPosition, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.OnCombatReadyUpdate, AiRotationController.ClientSideLogic, AiAnimationController.SPEED_DIRTY_THRESHOLD, GameManager.botSendThreshold
findings.modding: A client-side mod can NEVER read a bot's state, target or cover — only these animator SyncVars. Any AI-behaviour mod must run on the host. Hook the UserCode_* receive side for client-visible reactions.

findings.title: STEP 45 — Reinforcement, timed path: RaidManager.Update() → CheckIfCanSendReinforcementsTimed() ← AI_BackupCondition()
findings.detail: RaidManager.Update() drives CheckIfCanSendReinforcementsTimed(), gated by hasReinforcements (bool), timedBackup (bool) and reinforcementMinMaxTimer (Vector2), with the population predicate RaidManager.AI_BackupCondition() -> bool reading minAIBackupAmount against the live count maintained by RaidManager.UpdateAICount(). The count is published to clients by SERVER_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int amount) -> RPC_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int amount), with hasNotified/hasNotifiedEnemiesDead as one-shot latches.

findings.modding: UpdateAICount is the count the whole reinforcement and 'enemies dead' logic reads — patch it and both the HUD number and wave triggers follow.

findings.title: STEP 46 — Reinforcement, trigger path: ReinforcementTrigger.OnTriggerEnter → aiReinforcement.CMD_StartReinforcement → RPC_StartReinforcement → SpawnBots()
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ReinforcementTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(UnityEngine.Collider other) is a volume the player walks into; it fires Il2Cpp.aiReinforcement.CMD_StartReinforcement() -> RPC_StartReinforcement() (both actually weaved — UserCode_CMD_StartReinforcement and UserCode_RPC_StartReinforcement both exist), which plays the vehicle arrival via animator and then calls aiReinforcement.SpawnBots() over Bots (GameObject[]) at Spawns (GameObject[]), enabling gameObjectsToEnable and latching activated. The vehicle carries vehicleHealth (Il2Cpp.VehicleHealth). TRAP: aiReinforcement.CMDSpawnTargets() has NO UserCode_ twin and is a plain local call despite the name.

findings.modding: Destroying the reinforcement vehicle (it has VehicleHealth) is a plausible way to cancel a wave. Custom maps get reinforcements by placing an aiReinforcement vehicle plus a ReinforcementTrigger volume.

findings.title: STEP 47 — Reinforcement, mod path: SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string) → RespawnCustomAI() → ServerSpawnAI(true)
findings.detail: RaidManager exposes a string-keyed, server-side custom spawn API: SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string botName), SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_RemoveAll(), RespawnCustomAI(), RespawnAI(). The name resolves against the registry pair GameManager.allAITypes_s (Il2CppStringArray) and GameManager.AllAITypes (List<GameObject>), populating RaidManager.customAI (List<GameObject>) which ServerSpawnAI(true) then consumes. WaveSurvival has its own parallel wave source (survivalWaves / survivalWaveEntries unified by GetWave(int) -> ResolvedWave) with per-wave difficulty and EnemiesMinMaxSpawnCount.

findings.modding: This is the intended path for custom enemies — register the name into allAITypes_s/AllAITypes, call AddAI, call RespawnCustomAI. No prefab patching of the spawner needed. WaveSurvival.survivalWaveEntries can be appended at runtime without touching the scene.

findings.title: STEP 48 — Incoming damage on a bot uses a DIFFERENT entry point from players: Health.ProcessAIDamage
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Health.ProcessAIDamage(Il2CppFIMSpace.FProceduralAnimation.RagdollAnimator2BoneIndicator indic, int hitboxIndex, UnityEngine.RaycastHit _hit, float _damage, int shooterID, float _bleedChance, float _bleedDamage) bypasses the HealthBodyPart enum entirely and works off a ragdoll bone indicator plus an integer hitbox index resolved by Health.GetHitboxIndex(string). Players instead go through CMDTakeDamage(float, HealthBodyPart, HealthBodyPart crossedDamage, int shooterID). shooterID is a plain int netId threaded from BulletInstance.shootersNetworkID — that is the kill-attribution channel.
findings.members: Health.ProcessAIDamage, Health.GetHitboxIndex(string), Health.CMDTakeDamage, Health.ProcessCrossDamage, BulletInstance.shootersNetworkID
findings.modding: A damage mod that only patches CMDTakeDamage without warning misses every AI hit. You must patch ProcessAIDamage too.

findings.title: STEP 49 — Hit reaction and suppression feedback before death
findings.detail: Health.CMDProcessAIAnimation(int hitboxIndex, UnityEngine.Vector3 direction) -> RPCProcessAIAnimation() plays the reaction, selecting a clip NAME from V2AIParametres.HitReactionsBody (string[]). In parallel the brain registers incoming fire: underFire, UnderFireTimer/UnderFireTime, suppressionResistance, and may respond via doesCounterFire / coverInsteadOfCounterFireChance / Evade(). Bleeding and fractures are separate replicated channels: CMD_Bleed(HealthBodyPart, float _damage, int shooterID), CMD_Fracture(HealthBodyPart, int shooterID) -> RPC_Fractured, with per-limb SyncVars NetworkBleedingDamage_Head/Chest/Stomach/LArm/RArm/LLeg/RLeg.
findings.members: Health.CMDProcessAIAnimation(int,Vector3), Health.RPCProcessAIAnimation, V2AIParametres.HitReactionsBody, BrainAI.underFire, BrainAI.suppressionResistance, Health.CMD_Bleed, Health.CMD_Fracture
findings.modding: Hit-reaction clips are string state names on V2AIParametres — new reactions only need matching Animator state names, no code.

findings.title: STEP 50 — Death: Health.CheckDeath() → Health.Die(HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath, int shooterID) → ProcessDeathServer()
findings.detail: Health.CheckDeath() (guarded by the deadChecked int latch) leads to Health.Die(Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath, int shooterID) — a weaved RPC (UserCode_Die__HealthBodyPart__Int32) — which runs ProcessDeathServer() and SpawnBloodPool(HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath), sets the isDead SyncVar and records Health.MyCauseOfDeath. The cause of death selects the death animation from V2AIParametres' per-limb string arrays: DeathHeadClips, DeathNeckClips, DeathChestClips, DeathStomachClips, DeathBackClips, DeathLArmClips, DeathRArmClips, DeathLLegClips, DeathRLegClips — plus IncapacitatedBackClips/IncapacitatedChestClips/IncapacitatedStomachClips, evidence of a downed-but-not-dead state that exists for only three body regions.

findings.modding: Health.Die is the single choke point for 'a bot died' on the server. New death animations only need matching Animator state names in the V2AIParametres clip arrays.

findings.title: STEP 51 — Ragdoll handoff is FIMSpace Ragdoll Animator 2, and the corpse stays shootable
findings.detail: Death hands the body to Il2CppFIMSpace.FProceduralAnimation.RagdollAnimator2 (V2AIParametres.Ragdoll, FallImpactPower, Force : UnityEngine.ForceMode, Sleep) — not PuppetMaster. Health drives it with PerformRagdollAction(), AddVelocityToRagdoll(), ForceDeathPose(), SERVER_RagdollPlayAnimation(string animName, float blendtime) -> RPC_RagdollPlayAnimation, SetRagdollToSleep(float delay, bool headshot) and a family of blend coroutines (SmoothChangeRagdollBlend, SmoothChangeSpringsValueOnFall, SmoothChangeMuscleDampingOnFall, SmoothChangeLimbValueOnFall(int chainIndex,...), SmoothChangeConnectedMassValueOnFall, SmoothChangeLimbForceValueOnFall(..., ERagdollBoneID), SmoothChangeMultipleLimbsForceOnFall(float, LimbForceEntry[]), SmoothChangeChainMassMultiplier(..., ERagdollChainType)). The corpse remains a damage target: RagdollHealth (SyncVar), SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth(), TakeRagdollDamage(float), RPC_RagdollBleedout(), ragdollBleedoutTime/ragdollBleedoutTimer, ragdollDead, ragdollDisableTime, and SmoothSyncMirror arrays activeRagdollSync/fullHealthSync swap the network sync mode.
findings.members: Health.PerformRagdollAction, Health.SetRagdollToSleep(float,bool), Health.SERVER_RagdollPlayAnimation, Health.RagdollHealth (SyncVar), Health.TakeRagdollDamage, Health.RPC_RagdollBleedout, V2AIParametres.Ragdoll, Health.activeRagdollSync
findings.modding: GameManager.SetAIRagdollState(bool) and ToggleRagdollsStayOnAfterDeath() are the shipped switches. A downed bot can still be finished off — RagdollHealth is a second health pool with its own bleedout timer.

findings.title: STEP 52 — Target-pool cleanup: Health.RemoveTargetsOnDeathOrDestroy() is the de-registration seam
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Health.RemoveTargetsOnDeathOrDestroy() sits immediately before OnDestroy() in the method table and is the counterpart to TeamRuntimeData.AddTarget(Transform) / RemoveTarget(Transform) — it pulls the dead entity out of every team's target list so surviving bots stop scoring the corpse in EyesAI.ScoreTarget. TeamIdentifier.OnDestroy() correspondingly calls TeamManager.RemoveOperatorFromTeam(int teamID, TeamIdentifier). Health.AllAlivePlayers is a static HashSet<Health> maintained across the same lifecycle.

findings.modding: If you spawn a custom entity into the target pool, you must remove it here or every bot keeps aiming at a destroyed transform. This is the most likely source of a null-target hang in a custom-AI mod.

findings.title: STEP 53 — Brain shutdown: BrainAI.ReleaseCover(), scriptsDisableAfterLookFade, and the cover-reservation leak
findings.detail: On death the brain must call BrainAI.ReleaseCover() -> DynamicCoverFinder.UnregisterCoverPosition(Vector3), otherwise the reservation in _activeCoverPositions persists and IsTooCloseToActiveCover keeps that spot blocked for every other bot for the rest of the raid (MinCoverSeparation). Behaviour teardown is data-driven: V2AIParametres.scriptsDisableAfterLookFade (UnityEngine.Behaviour[]) and BotNetworking.scriptsToDisable (Behaviour[]) are the manifests of what gets switched off. BrainAI.OnKill() -> Il2CppSystem.Collections.IEnumerator exists but its subject is ambiguous from the signature — whether it fires on this bot killing something or on this bot being killed cannot be settled statically.

findings.modding: Runtime probe: log DynamicCoverFinder._activeCoverPositions.Count across a firefight. If it only grows, ReleaseCover is not running on death and that is a real bug worth patching around.

findings.title: STEP 54 — Kill attribution and objective bookkeeping
findings.detail: Per-player scoring: PlayerMaster.AddBotKill() with the replicated row playerBoardItem.Kills (ushort SyncVar, hook OnKillsChanged). Mission stats: OperationsManager.AddKill() bumping the TotalKills SyncVar. HVTs take an extra step — Health.hvtConfirmedDead (SyncVar) plus a client-asserted body confirm through RaidManager.CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, uint hvtID) -> RPC_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, int remaining), setting OperationsManager.HVTdead and playerBoardItem.HVTKilled. In WaveSurvival the death instead routes to SERVER_OnEnemyDeath/OnEnemyDeath -> RPC_AlertEnemyCount(int) against the enemysAlive SyncVar.

findings.modding: CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA takes a fully client-supplied name and netId — hook UserCode_CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA__String__UInt32 on the server to gate it. Whether the server re-validates hvtID against OperationsManager.AI_HVTs is unprovable from signatures and needs a runtime probe.

findings.title: STEP 55 — Population bookkeeping closes the loop back to reinforcement and mission end
findings.detail: After each death RaidManager.UpdateAICount() recomputes the live count, publishes it via SERVER_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int) -> RPC_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int), and sets hasNotifiedEnemiesDead when the map is clear. That same count feeds AI_BackupCondition() (STEP 45), so kills directly gate reinforcement waves. Mission outcome is decided elsewhere entirely: GameManagerNetwork.CompleteOperation() / SERVER_FailOperation() -> RPC_FailOperation(), with CheckAchievements()/CheckTier1Challenge()/CheckTier1NightChallenge() reading OperationsManager.TotalBots, TotalKills, WasNight and EffectiveHasCheated.

findings.modding: EffectiveHasCheated is a computed getter over the HasCheated SyncVar and DevCheatBypass — patching the getter is the clean way to keep achievements while modding.

findings.title: STEP 56 — Final destruction: BrainAI.OnDestroy() unregisters from every scheduler roster
findings.detail: BrainAI.OnDestroy() is the last step, removing the bot from GameManager.allAI (List<BrainAI>), the static BrainAI.AllBrainAI HashSet, GameManager._priorityBrainUpdates and GameManager.allAIActiveSuppressing; Health.OnDestroy() and TeamIdentifier.OnDestroy() do the same for GameManager.allBotHealth and TeamManager. The manual equivalents shipped for debugging are GameManager.DebugDestroyAllAi() and DebugDestroyAllAiNonCheat() (the latter presumably skipping the HasCheated flag), plus GetAICount() and Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState().

findings.modding: Use the shipped QFSW Quantum Console commands before writing instrumentation — Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState, GetAICount, SetAIAgentsState(false) and SetAI_UpdateIntervals(int) cover most of what an AI mod needs to observe.

findings.title: STEP 0 — Process start: 52 [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod] static resetters run before any scene
findings.detail: 52 types across Assembly-CSharp declare a private static parameterless `OnLoad()` with no Unity lifecycle role — the IL2CPP signature of `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod]`. Every singleton on the boot-to-mission path has one: GameManager.OnLoad, GameManagerNetwork.OnLoad, NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnLoad, OperationsManager.OnLoad, PlayerMaster.OnLoad, GameMode.OnLoad, InfiltrationManager.OnLoad, MissionLaptopNetworkState.OnLoad, InfilSelectorDisplayer.OnLoad, RaidManager.OnLoad, TeamManager.OnLoad, PoolInitializer.OnLoad, ObjectPooler.OnLoad, LoadoutManager.OnLoad, MenuControllerV2.OnLoad, OfflineMenuController.OnLoad, PlayMenu.OnLoad, InputLayer.OnLoad, HelicopterV3.OnLoad, playerBoardItem.OnLoad, Il2CppVectorGames.SteamLobby.OnLoad. These are static-field nullers — this is the earliest point a mod can run alongside game code. No authority concept yet; this is pre-network.

findings.modding: Harmony-postfix any of these to seize control before the first Awake in the build. GameManager.OnLoad / NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnLoad are the two that fire before every other subsystem exists, so they are the safest place to install a mod's own singleton.

findings.title: STEP 1 — ApplicationSplashScreen.Start -> StartLoading -> Update -> Load: shader warm, RAM/HDD gate, safe-mode prompt
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.ApplicationSplashScreen` is the first scene's controller. `Start()` -> `StartLoading()` (with a lambda `_StartLoading_b__11_0`) prewarms `allShaderVariantsCollection` (ShaderVariantCollection) while showing `WarmingIndicator` / `LoadingAnimation` / `splashScreenImages` (GameObject[]); `Update()` polls; `Load()` performs the actual scene switch. It carries a real hardware gate: `HalfResRamLimit` (int) forces half-res textures under a RAM threshold, `HDD_Warning` (GameObject) warns on spinning disk, and `SafeMode_Option` + `LoadFromSafeMode()` / `DontLoadFromSafeMode()` offer a reduced-settings boot. `cancelLaunch` (bool) plus `ErrorMessage` / `errorCode` (TextMeshProUGUI) abort the launch. Purely local — no network exists yet.

findings.modding: `ApplicationSplashScreen.Load` is the single choke point for 'game has finished booting, menu is about to load'. Patch `cancelLaunch` or `Load` if a mod needs to inject before the menu scene. Shader prewarm here is why runtime-loaded AssetBundle materials lose their shader binding — the variant collection is fixed at this moment.

findings.title: STEP 2 — Persistent-singleton boot: SteamManager, ForceInitSteamTransport, SaveManager migrations, InputLayer binds, PlayMenu settings
findings.detail: Before the menu is interactive: `Il2Cpp.SteamManager` (Instance/Initialized/ForceEarlyInit) brings up Steamworks; `Il2Cpp.ForceInitSteamTransport.Initialize()` -> `InitSteamTransport()` forces the FizzySteamworks transport awake (it exists precisely because Mirror's transport Awake ordering is unreliable); `Il2Cpp.SaveManager.Initialize()` + `MigrateToSavesDirectory()` / `MigrateRootFilesToSlot0()` and `Il2Cpp.PlayerPrefsMigration.MigrateAll()` / `Il2Cpp.WeaponPresetMigration.MigrateAll()` bring ES3 storage up to Version2; `Il2Cpp.InputLayer.LoadKeyBinds()` + `ConfigureAllBindTypes()` restores binds from KeyBinds.es3; `Il2Cpp.PlayMenu.get_singleton()` applies the ~40 Key_* graphics/audio settings; `Il2Cpp.PoolInitializer.Awake()` -> `InitPools()` builds the decal/VFX/bullet pools. `Il2Cpp.MenuControllerDDOL` is the DontDestroyOnLoad holder that survives every subsequent scene change.

findings.modding: A mod's own persistent settings should ride SaveManager.SetInt/SetFloat with a namespaced key + FlushDirtyFiles(). PoolInitializer.InitPools is the last moment to register a custom pooled prefab cheaply — after this, ObjectPooler.TryInitializePool must be called manually.

findings.title: STEP 3 — Main menu scene: MenuControllerV2.Start -> Init, SteamLobby.Awake/Start, NetworkManagerVectorGames.Awake
findings.detail: The menu shell is `Il2Cpp.MenuControllerV2` (SHIFT-styled: `mainPanelManager` -> Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.MainPanelManager). `Start()` -> `Init()` -> `setDefaults()` / `setPlayerPersonal()` / `addResolutions()` builds the panels and pulls the Steam persona; `Il2CppVectorGames.SteamLobby.Awake()/Start()` installs the Steam callbacks (`lobbyCreated`, `gameLobbyJoinRequested`, `lobbyEntered`, `lobbyMatchList`, `lobbyDataUpdate`) and runs `SetPreAlphaStatus()` plus the `Il2Cpp.SteamAuthID` HTTP allowlist check (`getData(url)` -> `passed()` / `failed()`). `NetworkManagerVectorGames.Awake()` establishes the Mirror singleton and DDOLs it. `Il2Cpp.MenuController` (v1) and `Il2Cpp.OfflineMenuController` are parallel variants; only one is live per scene. Server browser: `MenuControllerV2.refreshServerBrowser()` -> `SteamLobby.FindGame()` -> `BuildSearchKeys()` / `RequestNextSearch()` -> `OnLobbyMatchListReceived` -> `BuildLobbyListUI()` -> `SortJoinableLobbiesByPing()`.

findings.modding: MenuControllerV2 is the right main-menu target; MenuController (v1) is weaved but superseded and OfflineMenuController is a third variant. Confirm which is alive with one FindObjectsOfTypeAll sweep at scene load rather than assuming.

findings.title: STEP 4 (HOST-ONLY) — MenuControllerV2.startHost_Steam / startHost_SteamSolo / startHost_Offline -> transport pick -> SteamLobby.HostLobby
findings.detail: Three host entry points on `MenuControllerV2`: `startHost_Steam()`, `startHost_SteamSolo()` (reached via `LoneWolfUIButtonPressed()`), `startHost_Offline()` — all funnel through `startHost(bool transport)`. Transport selection is `NetworkManagerVectorGames.transportSteam()` (assigns the `Steam` Transport property = FizzySteamworks) or `TransportOffline()` (assigns `OfflineTransport`). Steam paths then call `SteamLobby.HostLobby()` or `HostLobbySolo()`. A fourth, non-Steam path ships in retail: `NetworkManagerVectorGames.startClientKCP()` + `ToggleConnectionMenu()` with Mirror's stock `managerHUD`. Host-only by definition — the client half of the menu is `refreshServerBrowser` -> `JoinLobby`.

findings.modding: startHost_Offline + TransportOffline is the whole solo path — a mod wanting a headless/LAN host can assign a KcpTransport into the `Steam` slot before startHost, or call startClientKCP() directly, with no Steam matchmaking involved.

findings.title: STEP 5 (HOST-ONLY) — SteamLobby.OnLobbyCreated writes lobby metadata; Mirror StartHost fires NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnStartServer
findings.detail: Steam's `LobbyCreated_t` callback lands in `SteamLobby.OnLobbyCreated(LobbyCreated_t)`, which publishes the searchable metadata via `SetLobbyData(key, value)` / `SetLobbyDataInt(CSteamID, key, int)` using the key fields `HostAddressKey`, `MapIDKey`, `LobbyDataKey`, `LobbyLocationKey`, plus `LobbyName`, `LobbyPassword`, `lobbyType`, and the time-bucketed browser key from `GetHostLobbyKey()`. `SetMaxConnections(int)` sets the cap and `PublishLobbyPlayerCountDetails()` keeps occupancy fresh. In parallel Mirror's StartHost drives `NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnStartServer()`, which is where `GameManagerNetworkPrefab` (the authoritative match-state object) is spawned, and `OnStartClient()` on the host's own client half.

findings.modding: SetLobbyData is the advertised-capability channel — a mod that changes networked state should stamp a mod tag here and refuse mismatched peers itself, because `LobbyItem.VersionMismatchObject` only *displays* a version mismatch and nothing in the connect path rejects it.

findings.title: STEP 5b (CLIENT) — SteamLobby.JoinLobby / OnGameLobbyJoinRequested -> OnLobbyEntered -> StartClient
findings.detail: The joining client's path is `SteamLobby.JoinLobby(CSteamID)` (browser row) or `OnGameLobbyJoinRequested(GameLobbyJoinRequested_t)` (Steam friends 'Join Game'), then `OnLobbyEntered(LobbyEnter_t)` reads `HostAddressKey` off the lobby and starts the Mirror client, with `ReportFailedLobbyEnter(EChatRoomEnterResponse)` on failure. Client-side `NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnClientConnect()` runs and the static `OnClientConnected` Action fires.

findings.modding: `NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnClientConnected` / `OnClientDisconnected` are static Il2CppSystem.Action add/remove accessors — subscribe instead of Harmony-patching for connect/disconnect notification.

findings.title: STEP 6 (HOST-ONLY) — OnServerConnect -> TryGetSteamId -> CheckBanned, then OnServerAddPlayer spawns the persistent PlayerMaster pair
findings.detail: `NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnServerConnect(NetworkConnectionToClient)` resolves the peer's transport identity with the private static `TryGetSteamId(NetworkConnectionToClient, ref CSteamID)` (only source is FizzySteamworks.ServerGetClientAddress) and runs `CheckBanned(string steamId, NetworkConnectionToClient)` against `bannedPlayers` (List<string>), caching into `bySteamId` (Dictionary<ulong, NetworkConnectionToClient>). `OnServerAddPlayer(NetworkConnectionToClient)` then spawns the connection's player object — which is NOT the avatar. It is the `Il2Cpp.PlayerMaster` + `Il2Cpp.PlayerMasterClientSide` pair, a scene-persistent identity/loadout/score object that survives every subsequent scene change. The avatar (`PlayerNetworking`) is a separate object spawned much later (step 22).

findings.modding: The two-object split (persistent PlayerMaster vs per-scene PlayerNetworking avatar) is the single most important structural fact of this pathway. Anything a mod wants to persist across the op-room -> mission transition must live on PlayerMaster, not on the avatar.

findings.title: STEP 7 — PlayerMaster.OnStartServer / OnStartClient / Start; SetMyName (Command) and SERVER_SpawnListPlayer -> RPC_SpawnListPlayer build the scoreboard row
findings.detail: `PlayerMaster.OnStartServer()` (host) and `OnStartClient()` (everyone) run, plus `Start()` and `ServerJustStarted()`. The owning client then asserts its identity with `SetMyName(string myName, Steamworks.CSteamID cSteamID)` — weaved as `UserCode_SetMyName__String__CSteamID` with no NetworkConnectionToClient parameter, i.e. a Mirror **Command**, so name and SteamID64 are client-claimed. Server responds with the plain [Server] method `SERVER_SpawnListPlayer()` -> ClientRpc `RPC_SpawnListPlayer(uint _boardItemNetID, ulong _64id)` which links each client to its `Il2Cpp.playerBoardItem` row (`forLobby` flag distinguishes lobby list from in-mission scoreboard). Loadout is pulled locally: `LoadMagsList()`, `LoadGrenadesList()`, `CheckForValidMags()`. Team is assigned by `OperationsManager.AutoAssignTeamOnPlayerJoin(PlayerMaster)`.

findings.modding: `PlayerMaster.AllPlayerMasters` (static List) plus `OnPlayerCountChanged` (static Action) is the correct roster handle from here on — no scene searching. Note SetMyName is spoofable and is a different identity from the transport SteamID used by CheckBanned.

findings.title: STEP 8 (HOST-ONLY) — NetworkManagerVectorGames.SwitchToLobby -> ServerChangeScene -> SwitchSceneAfterSeconds -> ApplyServerSceneChange
findings.detail: The move out of the menu into the Operation Room / lobby scene is `SwitchToLobby()`, which goes through the overridden `ServerChangeScene(string newSceneName)`. That override does not change scene immediately — it wraps the change in the coroutine `SwitchSceneAfterSeconds(string) -> IEnumerator` and commits via `ApplyServerSceneChange(string)`. `MenuScene` (string) holds the return-to-menu scene name and `LeaveMatch()` is the reverse. Every scene transition in the game — menu -> op room, op room -> mission, mission -> op room — runs through this same three-method funnel, and it is server-authoritative in all cases.

findings.modding: `ApplyServerSceneChange` is the one place to intercept or redirect every scene transition in the game. The deliberate delay coroutine exists so RPCs in flight land first — a mod that calls Mirror's ServerChangeScene directly will skip it and hit the spawn races the failsafes in step 10 exist to paper over.

findings.title: STEP 9 (CLIENT) — OnClientChangeScene -> BeforeSceneUnload/BeforeUnloadScene -> load -> OnClientSceneChanged
findings.detail: Each client receives Mirror's SceneMessage into `NetworkManagerVectorGames.OnClientChangeScene(string newSceneName, Il2CppMirror.SceneOperation sceneOperation, bool customHandling)`. Teardown hooks fire first: `GameManagerNetwork.BeforeSceneUnload()` and `GameManager.BeforeUnloadScene(string sceneName)`; on the host `GameManager.Server_BeforeLoadScene(string sceneName)` runs on the outbound side. The Lovatto loading screen (`Il2Cpp.bl_SceneLoader.LoadLevel(string)` / `DoAsyncOperation(string)` / `UpdateProgress()` / `TransitionToScene()`, with `bl_LoadingScreenUI` tips and backgrounds) covers the load, and `Il2Cpp.bl_SceneLoaderManager.GetSceneNames()` is the scene registry. `OnClientSceneChanged()` closes the transition.

findings.title: STEP 10 — Scene-loaded fan-out: GameManager.OnSceneLoaded / OnSceneLoadedMirrorSafe, GameManagerNetwork.OnSceneLoadedMirrorHookFuckMirrorIHateMirror, SpawnObjectsFailSafe, SceneStarterFailsafe
findings.detail: On load completion the game runs a stack of hooks, in this order by dependency: `GameManager.OnSceneLoaded(Scene, LoadSceneMode)` (the SceneManager.sceneLoaded subscriber) -> `GameManager.OnSceneLoadedMirrorSafe(Scene)` -> `GameManager.VectorFailsafe() -> IEnumerator`, alongside `GameManagerNetwork.OnSceneLoadedMirrorHookFuckMirrorIHateMirror()`, the `SpawnObjectsFailSafe() -> IEnumerator` coroutine, `TestAllGayUnspawnedObjects()`, and `Il2Cpp.SceneStarterFailsafe.Start()` -> `GameManagerNetwork.FromSceneStarterFailsafe()`. Per-client netId repair rides `DestroyObjectFailsafeCheckBecauseMirrorIsFuckingGayAsFuck(uint id, NetworkConnectionToClient sender)` (Command, connection last) -> `OhShitHomieYouGotFuckedBecauseMirrorIsDogShit(NetworkConnectionToClient target, uint ID)` (TargetRpc, connection first). `LoadingFailsafe()` / `CloseAllFailScreens()` cover the stuck-loading case. `GameManager.WarmDecalPools()` / `WarmSurfaceDecals(SurfaceInformation)` prime the decal pools for the new scene.

findings.title: STEP 11 — Operation Room is live: OperationRoomLoader.Switch, and the player gets a pawn there through the same spawn chain as a mission
findings.detail: The Operation Room is an ordinary networked scene, not a special menu. `Il2Cpp.OperationRoomLoader.Switch()` / `OperationTrainingAreaSwitch()` toggle `IndoorsArea` (GameObject[]) and `OutdoorsArea` (GameObject[]) — the FOB interior vs the training area. `GameManagerNetwork.get__inOpRoom()` is the flag distinguishing op room from mission. The player receives a real `PlayerNetworking` avatar here via the identical spawn chain used in a mission (steps 22-23), which is why the armory, character customisation and the laptop are all normal in-world interactables. `Il2Cpp.InteractableSceneTransition` is a second, board-bypassing exit from this room: it carries `sceneName`, `infilName`, `areaName`, `gameMode`, `InfilTime` directly and votes via `EnterScene()` / `SendRequest(string)` -> `CMD_SendRequest(string,int)` -> `RPC_SendRequest(string,int)` against `timesRequested`.

findings.title: STEP 12 — Approach the Cerberus laptop: PlayerNetworking.ScanForInteractable -> ProcessInteractable -> MissionLaptop.AccessLaptop(PlayerNetworking)
findings.detail: Interaction is owned by the avatar: `PlayerNetworking.ScanForInteractable() -> bool` (backed by `_interactableRayHit`), `ScanForNearbyInteractable() -> bool` (`interactionDetectionRange`), then `ProcessInteractable()`, with labels driven into `interactTxt` / `InteractionContextText`. Committing gives `Il2Cpp.MissionLaptop.AccessLaptop(Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking _playerNetworking)`, which raises `PlayerBlocker`, enables `LaptopPlayerCamera` (a per-laptop Cinemachine camera), turns on `uiRaycaster` (GraphicRaycaster) over the world-space `osCanvas`, and hands control to the DreamOS `computerManager` (WorldSpaceManager). Exit is `ExitLaptop()` on a `timeBeforeExit` / `_timerBeforeExit` countdown, with `ShitToKillWhenNotUsing` (GameObject[]) disabled while idle. Purely client-local — nothing about opening a laptop crosses the wire.

findings.modding: Mod UI added to the laptop must be parented under the world-space DreamOS Canvas or MissionLaptop.uiRaycaster will not hit it. `Il2Cpp.LaptopWindowNetworkNotify` (Window -> DreamOS.WindowManager, OnOpen/OnClose/OnMinimize/OnMaximize subscribed in Awake) is the copy-this pattern for a new laptop app.

findings.title: STEP 13 — MissionLaptop.SpawnOperations builds the operation list from OperationsManager.ActiveOperations / SimulationOperations
findings.detail: `MissionLaptop.SpawnOperations()` populates `ActiveOperationsList` and `SimulationOperationList` (Transforms) by walking `OperationsManager.get_ActiveOperations()` and `get_SimulationOperations()`, both `Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation>`, and calling `CerebusOperation.CreateInstance(Transform parent, MissionLaptop laptop)` — the virtual entry point on `Il2Cpp.CerebusUiBase` (`OnCreated`, `OnUpdate`, `OnClick`, `OnSingleClick`, `OnDoubleClick`, with `clickcount`/`clickcountTimer` disambiguation). Each row is an `Il2Cpp.OperationSelectionUI` with `NameTextBox`/`SecondTextBox`/`ThirdTextBox` (LocalizationTMPEvent) and two gating overlays `ClassfiedCover` (sic) / `RegionCover`. Tab switching is `ActiveOperationsTab` / `SimulationOperationsTab`. Everything here is a local UI build off replicated arrays.

findings.modding: CerebusUiBase is the designed extension point for a custom list entry. Whether an il2cpp subclass can be injected (ClassInjector.RegisterTypeInIl2Cpp + virtual dispatch reaching managed code) is the open question; the fallback is Harmony-patching OperationSelectionUI.OnClick and branching on a marker component.

findings.title: STEP 14 — Operation click is networked: MissionLaptopNetworkState.OperationSingleClicked -> SyncVar CurrentSelectedOperation -> every laptop redraws
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.MissionLaptopNetworkState` (singleton, `get_instance`, `AllMissionLaptops` = List<MissionLaptopDisplayer>) is the shared planning state — 19 SyncVars, each with a hook. Clicking a row calls `OperationSingleClicked(Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation clicked)`, which writes the SyncVar `CurrentSelectedOperation` (int index) plus `SelectedOperationLocked`; the hooks `OnSelectedOperationChanged(int previous, int current)` and `OnOperationLockedChanged(bool,bool)` then run `SetInitialLaptopState` / `MissionLaptopDisplayer.SetSelectedOperation()` on **every** laptop in the level. `GetOperationByIndex(int)` resolves the index back to a CerebusOperation. Page state is the same shape: `SetCurrentPage(int)` / `OnCurrentPageChanged`, `SetSimulationPage(bool)` / `OnSimulationPageChanged`, `SetMinimized(bool)` / `OnMinimizedChanged`.
