findings.title: STEP 15 — Target package selection: MissionLaptop.SpawnTargetPackages(CerebusOperation) -> TargetPackageSingleClicked -> SyncVar CurrentSelectedTargetPackage
findings.detail: `MissionLaptop.SpawnTargetPackages(Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation _operation)` fills `TargetPackageParent` with `Il2Cpp.CerebusTargetPackage` rows. Selecting one runs `MissionLaptopNetworkState.TargetPackageSingleClicked(CerebusTargetPackage)`, writing SyncVars `CurrentSelectedTargetPackage`, `SelectedTargetPackageLocked` and `SelectedTargetPackageSimulation`, with hooks `OnSelectedTargetPackageChanged(int,int)`, `OnTargetPackageLockedChanged`, `OnTargetPackageSimulationChanged` driving `MissionLaptopDisplayer.SetSelectedTargetPackage()`. `SetAllTargetPackages(CerebusTargetPackage)` bulk-sets. Gating for locked content is `CerebusOpboard.isLocked` + `unlockCode` checked against progression, surfaced as `MissionLaptop.LockedOperationString` / `SimulationMapUnlockString` (LocalizedString) and the `ClassfiedCover` overlay.

findings.title: STEP 16 — Opboard instantiation: MissionLaptopDisplayer.SpawnOperationBoard -> MissionLaptop.SpawnTargetPackagePlanning(CerebusOpboard) -> CerebusOpboard.CreateInstance -> OperationBoardUI.Setup
findings.detail: `MissionLaptopDisplayer.SpawnOperationBoard()` -> `MissionLaptop.SpawnTargetPackagePlanning(Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard opboard)` fills `opBoardParent`, calling `CerebusOpboard.CreateInstance(Transform parent, MissionLaptop laptop)` then `Il2Cpp.OperationBoardUI.Setup(CerebusOpboard opboard, MissionLaptop laptop)` and `MissionLaptopDisplayer.SetOpBoardInfo()` / `SetOpBoardSimulationStatus()`. The CerebusOpboard is the authored mission record: `MapPrefab` (GameObject), `AvailableInfils` (string[]), `MinAI`/`MaxAI`, `Difficulty` (AIDifficulty), `PrepTimeInSeconds`, `SelectedInfiltrationTime`, `INFILTRATION_TARGET`/`INFILTRATION_TIME`, `TARGETPACKAGE` (TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS[]), `AffectGamemode` + `GameModeOverride`, `requireEnoughInfils`/`requireEnoughExfils`, `TargetRaidTime`, `AchievementName` + `achievement_aiDifficulty` + `achievement_min_ai_amount`, `HVTSpawnIsRandom`, `SituationReport` (LocalizedString). This data is identical on every client because it comes from the same prefab.

findings.title: STEP 17 — Infil choice on the board map: MapInfilMarker.OnButtonPressed -> OperationBoardUI.InfilTargetButtonPressed(int,bool) -> MissionLaptopNetworkState.SetInfilActive -> long ActiveInfilMask
findings.detail: The board map carries `MapInfilMarkers` and `FullscreenMapInfilMarkers` (Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.MapInfilMarker>). Each marker knows `InfilName`, `MarkerIndex`, `MaxPlayers`, `CurrentNumPlayers`, and its kind via `IsGroundInfil` / `IsHeliInfil` / `IsExfil` (with distinct Selected/Deselected marker GameObjects). `OnButtonPressed()` -> `OperationBoardUI.InfilTargetButtonPressed(int index, bool active)` -> `MissionLaptopNetworkState.SetInfilActive(int index, bool active)`, which flips a bit in the SyncVar `ActiveInfilMask` (**long** — hard cap of 64 infils per map). The hook `OnActiveInfilMaskChanged(long previous, long current)` fans out to `OperationBoardUI.SetActiveInfilsMaskUI(long)` and `MapInfilMarker.SetInfilVisualsActive(bool)` on every laptop. `SetAllInfilsActive()` and `IsInfilActive(int)` round out the API. This selects which infils are *available*; picking your own seat happens later (step 20).

findings.title: STEP 18 — Board parameter sliders write MissionLaptopNetworkState SyncVars, but most of them never reach the server as launch payload
findings.detail: `OperationBoardUI` exposes the full tuning surface — `SetInfiltrationTime(int)`, `SetPreparationTime(int)`, `SetAI_COUNT(float)`, `SetOpforDifficulty(int)`, `SetAI_HVT_COUNT(float)`, `SetHVTSpawnPoint(int)`, `SetPVPTimeLimit/SetPVPRoundLimit/SetFFATimeLimit/SetFFAKillLimit(int)`, `SetPVPParam1/SetPVPParam2(int)` — over DreamOS HorizontalSelector/SliderManager widgets, each writing through `MissionLaptopNetworkState.SetSelectedInfilTime / SetSelectedPrepTime / SetEnemyCount / SetHVTEnemyCount / SetDifficulty / SetHVTSpawnType / SetPVPParameterOne / SetPVPParameterTwo`, replicated as SyncVars with the shared hook `OnOperationParametersChanged(int previous, int current)` and echoed back into `SetInfilTimeUI` / `SetPrepTimeUIValue` / `SetAICountUI` / `SetDifficultyUI`. Critically, NONE of AI count, difficulty, HVT count or PVP/FFA limits appear in the StartOperation payload of step 19 — `OperationsManager.FFA_TimeLimit / FFA_KillLimit / PVP_TimeLimit / PVP_RoundLimit` are plain fields with no Network* accessor, i.e. not SyncVars. Only prep time and infil time survive into the launch call.

Runtime slider changes made by a NON-HOST client have no synced channel into OperationsManager and are very likely dropped. Runtime probe: as a joined client, move the AI-count slider, launch, then read OperationsManager.singleton on the host. A mod wanting client-configurable rules must add its own Command.

findings.title: STEP 19 — Execute: OperationBoardUI.ExecuteOperationButtonPressed -> infil/exfil gating -> EnableConfirmationMenu -> StartOperationButton -> CerebusOpboard.Start_Operation
findings.detail: `ExecuteOperationButtonPressed()` first checks the authored requirements: `CerebusOpboard.requireEnoughInfils` / `requireEnoughExfils` against the current mask, showing `NotEnoughInfilsButton` / `NotEnoughExfilsButton` instead of `ExecuteOperationButton` when unsatisfied. Passing that, `EnableConfirmationMenu()` opens `ConfirmationWindow` (Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.ModalWindowManager) and `MissionLaptopNetworkState.SetShowingMissionStartConfirmation(bool)` replicates the modal so every laptop shows it (SyncVar `ShowingStartMissionConfirmation`, hook `OnShowingStartMissionConfirmationChanged`). `StartOperationButton()` commits -> `CerebusOpboard.Start_Operation()`. `CloseConfirmationWindow()` / `CancelOperationButton()` back out.

findings.title: STEP 20 — OperationsManager.StartOperation -> CMD_StartOperation (Command, any client) -> server writes the launch SyncVars
findings.detail: `CerebusOpboard.Start_Operation()` calls `OperationsManager.StartOperation(string sceneName, int prepTime, string displayName, string infilTime, string _activeAchievement, float targetTime)`, mirrored exactly by `CMD_StartOperation(same 6 args)` — weaved as `UserCode_CMD_StartOperation__String__Int32__String__String__String__Single` with no NetworkConnectionToClient parameter, so it is a real Mirror **Command** and any client can fire it. On the server it writes the SyncVars `isStarting` (hook `StartingBool(bool,bool)`), `PrepTimer` (hook `PrepTimerUpdate(float,float)`), `CurrentGameMode` (hook `GameModeChanged(GameMode,GameMode)` — sourced from `CerebusOpboard.AffectGamemode` + `GameModeOverride`), `activeAchievementName`, `RaidTargetTime`, plus `currentScene` / `InfiltrationName` / `operationMapID` and the display strings on `Il2Cpp.OperationUiSync` (SyncVars `CurrentLocation`, `OperationTime`, `InfilName` with hooks `OnOperationNameChanged` / `OnOperationTimeChanged` / `OnInfilPointChanged`). `ResetStats()` clears IntelCollected/TotalKills/TotalBots/TotalOperatorsInRaid.

findings.detail: The server broadcasts `OperationsManager.RPC_StartOperation(int defaultInfil)` (weaved `UserCode_RPC_StartOperation__Int32`). Clients respond with `MissionLaptopDisplayer.SetMissionStarting()` / `OperationBoardUI.SetMissionStarting()` and `MissionLaptopNetworkState.StartingBoolChanged(bool)`, and the deploy screen comes up on `Il2Cpp.InfilSelectorDisplayer` (singleton `get_instance`): `SpawnMap(GameObject mapPrefab)` instantiates `CerebusOpboard.MapPrefab` under `MapParent`, `ShowInfilSelection()` raises `SelectInfilUI`, `SetInfilEnabled(int index, bool)` applies the ActiveInfilMask, and `SetOperationName(string)` / `SetOperationTime(string)` fill `LocationText` / `DeployTimeText` / `LocalTimeText` / `ObjectiveText` from OperationUiSync. `defaultInfil` is the pre-selected index. `OperationsManager.ResetAllPlayerInfilIndices()` clears prior picks.

The displayer pools its player icons (`playerIconPool` Stack, `GetMapIconFromPool()`, work batched in LateUpdate via `playerIconsDirty`) — return icons to the pool, never Destroy them.

findings.title: STEP 22 — Ready-up is per-player infil selection: InfilSelectorDisplayer.RequestInfilIndex(int) -> PlayerMaster.CMD_RequestInfilTarget(int) -> SyncVar CurrentInfilIndex
findings.detail: There is no separate ready button — committing to an infil IS the ready action. `InfilSelectorDisplayer.RequestInfilIndex(int index) -> bool` (returns false when the marker is at `MapInfilMarker.MaxPlayers`) calls `PlayerMaster.CMD_RequestInfilTarget(int _infil)`, a weaved Command (`UserCode_CMD_RequestInfilTarget__Int32`). The server writes the SyncVar `CurrentInfilIndex` (hook `OnInfilChanged(int oldVal,int newVal)`); the exfil twin is `CMD_RequestExfilTarget(int)` -> `CurrentExfilIndex` -> `OnExfilChanged`. Readable names come from `PlayerMaster.get_CurrentInfil()` / `get_CurrentExfil()` (strings). Hooks drive `InfilSelectorDisplayer.UpdateMarkers(int)` and `RefreshPlayerIcons()` so everyone sees who has stacked on which bird. `SetInfilConfirmText(string)` updates `confirmText` / `ConfirmButton`; `AbortOperationButtonPressed()` sits alongside.

A mod adding infils must keep `InfilMethods.infilName` in some `ExfilZone.linkedInfils` list or the raid becomes unwinnable — that tie is string-matched.

findings.title: STEP 23 (HOST TICKS) — Prep timer: OperationsManager.Update counts PrepTimer down; abort is CancelOperation -> CMD_CancelOperation -> RPC_CancelOperation
findings.detail: `OperationsManager.Update()` decrements the SyncVar `PrepTimer` on the server; the hook `PrepTimerUpdate(float previous, float current)` and the computed `PrepRemainingTime` drive the countdown UI, formatted by the static helper `ToClockMMSS(float seconds) -> string`. `isStarting` (hook `StartingBool(bool,bool)`) gates the whole state. The initial value comes from `CerebusOpboard.PrepTimeInSeconds` overridden by the board slider. This window is the armory/loadout phase in the op room. Aborting: `OperationBoardUI.AbortOperationButtonPressed()` or `InfilSelectorDisplayer.AbortOperationButtonPressed()` -> `OperationsManager.CancelOperation()` -> `CMD_CancelOperation()` (weaved Command, any client) -> `RPC_CancelOperation()` broadcast.

Worth a guard in any co-op mod. Read `Mirror.RemoteCalls.RemoteProcedureCalls.remoteCallDelegates` at runtime to settle it.

findings.title: STEP 24 (HOST-ONLY) — Timer expiry: OperationsManager.SERVER_LoadOperation -> AutoSetTeams / AssignTeamsPVE / AssignTeamsTDM -> ServerChangeScene
findings.detail: `SERVER_LoadOperation()` is a plain [Server] method (no UserCode_ pair — host only, unreachable from a client). It assigns sides through `AutoSetTeams()` -> `AssignTeamsPVE()` or `AssignTeamsTDM()` (using `GetShortTeam()` to balance), writing `TeamIdentifier.TeamID` SyncVars into `TeamManager.OperatorTeams`, then calls `GameManager.Server_BeforeLoadScene(string sceneName)` and hands the scene name from `OperationsManager.currentScene` to `NetworkManagerVectorGames.ServerChangeScene(string)` — re-entering the step 8/9/10 transition funnel, this time toward the mission scene. `GameManagerNetwork.ShowLoadingScreen()` covers the gap.

findings.title: STEP 25 — Per-client readiness after the mission scene loads: PlayerMaster.OnSceneLoaded -> WarmSceneAndSignalReady -> PlayerMasterClientSide.IsLoaded -> GameManagerNetwork.ReadyPlayers -> AllPlayersLoaded
findings.detail: `PlayerMaster` survives the scene change (it is the connection object) and subscribes `OnSceneLoaded(Scene scene, LoadSceneMode mode)`, which starts `WarmSceneAndSignalReady() -> IEnumerator`. That coroutine warms the scene and then sets the SyncVar `PlayerMasterClientSide.IsLoaded` (hook `OnReadyChanged(bool previous, bool current)`, static tally `NumPlayersReady`). The server counts these into the SyncVar `GameManagerNetwork.ReadyPlayers` and flips the SyncVar `AllPlayersLoaded` (hook `OnAllPlayersLoaded(bool previous, bool current)`), which triggers `HideLoadingScreen()` / `HideLoadingScreenDelay() -> IEnumerator` and unblocks the mode. Arrival is announced by `PlayerMaster.SERVER_SendJoinMessage()` (plain [Server]) -> `RPC_SendJoinMessage(string playerName)` -> `ChatController.AddToChatOutput(string)`. Voice is reset across the boundary by `ResetVoiceForSceneChange()` / `ServerResetVoiceState()`.

findings.title: STEP 26 — Mode boot: GameMode.Start -> Initialize -> WaitForPlayerMasterAndWarm -> WarmShadersAndSignalReady -> WaitForPlayers -> Server_AllPlayersLoaded (host-only)
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.GameMode` (abstract NetworkBehaviour base, `static singleton`, `isNight`, `didStartClient`) drives mission startup: `Start()` -> `Initialize()`, then the coroutine chain `WaitForPlayerMasterAndWarm() -> WarmShadersAndSignalReady() -> WaitForPlayers()`, ending in the virtual `Server_AllPlayersLoaded()` — implemented by exactly four types: `Il2Cpp.InfiltrationManager` (all four PVE variants), `Il2Cpp.PvpGameode`, `Il2Cpp.FFA`, `Il2Cpp.WaveSurvival`. Server_AllPlayersLoaded is a plain virtual, not weaved — host only. The client-side counterparts are `LoadingCompleteClient()` and `Client_AllPlayersLoaded()`. `RaidManager.singleton` (the per-map PVE content director, a separate object from the mode) has already run its `Awake()` / `OnStartServer()`.

findings.title: STEP 27 — Avatar spawn: PlayerMaster.SpawnPlayer -> ClientSpawnBS -> CMDSpawnPlayer(NetworkIdentity) -> SpawnPlayerServer -> RPCSpawnPlayer(PlayerNetworking, Vector3)
findings.detail: This is where the actual body appears, and it is a separate networked object from PlayerMaster. Local kickoff: `PlayerMaster.SpawnPlayer()` -> `ClientSpawnBS()` -> the weaved Command `CMDSpawnPlayer(Il2CppMirror.NetworkIdentity netid)` (`UserCode_CMDSpawnPlayer__NetworkIdentity`). Server side: `SpawnPlayerServer()` (plain [Server]) or `SpawnPlayerServerDelayed(float time)` instantiates `PlayerV2Prefab` (with `PlayerV1Prefab` as the legacy slot), NetworkServer-spawns it with authority for that connection, records it via `SetPlayerSpawnedObject(Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking playerNetworking)` into the SyncVar `PlayerSpawnedObjectID` (hook `OnPlayerObjectUpdate(int,int)`), and broadcasts the ClientRpc `RPCSpawnPlayer(Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking playerNetworking, UnityEngine.Vector3 _spawnRotation)`. Placement inputs are `PlayerMaster.LastSpawnPoint` (Transform) and `spawnRotation` (Vector3). Respawn later reuses the same chain via `Respawn_Local()`, `CLIENT_RequestAutoRespawn()`, `PlayerMasterClientSide.StartRespawnProcess()` / `AutoSpawnPlayer()`.

findings.title: STEP 28 — Authority handoff: CMD_GetSetPlayerObject -> TargetRPC_GetSetPlayerObject -> OnPlayerObjectSet -> PlayerNetworking.HasAuthSetup / NoAuthSetup
findings.detail: After the avatar exists, each client must learn which NetworkIdentity is its own. `PlayerMaster.CMD_GetSetPlayerObject(NetworkIdentity targetNetID)` (Command) is answered by `TargetRPC_GetSetPlayerObject(Il2CppMirror.NetworkConnection networkConnection, NetworkIdentity identity)` — connection parameter FIRST, so a **TargetRpc** to that one client — landing in `OnPlayerObjectSet(NetworkIdentity identity)`, with `DelayGetPlayerObject() -> IEnumerator` as the poll-until-resolved fallback for the netId-arrives-before-the-spawn race. The avatar then configures itself: `Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking.HasAuthSetup()` (owner) or `NoAuthSetup()` (remote proxy) toggle six designer-populated arrays — `scriptsEnableAuth`, `scriptsDisableAuth`, `gameObjectseEnableAuth` (sic), `gameObjectsDisableAuth`, `scriptsDisableNoAuth`, `gameObjectsDisableNoAuth` — plus `AuthShadowedParents` and `rotationTrackerNoAuth`. `PlayerMaster.get_PlayerSpawnedObject()` is the resolved handle.

findings.title: STEP 29 (HOST-ONLY) — InfiltrationManager.Server_AllPlayersLoaded -> RespawnPlayers -> Server_StartInfil -> StartInfil(InfilMethods, index)
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.InfiltrationManager` (singleton `get_instance`) is the PVE mode controller and owns insertion. Its `Server_AllPlayersLoaded()` override runs `RespawnPlayers() -> IEnumerator` (which drives the step-27 spawn chain for everyone) and then `Server_StartInfil()`, which walks `infilMethods` (Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.InfilMethods>) and calls `StartInfil(Il2Cpp.InfilMethods method, int infilIndex)` per selected infil. `Il2Cpp.InfilMethods` is the authored per-infil record: `infilName` (string, the key that ties to `ExfilZone.linkedInfils` and `CerebusOpboard.AvailableInfils`), `infilObject` (GameObject), `SpawnBehaviour` (Behaviour), `extracts` (ExfilZone[]), `isPrepared` (bool), and the branch discriminator `VehicleInfiltration` (bool) with `VehicleAnimatorInfiltrationClips` (string[]). Every one of Server_AllPlayersLoaded / RespawnPlayers / Server_StartInfil / StartInfil / MovePlayersToSpawn / SpawnHelicopter / SpawnVehicleV2 has NO UserCode_ pair — confirmed host-only.

findings.title: STEP 30a — Walk-in branch: InfiltrationManager.MovePlayersToSpawn -> RPC_SetSpawnPosition (TargetRpc) -> GameManager.MovePlayerToSpawn coroutine
findings.detail: For a non-vehicle infil, `MovePlayersToSpawn(Il2Cpp.InfilMethods method)` runs on the host and, per player, sends `RPC_SetSpawnPosition(Il2CppMirror.NetworkConnectionToClient target, UnityEngine.Vector3 pos, UnityEngine.Quaternion rot)` — connection parameter FIRST and weaved as `UserCode_RPC_SetSpawnPosition__NetworkConnectionToClient__Vector3__Quaternion`, so a **TargetRpc** to exactly one client. The receiving client runs `Il2Cpp.GameManager.MovePlayerToSpawn(Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation) -> IEnumerator`, a coroutine (not an instant teleport — it has to disable the CMF controller, place the capsule, and re-enable, which is why it yields). Fallback pickers live on GameManager: `nextSpawnPosition(bool useTeams, int team, int iteration)`, `nextSpawnPositionRandom()`, `BestFFASpawn(int startIndex)`, `nextEnemySpawnPosition()`, over `SpawnPointsInScene` / `Pspawns` / `Espawns` / `heliSpawns` with `RandomSpawns` / `SetRandomPlayerSpawns(bool)` and the index cursors `PnextSpawnIndex` / `EnextSpawnIndex` / `nextTeamIndex`. `Il2Cpp.SpawnPoint` carries only `{bool CanSpawnPlayer; int Team}`. `InfiltrationManager.DefaultSpawn` is the last-resort GameObject.

findings.title: STEP 0 (tooling) — method bodies ARE readable: a native disassembler + RVA map is already built in the scratchpad, so this whole trace is proven, not inferred
findings.detail: The Phase-1 constraint 'you cannot see method bodies via the inspector' is true of InteropInspector but NOT of the target. D:\Games\OPERATOR\GameAssembly.dll game code lives in the section named `il2cpp` (RVA 0x6F2000, size 0x4860081) — NOT `.text` (which is only the il2cpp runtime). A 165,503-entry RVA->`Assembly!Type::Method` map already exists at <scratchpad>\ILProbe\rvamap.tsv, and <scratchpad>\disasm.py is a working capstone x86-64 harness. I added two reusable scripts: <scratchpad>\calls.py (disassemble a method, resolve every direct `call rel32` to a name) and <scratchpad>\xref.py (linear E8 scan over .text+il2cpp building a full reverse call-edge index, cached to edges.pkl). Every claim below marked proven-static was read out of the actual machine code. WARNING: I overwrote <scratchpad>\all.txt (a prior Phase-1 index) with a flattened copy of teardown_findings.json; that copy also exists as <scratchpad>\findings_flat.txt. The 943-name type index survives as <scratchpad>\allnames.txt / alltypes.txt / full.txt.

findings.title: STEP 1 — WeaponV3.Update polls InputLayer.GetKey(InputKey.Shoot); the trigger is edge-triggered in semi/burst and level-triggered in full-auto
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponV3.Update (RVA 0xA54B60) is the input pump. It reads `InputLayer.GetKey(InputKey key, bool ActivatedThisFrame)` 25 times; `InputKey.Shoot` is the integer 31 (0x1F) and is read at 0xA56090, 0xA56236, 0xA56393, 0xA56554, 0xA565F2, 0xA56696, 0xA576E8. Every Shoot read passes ActivatedThisFrame=true (dl=1) EXCEPT the one at 0xA565F2 which passes 0 — that is the full-auto branch. The branch selection at 0xA56336 is a jump table on the fire-mode int (GunStats.fireMode), so semi/burst/auto are separate code paths each with their own trigger read. Also read here: Firemode(38), ChamberRound(32), Reload(33), EmergencyReload(34), CheckMag(35), CheckChamber(36), Inspect(37), Lasers/Flashlights(16-19). InputLayer holds Dictionary<InputKey,InputKeyBindInstance> Keybinds and a MouseInputSuppressed/InputDisabled pair.

findings.title: STEP 2 — WeaponV3.CanFire() gates on weapon completeness, not on ammo or rate of fire
findings.detail: WeaponV3.CanFire (0xA42CF0) calls exactly three things: UnityEngine.Object.op_Equality, InputLayer.GetKey, WeaponMods.CheckIfWeaponIsComplete, and HintManager.SpawnPopup. So the 'can I shoot' predicate is really 'is this weapon assembled', and on failure it shows a UI hint rather than firing. Rate of fire is NOT here — it is the `fireTimer` float field on WeaponV3 evaluated inside Update, together with `releaseTrigger` (semi-auto latch) and `pulledTriggerOnEmpty` (dry-fire). The call order in Update is: get_isOwned -> InputLayer.GetKey(Shoot) -> CanFire() -> Fire() -> CMD_Fire(roundInChamber).

findings.title: STEP 3 — WeaponV3.Fire() runs on the owner AND (via RPC) on every remote; it is not ownership-gated
findings.detail: WeaponV3.Fire (0xA46AC0) calls WeaponSetAnimationLayerWeight, PlayerNetworking.set_CanSwitchWeapon(false), NetworkBehaviour.get_isOwned, WeaponV3.DischargeRound (0xA46C63), WeaponPlayAnimation, and DelayExt.PlayAfterSeconds (the `<Fire>b__139_0` lambda). Critically the get_isOwned at 0xA46BD7 guards only a small block (zeroing a field on _health) and branches past it at 0xA46BDE — DischargeRound at 0xA46C63 is reached regardless of ownership. Its real guards are `gunStats.field@0x34 > 0` and `gunFunction.field@0x48 != 0` (chamber state). Ownership separation happens one level deeper, inside SpawnBullet.

On success it continues: WeaponPlayAnimation -> UnityEngine.Random.Range (the MOA roll) at 0xA447C0 -> SpawnBullet at 0xA4485F -> MuzzleDevice.FireMuzzleFlash -> WeaponV3.PlayGunshotAudio -> Transform.SetPositionAndRotation + BulletShell.Ejection -> WeaponV3.ChamberRound -> WeaponV3.ApplyRecoil -> AudioSource.Play -> WeaponSFX.Fire_StopLoop / FireSuppressed_StopLoop.

findings.title: STEP 5 — WeaponV3.CMD_Fire(roundInChamber) -> UserCode_CMD_Fire -> RPC_Fire is the COSMETIC channel; it carries no ballistics
findings.detail: CMD_Fire (0xA40B00, requiresAuthority=TRUE — the byte at [rsp+0x28] into SendCommandInternal is literal 1) writes one bool. Its server handler UserCode_CMD_Fire__Boolean (0xA595C0) does exactly two things: set_NetworkroundInChamber(value) (a SyncVar write, server-authoritative) and SendRPCInternal for RPC_Fire (hash 0x9F036660, channelId=1, includeOwner=1). UserCode_RPC_Fire (0xA5A2B0) then runs on every client: `if (isOwned) return;` (0xA5A2DF/jne 0xA5A33A) then tail-jumps to either WeaponV3.Fire (0xA5A34A) or WeaponV3.SimulateFire (0xA5A335) depending on a null test on field@0xA8->[+0x10]. SimulateFire (0xA53940) is pure presentation: WeaponPlayAnimation, MuzzleDevice.FireMuzzleFlash, WeaponSFX.Fire / FireSuppressed / Fire_StartLoop / FireSuppressed_StartLoop.

Hooking CMD_Fire/RPC_Fire gives you every shot event including dry-fires and misfires but never the trajectory; hooking CMD_SendBullet (step 7) gives you trajectories only. Rate-of-fire anticheat belongs on UserCode_CMD_Fire because it is the one the server actually executes per trigger pull.

findings.title: STEP 6 — the MOA spread vector is rolled client-side in DischargeRound and never recomputed anywhere
findings.detail: The Random.Range at 0xA447C0 inside DischargeRound produces the Vector3 handed to SpawnBullet as `_moaSpread`; WeaponV3 caches it in `moaSpread` (Vector3) alongside `_MOA` (float, derived from GunStats.MOA + attachment modifiers + Bullet.selfMOA). A second Random.Range lives inside SpawnBullet at 0xA54486 for the per-projectile roll (buckshot pellets / Bullet.selfMOA). Nothing on the server side ever calls Random or reads GunStats.MOA — UserCode_CMD_SendBullet contains zero arithmetic (see step 8).

findings.title: STEP 7 — WeaponV3.SpawnBullet(muzzlePos, muzzleRot, moaSpread, _isOwned): non-owners return immediately; the owner increments its shot stat and sends CMD_SendBullet
findings.detail: SpawnBullet (0xA53E30) opens with `cmp byte [rbp+0x50], 0; je 0xA54375` where 0xA54375 is a bare epilogue+ret — i.e. **if _isOwned is false the method does nothing at all**. With _isOwned true it: increments the shots-fired counter (`inc dword [WeaponStatDetails+0x64]`), resolves/caches the muzzle transform into field@0x148, then at 0xA53F8B checks Mirror NetworkBehaviour.isOwned and if true writes Vector3+Quaternion+Vector3 into a pooled NetworkWriter and calls SendCommandInternal with hash 0xCCD25738 (= CMD_SendBullet, requiresAuthority=1) at 0xA5405E. It then falls through to the local spawn: either a buckshot fan-out through SpawnProjectile (0xA54353) or the single-round path Random.Range -> Bullet.SpawnBullet (0xA54546) -> BulletInstance.ApplyMoaSpread -> StartBulletP2. DischargeRound passes `_isOwned = NetworkBehaviour.isOwned` (0xA44824/0xA4485B).

findings.title: STEP 8 — the server does NOT validate the shot: UserCode_CMD_SendBullet and RPC_SendBullet are literally the same function body
findings.detail: WeaponV3.RPC_SendBullet and WeaponV3.UserCode_CMD_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3 both live at RVA 0xA4FDC0 — the linker folded them because the Command's handler body is nothing but `this.RPC_SendBullet(a,b,c)` after inlining. The body: NetworkWriterPool.Get, WriteVector3, WriteQuaternion, WriteVector3, SendRPCInternal(hash 0xDC30B5B1). Zero comparisons, no muzzle-position plausibility check, no rate check, no spread recompute. The rebroadcast flags read out of the stack home slots are channelId=0 (Reliable) and **includeOwner=FALSE** (both taken from a register the compiler knows is zero — the adjacent MethodInfo* slot proves rax==0 there). Contrast RPC_Fire, which passes literal channelId=1 and includeOwner=1.

Anti-cheat has exactly one insertion point — prefix UserCode_CMD_SendBullet on the host, re-derive spread from GunStats.MOA, clamp muzzlePos against the sender's PlayerNetworking transform, and rate-limit per netId.

findings.title: STEP 9 — UserCode_RPC_SendBullet on every non-owner calls SpawnBullet(..., _isOwned: true)
findings.detail: UserCode_RPC_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3 (0xA5A3D0) copies the three struct args to the stack, writes literal 1 into the `_isOwned` argument slot ([rsp+0x20]) and 0 into the MethodInfo slot, then calls WeaponV3.SpawnBullet at 0xA5A41E. So on remotes the `_isOwned` PARAMETER is true (it means 'this call is authoritative for spawning'), while the Mirror `isOwned` PROPERTY checked at 0xA53F8B is false — which is why remotes spawn the projectile but do not re-send the Command. The two 'owned' concepts are deliberately different and easy to confuse.
findings.members: WeaponV3.UserCode_RPC_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3, WeaponV3.SpawnBullet
findings.modding: To observe every shot fired by every player from any client, hook UserCode_RPC_SendBullet (remote shots) plus WeaponV3.SpawnBullet with _isOwned true (your own).

findings.title: STEP 10 — WeaponV3.SpawnProjectile stamps the authority flag onto the projectile: BulletInstance.isOwner = weapon.isOwned
findings.detail: SpawnProjectile (0xA546C0) is 0x140 bytes and fully readable: `BulletInstance b = Bullet.SpawnBullet(prefab, muzzlePos, muzzleRot)`; `b.isOwner[+0xC0] = this.isOwned` (0xA54732/0xA54740); `b.isPlayer[+0xC1] = 1` hardcoded; `b.shootersGameObject[+0xD8] = this._health[+0x148]`; `b.ApplyMoaSpread(moaSpread)`; `b.suppressedAmount[+0xD0] = gunStats.field@0x1C`; tail-jump to `b.StartBulletP2()`. **This single byte is the entire damage-authority model of the game** — see step 18.
findings.members: WeaponV3.SpawnProjectile, BulletInstance.isOwner (+0xC0), BulletInstance.isPlayer (+0xC1), BulletInstance.shootersGameObject (+0xD8), BulletInstance.suppressedAmount (+0xD0)
findings.modding: Force isOwner=false on your own rounds and you fire completely harmless bullets that still look and sound right to everyone. Force it true on a received round and you become a second damage source for someone else's shot (the server accepts it, see step 25).

findings.title: STEP 11 — Bullet.SpawnBullet rents from BulletManager's pool and copies the ~40-field stat block
findings.detail: Bullet.SpawnBullet(Bullet prefab, Vector3 muzzlePos, Quaternion muzzleRot) (0xAFA9C0) calls BulletManager.Get() and (via inlined RentInstance/CopyStatsFrom/Register — BulletManager.RentInstance and BulletInstance.CopyStatsFrom have zero direct callers, both inlined here) produces a pooled BulletInstance. Il2Cpp.Bullet is a MonoBehaviour data template with no behaviour; BulletInstance is a plain managed object with no Transform and no Unity lifecycle. Oddity: Bullet.SpawnBullet also calls sc.terrain.proceduralpainter.TerrainPainter.RefreshVegetation.
findings.members: Bullet.SpawnBullet, BulletManager.Get, BulletManager.RentInstance, BulletManager.ReturnInstance, BulletInstance.CopyStatsFrom, BulletManager._pool, BulletManager._bullets
findings.modding: CopyStatsFrom is inlined, so a Harmony patch on it will never run. To rewrite per-round stats, postfix Bullet.SpawnBullet (it returns the BulletInstance) or WeaponV3.SpawnProjectile.

findings.title: STEP 12 — BulletInstance.StartBulletP2 resolves shooter identity as a Mirror netId, acquires the tracer, and fires the muzzle-suppression pulse
findings.detail: StartBulletP2 (0xAF54C0). BulletInstance.StartBullet (0xAF5CB0) has ZERO callers and is dead. P2 does: from shootersGameObject[+0xD8] (a Health) TryGetComponent one component type — if found, take its field@0x88 and call Mirror.NetworkBehaviour.get_netId (0xAF5640), storing the result in shootersNetworkID[+0xE0]; else TryGetComponent a second type and read an int field@0x30 (the AI path). Then Random.Range + Quaternion.Internal_FromEulerRad + op_Multiply (the spread application), ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled (tracer), BulletCrack.CheckForInitialShotSuppression (0xAF5BFF), and BulletManager.Get to register. **shooterID is a Mirror netId, not PlayerMaster.UniqueID** — confirmed downstream by UserCode_CMDTakeDamage calling Mirror.Utils.GetSpawnedInServerOrClient on it. This corrects Phase-1 player-avatar#7.
findings.members: BulletInstance.StartBulletP2, BulletInstance.shootersNetworkID (+0xE0), Mirror.NetworkBehaviour.get_netId, BulletCrack.CheckForInitialShotSuppression, ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled, BulletInstance.StartBullet (dead)
findings.modding: Kill attribution: resolve a shooterID with Mirror.NetworkClient/NetworkServer.spawned[netId], not by scanning PlayerMaster.AllPlayerMasters for UniqueID. The value -3 is a reserved sentinel (step 30).

findings.title: STEP 13 — BulletManager.FixedUpdate is the batch tick: snapshot, BeginManagedTick, ScheduleBatch, Complete, then Travel per bullet
findings.detail: BulletManager.FixedUpdate (0xAF6C40) in order: Time.get_fixedDeltaTime, Physics.get_gravity, List<BulletInstance>.CopyTo into `_tickSnapshot` (so mutation during the tick is safe), BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick (0xAF7006), BulletInstance.Travel (0xAF703B) for bullets that need no ray, a String.Format + Debug.LogError guard path, BulletInstance.ReturnToPool, then RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch (0xAF7224) + Unity.Jobs.JobHandle.Complete (0xAF723E), then RaycastHit.get_collider + Object.op_Inequality to derive `chordHit` per bullet. BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick (0xAF4300) has ZERO callers — it is a 0x40-byte wrapper that just calls Travel, and FixedUpdate calls Travel directly instead. BulletManager.LateUpdate separately drives tracers via _tracerBullets.
findings.members: BulletManager.FixedUpdate, BulletManager._tickSnapshot, BulletManager._rayBullets, BulletManager._commands, BulletManager._results, BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick, UnityEngine.RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch
findings.modding: Patching BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick (the Phase-1 recommendation) will never fire. The correct per-tick hook is BulletInstance.Travel, and the correct per-hit hook is BulletInstance.ProcessBullet.

findings.title: STEP 14 — BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick builds one RaycastCommand chord per bullet per fixed step
findings.detail: BeginManagedTick(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, ref RaycastCommand command, ref bool needsRay) (0xAF1000) calls UnityEngine.RaycastCommand..ctor at 0xAF129F and BulletInstance.ReturnToPool at 0xAF1328 (lifetime expiry). The chord endpoints are cached as point1[+0x198]/point2[+0x1A4]. This batched pass is a broad-phase over the whole fixed step; it is NOT where the hit is resolved.
findings.members: BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick, BulletInstance.point1 (+0x198), BulletInstance.point2 (+0x1A4), BulletInstance.bulletLifeTime
findings.modding: The Jobs batch really does bypass Physics.Raycast hooks for this pass — but only for this pass. See step 15.

findings.title: STEP 15 — BulletInstance.Travel is the real integrator and it DOES call UnityEngine.Physics.Raycast directly, contradicting the 'no Physics.Raycast' assumption
findings.detail: Travel(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, bool skipRaycast) (0xAF5DF0) calls, in order: Object.op_Inequality, Component.get_transform, Transform.get_position, BulletInstance.get_forward, Vector3.Normalize, **UnityEngine.Physics.Raycast at 0xAF6206**, RaycastHit.get_point, BulletInstance.ProcessExplosive (0xAF625E), BulletInstance.ProcessBullet (0xAF626A), BulletCrack.ProcessCrackForAll (0xAF62F5), BulletInstance.ReturnToPool (0xAF6365). So the architecture is: batched RaycastCommand as a coarse chord test, then a conventional per-substep Physics.Raycast inside Travel (predictionStepsPerFrame = 6 on the generic round) that actually finds the hit. This corrects Phase-1 weapons-ballistics#0.
findings.members: BulletInstance.Travel, UnityEngine.Physics.Raycast, BulletInstance.ProcessBullet, BulletInstance.ProcessExplosive, BulletCrack.ProcessCrackForAll, BulletInstance.predictionStepsPerFrame
findings.modding: A Physics.Raycast transpiler/hook WILL see individual bullet rays. Still, the clean seam is BulletInstance.ProcessBullet — it is called from exactly one place (Travel) and receives the resolved hit in the instance field `hit` (+0x16C).

findings.title: STEP 16 — supersonic crack is emitted from Travel every substep, independently of any hit
findings.detail: BulletCrack.ProcessCrackForAll(Vector3 point1, Vector3 point2, float speed, Vector3 shooterPosition, BulletInstance bullet) is called at 0xAF62F5 inside Travel, after ProcessBullet. It intersects this substep's swept chord against the local listener, so cracks are geometric, not event-based. Ricochet audio is separate and lives in BulletInstance.Richochet (step 20) via BulletCrack.CanPlayRicochetSound / PlayRichochetsound.
findings.members: BulletCrack.ProcessCrackForAll, BulletCrack.SpeedOfSound, BulletCrack.CanPlayRicochetSound, BulletCrack.PlayRichochetsound, BulletCrack.MaxRicochetSoundsPerFrame
findings.modding: Crack runs on every peer's copy of the bullet regardless of isOwner, which is correct — that is how you hear other people's rounds go past.

findings.title: STEP 17 — BulletInstance.ProcessBullet dispatch order: VehicleHealth, BreakableSurface, BulletHittable (virtual), shooting-range scoring — all BEFORE any authority check
findings.detail: ProcessBullet (0xAF2100, 0x1410 bytes) begins with hit.collider / hit.transform, then transform.root.TryGetComponent -> VehicleHealth.CMD_TakeDamage (0xAF235E); TryGetComponent -> **BulletHittable.OnHit dispatched virtually** at 0xAF23F9 (`mov r10,[vtable+0x178]; call r10`, args rcx=component, rdx=this BulletInstance, r8=&_cachedRay[+0x13C], r9=&hit[+0x16C]) — this proves OnHit is virtual and that the four shipped overrides (OnBulletHitDamageable, OnBulletHitAddForce, OnBulletHitRangeTarget, **ShootableDoorPart**) are real dispatch targets; TryGetComponent into breakableSurface[+0x1B8] -> GK.BreakableSurface.Break(point, damage) (0xAF2472); CompareTag x2 -> RangeComputer.AddTargetHit (0xAF255F) / RangeComputer.AddCivilianHit (0xAF25BB). Phase-1 weapons-ballistics#18 called RangeComputer 'zero ballistics' — it is wired straight into the bullet hit path.
findings.members: BulletInstance.ProcessBullet, BulletHittable.OnHit (virtual, vtable slot +0x178), Il2Cpp.ShootableDoorPart.OnHit, VehicleHealth.CMD_TakeDamage, Il2CppGK.BreakableSurface.Break, RangeComputer.AddTargetHit, RangeComputer.AddCivilianHit
findings.modding: Confirms BulletHittable is a real virtual extension point — deriving from it and overriding OnHit works. Note all of this runs on EVERY peer (no isOwner gate yet), so VehicleHealth.CMD_TakeDamage and BreakableSurface.Break are invoked N times for N clients.

findings.title: STEP 18 — the armour plate is resolved next, and GetPenChance is fed the PLATE's durability fraction, not the victim's health
findings.detail: At 0xAF25D1 `hitCollider.TryGetComponent(out this._armour[+0x1C8])`. If found: `this._bluntDamageMultiplier[+0x134] = armour.bluntDamageMultplier[+0x34]`; `this.armorDamage[+0x80] *= armour.armourDamageMultplier[+0x38]`; `durFrac = maxDurability[+0x2C] > 0 ? durability[+0x30] / maxDurability : 0`; `ratingFactor = this._ratingFactors[armour.armourRating[+0x28]]` (dictionary lookup at 0xAF2691). Then at 0xAF2696 `if (ratingFactor > this.armourPenetration[+0x84])` -> roll: `if (Random.value > this.GetPenChance(durFrac)) this.armourPenetration = 0` (round STOPPED). Else (plate rating <= armourPenetration) the round defeats the plate outright and only `bulletDefect[+0x1D0] *= 0.5f`. Finally `armour.durability = max(0, durability - this.armorDamage)` at 0xAF26EE-0xAF2702. **GetPenChance(float healthFrac) receives durability/maxDurability** — this corrects Phase-1 weapons-ballistics#5, which read it as the target's remaining health.
findings.members: BulletInstance.GetPenChance, BulletInstance._armour (+0x1C8), BulletInstance._ratingFactors, BulletInstance.armourPenetration (+0x84), BulletInstance.armorDamage (+0x80), Armour.armourRating (+0x28), Armour.maxDurability (+0x2C), Armour.durability (+0x30), Armour.bluntDamageMultplier (+0x34), Armour.armourDamageMultplier (+0x38)
findings.modding: Worn plates are probabilistically weaker only in the contested band (ratingFactor > armourPenetration). A round whose armourPenetration >= the plate's rating factor is never rolled and always defeats it. _ratingFactors is per-BulletInstance so a postfix on Bullet.SpawnBullet can rewrite the whole caliber-vs-NIJ matrix per round.

findings.title: STEP 19 — a stopped round converts to blunt trauma using the ARMOUR's multiplier, and simultaneously loses its bleed and fragmentation
findings.detail: At 0xAF29B9/0xAF29E2 the code tests `armourPenetration == 0` (the flag zeroed in step 18) and if so: `this.damage[+0x60] = round((float)damage * this._bluntDamageMultiplier[+0x134])` at 0xAF29F1-0xAF2A0F. Note the multiplier used is the one copied off the Armour component, NOT Bullet.bluntDamageMultiplier (+0x78) — the bullet's own field is never read anywhere in ProcessBullet. Two further consequences of armourPenetration==0, both proven: at 0xAF3010-0xAF301F `fragDamage[+0x100] = 0`, and at 0xAF31DF-0xAF31EE the entire bleed block is skipped (`comiss armourPenetration, 0; jbe skip`). So a plate that stops a round removes bleeding entirely and leaves only scaled blunt damage.
findings.members: BulletInstance.damage (+0x60), BulletInstance._bluntDamageMultiplier (+0x134), BulletInstance.bluntDamageMultiplier (+0x78, unused), BulletInstance.fragDamage (+0x100), Armour.bluntDamageMultplier
findings.modding: Bullet.bluntDamageMultiplier (0.2 on the generic round) appears to be dead data — blunt is entirely an armour property. Verify at runtime before shipping a mod that tunes it.

findings.title: STEP 20 — surface lookup then ricochet: Surface.GetBulletImpactSurfaceInformation is called virtually off hit.textureCoord
findings.detail: At 0xAF2936 `RaycastHit.get_textureCoord`, then 0xAF2962 `mov rax,[vtable+0x198]; call rax` with rcx=Surface and rdx=the packed Vector2 — that is Il2Cpp.Surface.GetBulletImpactSurfaceInformation(Vector2 texCoord) resolved per-UV, returning a SurfaceInformation. That SurfaceInformation is then passed to BulletInstance.Richochet(SurfaceInformation) at 0xAF29A7. Richochet (0xAF44D0) uses hit.normal, Random.Range, Random.insideUnitSphere, Quaternion.LookRotation, then BulletCrack.CanPlayRicochetSound / BulletCrack.PlayRichochetsound. Ricochet is bounded by maxRicochets (3) / minRicochetAngle (45) / _ricochetCount (+0xF8).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.Surface.GetBulletImpactSurfaceInformation (virtual, vtable slot +0x198), BulletInstance.Richochet, SurfaceInformation.ricochetMultiplier, SurfaceInformation.ricochetDeflection, BulletInstance.maxRicochets, BulletInstance.minRicochetAngle
findings.modding: Per-UV surface resolution means a single mesh can have different ballistic materials per submesh/texture region — adding a Surface component with OverrideBulletImpact is enough to make any geometry behave differently, no code.

findings.title: STEP 21 — penetration: Collider.Raycast finds the exit point, then penetrationAmount and speed decay and the direction is randomly deflected
findings.detail: Inside ProcessBullet: 0xAF2B97/0xAF2C9E read penetrationAmount[+0x88]; 0xAF2CAF calls UnityEngine.Collider.Raycast (the back-face probe that produces penetrationPoint[+0x114]/hasPenetrationPoint[+0x120] and _cachedPenRay[+0x154]); 0xAF2DB2-0xAF2DD0 writes the decremented penetrationAmount; 0xAF2DE1-0xAF2DEA writes the reduced speed[+0x50] (SurfaceInformation.speedReduction); 0xAF2E39-0xAF2EB0 does Random.Range + Random.onUnitSphere + Quaternion.AngleAxis + Vector3.normalized + Quaternion.op_Multiply — the post-penetration deflection cone (SurfaceInformation.penetrationDeflection). BulletManager.ReleaseTracer is called at 0xAF2F09 when the round is retiring, and BulletInstance.SpawnImpactNewSystem is invoked at four distinct sites (entry impact, exit impact, flesh impact, retire impact).

findings.title: STEP 22 — BulletInstance.SpawnImpactNewSystem does frustum culling, per-frame budgeting, decal, VFX and SFX
findings.detail: SpawnImpactNewSystem(SurfaceInformation, RaycastHit, bool isPen) (0xAF4A00) calls hit.point, Camera.get_main, Camera.WorldToViewportPoint (the IsPointInFrustum cull, inlined), Time.get_frameCount (the per-frame budget counter), Random.Range, hit.normal, Quaternion.AngleAxis, SurfaceInformation.GetRandomImpactDecal, Quaternion.LookRotation, hit.transform, ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled, SurfaceInformation.GetRandomImpactEffect, SurfaceInformation.GetRandomImpactSound, BulletEffectManager.SpawnImpactSFX. The budget gate is BulletEffectManager.CanSpawnImpactVFX / MaxImpactVFXPerFrame / _impactVFXThisFrame / _lastResetFrame, and pool sizes come from PoolInitializer's divided global budget.

findings.modding: Impact FX are the one part of the pipeline that runs on every peer with no ownership gate, so they are the cheapest place to add visual mods — and the first thing to without warning disappear under high RPM.

findings.title: STEP 23 — THE AUTHORITY GATE: at 0xAF2F4F ProcessBullet tests BulletInstance.isOwner and returns if false; only the shooter's client ever originates damage
findings.detail: `cmp byte ptr [rdi+0xC0], r13b; je <end>` at 0xAF2F4F is the single instruction that makes damage client-authoritative. Everything before it (vehicle damage, breakables, BulletHittable, range scoring, armour wear, ricochet, penetration, impact FX) runs on every peer; everything after it (Health resolution, bleed, fracture, damage, gore) runs only where isOwner is true — i.e. on the machine of the player who pulled the trigger. Immediately after the gate: `hit.collider.transform.root.TryGetComponent(out Health h)`; if not found, return; then `if (h == this.shootersGameObject[+0xD8]) return` (0xAF2FC3-0xAF2FD3) — you cannot shoot yourself.
findings.members: BulletInstance.isOwner (+0xC0), BulletInstance.shootersGameObject (+0xD8), Il2Cpp.Health
findings.modding: Definitive answer to 'who is authoritative': the shooter. The host is a relay for damage exactly as it is for movement. A host-side anti-cheat cannot use ProcessBullet at all (it never runs there for other players' shots) — it has to sit on Health.UserCode_CMDTakeDamage.

findings.title: STEP 24 — fragmentation adds a separate damage term, rolled here and zeroed by armour
findings.detail: At 0xAF2FD9-0xAF3008: `if (this.fragmentationChance[+0x6C] > Random.value) this.fragDamage[+0x100] = Random.Range(0, this.maxFragmentationMultiplier[+0x70]) * (float)this.damage[+0x60]; else fragDamage = 0;` then `if (armourPenetration == 0) fragDamage = 0`. On the shipped GenericBullet fragmentationChance=0.05 and maxFragmentationMultiplier=0, so Random.Range(0,0) returns 0 and the frag term is always zero — the system is authored off, exactly as Phase-1 weapons-ballistics#22 suspected, and now proven to be a multiplier-of-zero rather than a disabled branch.
findings.members: BulletInstance.fragmentationChance (+0x6C), BulletInstance.maxFragmentationMultiplier (+0x70), BulletInstance.fragDamage (+0x100)
findings.modding: Set maxFragmentationMultiplier on a Bullet prefab and fragmentation immediately becomes live with no code change; it adds Random.Range(0,mult)*damage on top of base damage.

findings.title: STEP 25a (player targets) — Health.GetBodyPartFromTag(collider.tag) selects the limb; bleed and fracture go out as their own Commands before the damage Command
findings.detail: If the hit collider (or its parent, or _armour.indicReference at [+0x1C8]+0x20) has NO RagdollAnimator2BoneIndicator, this is a player. Code: `part = Health.GetBodyPartFromTag(hitCollider.tag)` at 0xAF31DA. Then, gated on armourPenetration > 0: `if (Random.Range(0,100) < HeavyBleedChance[+0x44]) bleedRate = 10.0f` (literal constant read from .rdata) `else if (Random.Range(0,100) < bleedChance[+0x40]) bleedRate = round(bleedDamage[+0x48])`, then `health.CMD_Bleed(part, bleedRate, shootersNetworkID)` at 0xAF3268. Then `if (Random.Range(0,100) < FractureChance[+0x3C]) health.CMD_Fracture(part, shootersNetworkID)` at 0xAF329F. On the generic round that is a 10% chance of a fixed 10/s heavy bleed, otherwise a 13% chance of a 3/s light bleed, and a 15% fracture chance rolled for ANY body part (Health only stores Fractured_ SyncVars for the four limbs).

findings.modding: Player hitboxes are resolved purely by collider TAG — adding a hitbox needs no code, just a tagged collider under the root that has the Health. The heavy-bleed rate of 10 is a hardcoded immediate in ProcessBullet, not a field, so it can only be changed by patching that method.

findings.title: STEP 25b (player targets) — the damage number: total = damage + round(fragDamage), and LArm/RArm REPLACE the base with damage * armDamageMultipiler
findings.detail: At 0xAF32A4-0xAF32E8: `total = damage[+0x60] + round(fragDamage[+0x100])`. Then `lea ecx,[bodyPart-3]; cmp cl,1; ja skip` — i.e. if bodyPart is 3 or 4 (LArm, RArm) it recomputes `total = round((float)damage * armDamageMultipiler[+0x68]) + round(fragDamage)`. With armDamageMultipiler = 1.8 on the generic round, arm hits do MORE damage than torso hits, not less. Then `if (total > 0) health.CMDTakeDamage((float)total, bodyPart, HealthBodyPart.NONE, shootersNetworkID)` at 0xAF331D — the crossedDamage argument is the literal 8 (`mov r9b, 8` = HealthBodyPart.NONE) on this path, so a single-limb hit never sets it.

findings.modding: Bullet.damage is an int and the only per-round damage number in the game (GunStats has none). Because the arm branch replaces rather than scales the total, an armDamageMultipiler below 1 makes arms tankier and above 1 makes them the best place to shoot — 1.8 shipped.

findings.title: STEP 25c (AI targets) — RagdollAnimator2BoneIndicator + Health.GetHitboxIndex(bone.name) routes to Health.ProcessAIDamage instead

Note the AI path passes bleed as PARAMETERS rather than issuing CMD_Bleed itself, does NOT apply armDamageMultipiler here, and is not gated on armourPenetration.

findings.modding: Confirms Phase-1 weapons-ballistics#8: a damage mod that only patches CMDTakeDamage misses the AI's damage SHAPING but not the application, because ProcessAIDamage itself calls CMDTakeDamage (step 26). Patch ProcessAIDamage to change bot lethality, CMDTakeDamage to change everything.

findings.title: STEP 26 — Health.ProcessAIDamage funnels back into the same Command, and is the ONLY caller of Gore.CheckForGore
findings.detail: ProcessAIDamage (0xF10BA0) calls, in order: Random.Range, **Health.CMDTakeDamage (0xF10C6F)**, Health.CMD_Bleed (0xF10DA7), hit.point -> **Gore.CheckForGore (0xF10E35)**, hit.normal, then NetworkWriterPool.Get + WriteVarInt + WriteVector3 + SendCommandInternal = Health.CMDProcessAIAnimation(hitboxIndex, direction). The xref index says Gore.CheckForGore has exactly one caller in the entire binary: Health.ProcessAIDamage. **Players never gore.** Gore.CheckForGore (0xEFB0B0) then does the nearest-gorePoint scan and branches on Mirror isServer: server calls SpawnGore(index) locally plus RPC_SpawnGore(index) (includeOwner=1), client calls CMD_SpawnGore(index) (requiresAuthority=FALSE); finally GoreHead.RandomiseBlendShapes.

Gore.SpawnGore does sharedMaterials swap + ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled + SkinnedMeshRenderer.set_rootBone/set_bones re-binding, so a custom gore head only needs matching bones.

findings.title: STEP 27 — through-and-through: after the flesh impact, damage decays as damage * incidenceAngle / 270 and destroyObject is latched
findings.detail: At 0xAF347D-0xAF349C: `this.damage[+0x60] = round((float)damage * incidenceAngle[+0x1B0] / 270.0f)` — the divisor 270 is a literal float in .rdata. That is the residual damage carried into the next body part or surface the same round hits, which is what feeds the `crossedDamage` second-body-part mechanic. At 0xAF34E9 `this.destroyObject[+0x130] = 1` latches retirement, and Travel then calls ReturnToPool. Impact counting uses currentImpactPenetrationCount[+0xF0] / currentImpactNonPenetrationCount[+0xEC] against maxImpactPenetration[+0xE8] / maxImpactNonPenetration[+0xE4].

findings.modding: Damage decay is angle-driven, not distance-driven: a shallow-angle hit that grazes loses almost everything, a perpendicular pass-through keeps a lot. Nothing in the pipeline reduces damage with range — Bullet.damage is range-independent by design.

findings.title: STEP 28 — Health.CMDTakeDamage is [Command(requiresAuthority = false)] — any client can damage any Health
findings.detail: Health.CMDTakeDamage (0xF08740) writes WriteFloat(damage), two byte-enum writes (via Mirror.GeneratedNetworkCode._Write_Mirror.SceneOperation, which the weaver reuses for all byte enums), WriteVarInt(shooterID), then SendCommandInternal with the requiresAuthority byte at [rsp+0x28] set from a zeroed register = FALSE. Same for Health.CMD_Bleed and Health.CMD_Fracture (literal 0), Health.CMD_HitReaction, Health.CMD_StopRun, Health.CMDProcessAIAnimation and Gore.CMD_SpawnGore. By contrast WeaponV3.CMD_Fire and WeaponV3.CMD_SendBullet both pass literal 1 (authority required — the shooter owns its own weapon). This is architecturally necessary (the shooter does not own the victim's NetworkIdentity) and is simultaneously the game's largest trust hole.
findings.members: Health.CMDTakeDamage, Health.CMD_Bleed, Health.CMD_Fracture, Health.CMD_HitReaction, Gore.CMD_SpawnGore, Mirror.NetworkBehaviour.SendCommandInternal
findings.modding: Host-side damage scaling, friendly-fire rules and anti-cheat all belong on Health.UserCode_CMDTakeDamage__Single__HealthBodyPart__HealthBodyPart__Int32 — it is the one chokepoint every player hit and every AI hit passes through, and it is the only place the host has a say.

findings.title: STEP 29 — server: UserCode_CMDTakeDamage resolves the shooter by netId and forwards to the 5-arg Health.TakeDamage
findings.detail: UserCode_CMDTakeDamage__Single__HealthBodyPart__HealthBodyPart__Int32 (0xF14060) calls Mirror.Utils.GetSpawnedInServerOrClient (0xF140D9) on the shooterID — proving shooterID is a netId — then Object.op_Inequality, Component.TryGetComponent, Component.get_transform, Transform.get_position (to synthesise the damage-source position), then Health.TakeDamage(damage, bodyPart, crossedDamage, shooterID, position) at 0xF1422B. It performs no clamping, no range check against the shooter's position, and no team check. UserCode_CMDTakeDamageFromPosition (0xF14010) is a two-instruction shim to the same 5-arg method.

findings.modding: The friendly-fire SyncVar GameManagerNetwork.FriendlyFire is NOT consulted here — if it is enforced at all it must be inside the 5-arg TakeDamage or further down. Worth a runtime probe.

findings.title: STEP 30 — server-side Health.TakeDamage(5-arg): cross-limb bleed-through, AI wake-up, suicide-bomber cook-off, then the ClientRpc
findings.detail: Health.TakeDamage (0xF137A0, the 5-arg local method) calls: Object.op_Inequality, **Health.ProcessCrossDamage (0xF13945)** which recursively re-enters TakeDamage for the second limb using ArmsDamageCross/StomachDamageCross/LegsDamageCross; Mirror.Utils.GetSpawnedInServerOrClient + TryGetComponent (shooter lookup); **GameManager.RequestPriorityBrainUpdate (0xF13B80)** — being shot promotes the victim bot to a priority AI tick; **BrainAI.SERVER_BomberExplode (0xF13BB8)** — the suicide-vest cook-off from Phase-1 ai-brain#26 is triggered right here on taking damage; and finally Health.TakeDamage (the 4-arg weaved form) at 0xF13C0C.

findings.modding: This is the correct place for a host-authoritative damage mod that still wants the cross-limb and AI-reaction behaviour to run. Patching the 4-arg RPC instead skips ProcessCrossDamage entirely.

findings.title: STEP 31 — Health.TakeDamage(4-arg) is a ClientRpc (includeOwner=true); its UserCode runs everywhere but the HP arithmetic is fenced behind isServer
findings.detail: Health.TakeDamage 4-arg (0xF135E0) is the RPC sender: WriteFloat + two byte-enum writes + WriteVarInt + SendRPCInternal(hash 0x89A82AF1, channelId=0, includeOwner=1). Its body UserCode_TakeDamage (0xF170D0) runs on every client and does, unconditionally: Mirror.Utils.GetSpawnedInServerOrClient (shooter), SteamLobby.UnlockAchivement, **Kinemation RecoilAnimation.Play** (the hit flinch), **MedicalSystem.ProcessDamage(damage)** (pain/heart-rate, purely local per Phase-1 player-avatar#9), and an isOwned-guarded timer reset. Then at 0xF1755A: `if (!NetworkBehaviour.isServer) goto epilogue` — everything below is host-only.

findings.modding: Hit feedback (flinch, pain, achievements) is client-side and free to mod without desync. HP itself is host-only, so a client-side HP patch changes nothing that replicates.

findings.title: STEP 32 — server-only HP math: a jump table on HealthBodyPart, per-limb subtraction, clamp at zero, and TotalHP recomputed as the SUM of the seven limbs
findings.detail: Behind the isServer fence, `switch(bodyPart)` (jump table at 0xF17583, bounds-checked against 7). Each arm of the table does `set_NetworkXHP(XHP - damage)` then `if (XHP < 0) set_NetworkXHP(0)`. Health field offsets read directly: TotalHP@0x80, HeadHP@0x88, ChestHP@0x8C, StomachHP@0x90, LArmHP@0x94, RArmHP@0x98, LLegHP@0x9C, RLegHP@0xA0. After the switch, at 0xF1779B-0xF177D9: `set_NetworkTotalHP(RArmHP + LArmHP + LLegHP + RLegHP + StomachHP + ChestHP + HeadHP)` — TotalHP is a derived sum, not an independent pool. The Chest arm additionally calls Health.TakeRagdollDamage when a corpse-state flag (field@0x238) is set, and the RLeg arm calls Health.CMD_StopRun when the leg reaches zero.

findings.modding: initTotalHP is therefore cosmetic — TotalHP is overwritten every hit with the limb sum. To change effective total health you must change the seven initXHP values. Field offsets above are build-specific; re-derive them if the game updates.

findings.title: STEP 33 — death conditions: HeadHP <= 1.0, ChestHP <= 0, or TotalHP <= 0. Stomach and the four limbs can never kill directly
findings.detail: Proven from the jump-table arms. Head: `comiss xmm8(=1.0f literal), HeadHP; jb skip` -> death when HeadHP <= 1.0 (not 0 — a deliberate one-point margin). Chest: `comiss xmm6(=0), ChestHP; jb skip` -> death when ChestHP <= 0. Stomach, LArm, RArm, LLeg, RLeg all `jmp` straight to the TotalHP recompute with no Die call. Then at 0xF177DE: `if (TotalHP <= 0 && shooterID != -3) Die(HealthBodyPart.Chest, -3)`. Cause-of-death selection: if crossedDamage != NONE the recorded cause is the CROSSED part (`movzx edx, crossedDamage; jmp Die`), else the hit part, else literal 7 (HealthBodyPart.SERVER) on one branch. **shooterID == -3 is a reserved sentinel meaning 'no attributable shooter'** and it suppresses the duplicate Die.
findings.members: Health.Die(HealthBodyPart,int), Health.MyCauseOfDeath, Health.MyKiller, Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart.SERVER (=7), Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart.NONE (=8)
findings.modding: A headshot kill is HeadHP<=1, so a 'survive one headshot' mod is a one-field change (initHeadHP) rather than a code patch. The -3 sentinel is what distinguishes bleed-out and environmental death from gunfire in the kill feed.

findings.title: STEP 34 — bleeding is a server tick inside Health.CallUpdate that re-enters TakeDamage with shooterID = -3
findings.detail: Health has no Update; GameManager.Update drives Health.CallUpdate (0xF09210, xref-confirmed as the only caller). CallUpdate opens with `if (isServer) Health.ProcessDeathServer()` (0xF092A6), then isOwned-guarded local work (InputLayer.GetKey for the voice/emote keys, agony SFX via NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer.PlayRandom, animator floats), then the bleed tick: at 0xF09CC6-0xF09D05 it calls the 5-arg `Health.TakeDamage(bleedRate, part, HealthBodyPart.NONE(r9b=8), -3 (0xFFFFFFFD), Vector3)` once per bleeding limb, reading NetworkBleedingDamage_* and writing them back (set_NetworkBleedingDamage_Stomach visible at 0xF0A0A6). It also does the ragdoll bleedout: set_NetworkRagdollHealth (0xF09AF2) and SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth (0xF09B48).

findings.modding: Confirms Phase-1 player-avatar#16 (patch CallUpdate, not Update) and adds the reason: it is also the bleed and ragdoll-bleedout clock, and it is where ProcessDeathServer is polled from rather than being called by Die.

findings.title: STEP 35 — Health.Die is a ClientRpc; UserCode_Die runs the whole death sequence on every client
findings.detail: Health.Die (0xF0AC50) writes the byte enum + VarInt shooterID and calls SendRPCInternal(hash 0x39D121ED, channelId=0, includeOwner=1). UserCode_Die__HealthBodyPart__Int32 (0xF14980, 0x2490 bytes — the largest method in this pipeline) does, in order: a delayed action via ThreadStart + DelayExt.PlayAfterSeconds; Mirror SyncVarEqual/SetSyncVar (isDead); RaidManager.UpdateAICount; WaveSurvival.OnEnemyDeath; GetSpawnedInServerOrClient (killer lookup); FindObjectsByType + WeaponModding.StopModding; scene-name check; BrainAI.OnKill; Collider.set_enabled(false); **Health.PerformRagdollAction (0xF153A7)**; Health.RemoveTargetsOnDeathOrDestroy; SaveManager.SaveSteamStorage/LoadSteamStorage; SteamLobby.UnlockAchivement; NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer.PlayRandom (death voice line); MainCameraSingleton.PlayDeathSfxEffect; audio fade and Behaviour.set_enabled(false) over scriptsDisableOnDeath; GameObject.SetActive over deactivateOnDeath/activateOnDeath; transform reparent/localPosition/localEulerAngles/localScale (corpse detach); set_NetworkTotalHP; weapon disposal via WeaponsAI.CMD_DropWeapon / WeaponV3.CMD_DropWeapon / WeaponV3.CMD_DieWithWeapon; GetComponentsInChildren + Collider.set_isTrigger + Rigidbody.set_isKinematic(false) + linearVelocity carry-over onto the ragdoll bodies; AddComponent + CharacterRagdollDisable.CallCoroutine; Object.Destroy.

findings.title: STEP 37 — the corpse remains a damageable, separately-networked entity that bleeds out on a server timer
findings.detail: After death the body keeps NetworkRagdollHealth (SyncVar). Health.TakeRagdollDamage (0xF13C20) calls set_NetworkRagdollHealth then Random.Range; it is invoked from UserCode_TakeDamage's Chest arm when the corpse flag (field@0x238) is set. Health.SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth (0xF12360) is itself weaved — it calls SendRPCInternal, so despite the SERVER_ prefix it is a ClientRpc sender, distinct from Health.RPC_RagdollBleedout (0xF11B80). It is ticked from Health.CallUpdate against ragdollBleedoutTime/ragdollBleedoutTimer, and Health.activeRagdollSync / fullHealthSync (Smooth.SmoothSyncMirror arrays) swap which transform-sync set is live for the corpse.

findings.detail: Health.ProcessDeathServer (0xF11480), reached only via `if (isServer)` at the top of Health.CallUpdate: Object.op_Inequality, **PlayerMaster.AddBotKill (0xF1152F)**, PlayerMaster.AddSurvivalPoints, playerBoardItem.set_NetworkKilledHVT, OperationsManager.set_NetworkHVTdead, **PlayerMaster.AddDeath (0xF116A7)**, **PlayerMaster.AddKill(PlayerMaster killed) (0xF11703)**, OperationsManager.AddKill, and finally **Mirror.NetworkServer.Destroy(gameObject) (0xF1176D)**. So the scoreboard update, HVT bookkeeping and the network despawn of the corpse all sit behind one server gate, decoupled from the Die RPC by one or more frames.

findings.title: STEP 39 — cleanup: BulletInstance.ReturnToPool releases the tracer and hands the instance back; EndBullet and ForceRetire are the same folded function
findings.detail: BulletInstance.ReturnToPool (0xAF4340) calls BulletManager.ReleaseTracer (0xAF43C3) and (inlined) BulletManager.Unregister/ReturnInstance; BulletManager.ReturnInstance (0xAF7BE0) also calls ReleaseTracer. It is invoked from three places: BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick (lifetime expiry), BulletInstance.Travel (destroyObject latch / out of range), and BulletManager.FixedUpdate (error path). BulletInstance.EndBullet and BulletInstance.ForceRetire share RVA 0xAF1D60 — identical bodies, folded by the linker; neither has any direct caller. Corpse cleanup is the parallel path: CharacterRagdollDisable.CallCoroutine plus UnityEngine.Object.Destroy in UserCode_Die, and Mirror.NetworkServer.Destroy in ProcessDeathServer.

findings.title: SUMMARY — authority ledger for one shot, in one place
findings.detail: OWNER (shooter's client) decides: trigger timing, CanFire, misfire roll, MOA spread vector, muzzle position and rotation, projectile simulation, all raycasts, surface/armour resolution, penetration, ricochet, WHICH Health was hit and WHICH body part, bleed/fracture/gore rolls, and the final damage number. SERVER decides: nothing about the shot itself — it rebroadcasts CMD_SendBullet verbatim (identical function body), and for damage it only writes the per-limb HP SyncVars, evaluates the death thresholds, runs ProcessCrossDamage, picks the death animation, and does kill attribution in ProcessDeathServer. ALL CLIENTS run: the projectile sim for visuals, crack, impact VFX/decals/SFX, BulletHittable.OnHit, BreakableSurface.Break, VehicleHealth.CMD_TakeDamage, hit flinch, MedicalSystem pain, ragdoll, gore, death sequence. The two gates that hold the whole model together are one byte (BulletInstance.isOwner at +0xC0, tested at ProcessBullet+0xE4F) and one branch (isServer at UserCode_TakeDamage 0xF1755A). requiresAuthority is FALSE on every Health Command.
findings.members: BulletInstance.isOwner, BulletInstance.ProcessBullet, Health.CMDTakeDamage, Health.UserCode_CMDTakeDamage, Health.TakeDamage(5-arg), Health.UserCode_TakeDamage, Health.Die, Health.ProcessDeathServer, WeaponV3.UserCode_CMD_SendBullet
findings.modding: Three mod archetypes and where each belongs. (1) Feel/visuals/audio: client-side, anywhere between BulletInstance.Travel and SpawnImpactNewSystem, no netcode. (2) Balance that must replicate: host-side on Health.UserCode_CMDTakeDamage (covers players AND bots, cannot be spoofed). (3) Ballistics behaviour: BulletInstance.ProcessBullet on the shooter, or Bullet prefab data for anything authorable. Anti-cheat has exactly two viable seams: UserCode_CMD_SendBullet (re-derive spread, validate muzzle pose against the sender) and UserCode_CMDTakeDamage (validate that a plausible round could have reached that limb).
